About

## Fulton Road and the West Side Bar Tradition

Cleveland's West Side has long maintained a bar culture that runs parallel to, and largely indifferent to, whatever is happening in the Flats or along East Fourth Street. The neighbourhood tavern model here is not a revival or a design concept; it is simply what survived. Johnny's Bar on Fulton, at 3164 Fulton Rd in the Old Brooklyn area, operates within that tradition. The address places it in a residential stretch where bars earn their regulars through consistency rather than programming, and where the room itself tends to communicate something before a single drink arrives.

Walking into a West Side neighbourhood bar of this type, the sensory register is immediate and legible: dim lighting calibrated to conversation rather than Instagram, a bar leading that has absorbed decades of evenings, and a crowd that already knows each other's orders. These are rooms built around familiarity, and Johnny's fits that description. The atmosphere is the product of time rather than design intent, which gives it a credibility that newer, concept-driven spaces on the East Side or in Ohio City spend considerable effort trying to manufacture.

## The Cocktail Programme in Context

Cleveland's cocktail scene has developed unevenly across the city's neighbourhoods. Downtown and Ohio City have attracted bars that invest in technical programmes, sourced spirits, and the kind of menu architecture you find at places like Acqua di Dea or [Blue Sky Brews](link_21). The West Side neighbourhood bar operates in a different register entirely. Here, the cocktail programme, such as it is, tends to prioritise approachability and value over technique. Classic builds, spirit-forward pours, and beer-and-shot combinations dominate. This is not a limitation so much as a different set of values about what a bar is for.

That distinction matters when placing Johnny's within the broader Cleveland drinking map. The bar does not position itself against the craft cocktail tier occupied by the Velvet Tango Room, which has been Cleveland's most recognised standard-bearer for serious cocktail craft since the early 2000s. Johnny's operates on a different axis: the neighbourhood institution that measures quality in reliability and in the kind of crowd that returns weekly rather than occasionally. Compared to the programmatic bars covered in [our full Cleveland restaurants guide](link_22), Johnny's represents the category that most visitors overlook and most locals depend on.

Nationally, the gap between programme-driven bars and neighbourhood taverns has widened as the craft cocktail movement matured. Operations like [Kumiko in Chicago](link_23), [Jewel of the South in New Orleans](link_24), and [Julep in Houston](link_25) have defined one end of the American bar spectrum, where technique, sourcing, and editorial intent drive every pour. [Bar Leather Apron in Honolulu](link_26), [ABV in San Francisco](link_27), and [Superbueno in New York City](link_28) each represent variations on that programme-led model, as does [The Parlour in Frankfurt](link_29) in the European context. Johnny's Bar on Fulton sits at the other end of that spectrum, where the value proposition is social continuity rather than craft distinction.

## Old Brooklyn as a Neighbourhood

Old Brooklyn is one of Cleveland's more stable residential neighbourhoods on the West Side, a stretch of modest housing stock, long-operating businesses, and a demographic mix that has shifted but retained working-class roots. The bar-to-resident ratio in Old Brooklyn reflects that history: these are establishments that serve the people who live within walking distance, not destination venues pulling from the metropolitan area. Johnny's on Fulton is embedded in that geography.

That neighbourhood context shapes the experience in practical ways. The crowd on a Friday evening will include people who have been coming for years, if not decades. New visitors will be immediately identifiable, which is not unwelcoming so much as accurate. Bars like this run on social memory, and the ideal way to engage with them is to understand you are entering someone else's regular spot rather than a public-facing hospitality venue designed to accommodate the uninitiated. The bar shares this character with venues like [Beachland Ballroom and Tavern](link_30) and [Brewnuts](link_31), each of which has a defined community relationship that precedes any editorial attention.

## Planning a Visit

That absence is itself informative: this is not a bar that markets itself or manages its public profile through digital channels. The address, 3164 Fulton Rd, is direct to reach by car from the West Side or from downtown via I-71 South. Street parking along Fulton is generally available in the residential blocks surrounding the bar.

Given the neighbourhood tavern format, there is no reservation system and no meaningful queue on standard evenings. The bar functions on a walk-in basis. Dress expectations are casual in keeping with the neighbourhood character.

# 10+ of the Best Cocktail Bars in Cleveland

*   Post author:[Amanda](link_16)
*   Post category:[Food/Drink](link_17)
*   Post last modified:May 23, 2025

Cleveland is arguably a beer city, with **[40+ craft breweries](link_18)** throughout the Great Cleveland area. The city does bars, breweries, and pubs very well – there’s literally something for everyone.

But what about spots for people who prefer cocktails to beer? Well, good news – Cleveland has plenty of cocktail bars, too!

Below is my list of the best dedicated cocktail bars in Cleveland, plus a few restaurants that also do notably great cocktails.

_**Note:**This list specifically focuses on cocktails and bars that primarily specialize in them. If you’re looking for mocktail options, **[I have another post for that](link_19)!**_

* * *

## Cleveland’s best cocktail bars

Here are the best cocktail bars in Cleveland, roughly listed in order of my favorites – though it admittedly does change from time to time, and you really can’t go wrong with any of these!

### Porco Lounge & Tiki Room

_2527 W 25th St, Cleveland_

![Image 3: Drinks at Porco Lounge & Tiki Room](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_9151-768x1024.jpg)

Tiki drinks at Porco

Located between the historic neighborhoods of Tremont and Ohio City in Cleveland, **Porco Lounge & Tiki Room** is a hidden oasis of a cocktail bar in a rather unassuming building along W 25th. The tiki vibes are strong here – and the drinks are even stronger! (Seriously, I think they make the strongest cocktails in the city.)

Porco will transport you to the South Pacific with its tiki decor and tropical cocktails, and it’s hands-down one of the best places to get a unique cocktail in Cleveland. Porco uses classic tiki cocktail recipes, made with fresh ingredients and house-made syrups.

Most of their cocktails are $18.

*   **What to order:**Tiki drinks, of course! My personal favorites are the Painkiller and Saturn, while my husband Elliot likes the Fog Cutter and Heart of Darkness. They also have a few shareable cocktails for groups, like the Scorpion Bowl. Find the **[full Porco menu](link_20)** here.
*   **Hours and reservations:**This spot is open Wednesday-Saturday evenings, and reservations are highly recommended. You can call, or **[reserve a table online](link_21)**.
*   **Good to know:**Porco also offers food from Pinoy Fine Foods! Highly recommended, as these drinks are super strong.

### Cloak & Dagger

_2399 W 11th St, Cleveland_

![Image 4: Cloak & Dagger](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_1530-768x1024.jpg)

Inside Cloak & Dagger

![Image 5: Drinks at Cloak & Dagger](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_1539-768x1024.jpg)

Cloak & Dagger drinks

**Cloak & Dagger** is giving dark academia with its low-lit bar and literary theme. This cocktail bar is located in Tremont, and is easily one of the best in Cleveland in terms of both drinks and overall vibe.

Cloak & Dagger is also unique in that they release a new “book” (i.e. a new menu) each season with brand new drinks. Meaning you can visit this cocktail bar over and over and always find something new to try.

All cocktails here are $16.

*   **What to order:**The menu is always changing! But they always have a “Legends” section of their more popular and classic drinks. The Dagger Dagger and Rabbit’s Foot are favorites of ours. They can also make several of their cocktails non-alcoholic. See the current **[Cloak & Dagger menu](link_22)** on their website.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Cloak & Dagger is open Tuesday-Sunday nights, and reservations are needed. You can **[make them online](link_23)** through OpenTable.
*   **Good to know:**They also have a small menu of all-vegan bar snacks.

### Amazonia

_1640 Hopkins Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 6: Drink at Amazonia bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Amazonia-1-450x600.jpg)

Such a pretty drink!

![Image 7: Inside Amazonia bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Amazonia-2-450x600.jpg)

Inside Amazonia

Listed on Google Maps as a pizza spot, **Amazonia** is also home to an incredible little speakeasy-style bar inside a converted house in Lakewood. The indoor bar space is dark and filled with antiques, trinkets, and the feeling of stepping into the attic collection of an old explorer.

The drinks here are inventive and delicious. Classic cocktails cost $13-$14, while themed specialty cocktails cost $16-$18.

*   **What to order:**The drink menu has changed since I visited, but definitely take a look at their specialty cocktail menu, which is always themed and thoughtful! See the **[full Amazonia menu](link_24)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Amazonia is open Tuesday-Sunday nights, and they don’t take reservations unless you have a large group.
*   **Good to know:** Amazonia has a great pizza menu, too, along with some small plates and a blackberry gelato that you really should try. It’s also connected to the patio at Hola Tacos.

### Society Lounge

_2063 E 4th St, Cleveland_

**Society Lounge** is a speakeasy-style bar downtown that is designed to take you back in time to the swanky social scene of decades past. Walk down the steps from E. 4th street into the newly-renovated elegant space, and enjoy specialty hand-crafted cocktails using fresh ingredients and homemade syrups.

Specialty drinks here are all $18.

*   **What to order:**My go-to is either the Burnin’ the Benjamins or Giggle Juice, while Elliot is all about the Legend of Bagger Vance. They also have mocktails See the **[full Society Lounge menu](link_25)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Society Lounge is open Tuesday-Saturday nights, and they do technically take reservations, though it’s through their “**[private events](link_26)**” page.
*   **Good to know:** Society Lounge is also known for transforming into the festive Miracle Pop-Up Bar during the Christmas season, which is one of the**[best holiday pop-up bars in Cleveland](link_27)**.

### Flower on Freeman

_2102 Freeman Ave, Cleveland_

![Image 8: Flower on Freeman bar interior](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Flower-on-Freeman-1-800x600.jpg)

Inside Flower on Freeman

![Image 9: Flower on Freeman charcuterie board](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Flower-on-Freeman-3-450x600.jpg)

Drinks and Gold Board for 2

Brand new in 2025, **Flower on Freeman** easily made it onto this list after just one visit. The bright bar in Duck Island (not far from West Side Market in Ohio City) feels both fancy and whimsical, with a colorful interior and a nice little patio space.

Drinks here average around $17, with a few more expensive ones. Mocktails are $7-$11.

*   **What to order:**The hand-crafted drinks here are beautiful and unique; I really liked the Pocket Full of Posey, while Elliot enjoyed the Smoked Blossom. They also have some unique mocktails on the menu. See the **[full Flower on Freeman menu](link_28)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**They’re open Monday-Saturday nights, and currently are not taking reservations, but that could change.
*   **Good to know:**Flower on Freeman also serves some small plates, and the Gold Board (for either 2 or 4 guests) might be the most beautiful cheese + charcuterie board I’ve ever been served.

### Velvet Tango Room

_2095 Columbus Rd, Cleveland_

![Image 10: Velvet Tango Room bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7265-768x1024.jpg)

Velvet Tango Room front bar

![Image 11: Drinks at Velvet Tango Room](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7261-768x1024.jpg)

Drinks at VTR

Just around the corner from Flower on Freeman, **Velvet Tango Room** is one of Cleveland’s longest-standing craft cocktail bars, having opened in 1996. More than 25 years later, this cozy and intimate cocktail bar is still one of the best places to grab a drink in Cleveland.

Inside, you’ll find a wood-paneled bar and an absolutely massive cocktail list. All drinks here are $20 (except during Happy Hour Monday-Friday), and are made to order.

*   **What to order:**There are so many cocktails to choose from. Under each type of alcohol on the menu you’ll find “Classics,” “Contemporary Classics,” and then “VTR Originals,” which you’ll only find at this bar. Last time I went I had an India Lime Fizz (a VTR gin original), and it was so good. Find the **[full Velvet Tango Room menu](link_29)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Velvet Tango Room is open 7 days a week, including late afternoons on Sundays. They do take reservations, and you can **[make them online](link_30)** through OpenTable.
*   **Good to know:**Their dress code is “business casual.” You can often catch live jazz music here, and they also opened a back patio last year, which is open weather-permitting.

### Vault

_2017 E 9th St, Cleveland_

![Image 12: Vault cocktail bar old vault door](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Vault-1-800x600.jpg)

Vault is literally inside old vaults!

![Image 13: Drink at Vault cocktail bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Vault-2-450x600.jpg)

Drink at Vault

If it’s upscale you’re looking for, head to **Vault**inside the Metropolitan at the 9 hotel in downtown Cleveland. This swanky cocktail bar is located in old bank vaults (hence the name) beneath the Cleveland Trust Co Rotunda.

If you want to drink in a historic spot with lots of gilded details, it’s hard to beat this one. All the drinks here are hand-crafted, and most cost $20+.

*   **What to order:**There are about 20 drinks on the menu here, including local takes on all the classics. I like the Safety Deposit, and Elliot once tried the AZ85 (a bourbon cocktail), of which they only sell 10 per night. See the **[full Vault menu](link_31)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:** They are only open Friday and Saturday nights, and they do not take reservations.
*   **Good to know:**You enter this one through the Metropolitan at the 9 hotel, and while there’s no published dress code, it IS a fancier place, and you’ll find most people in at least business casual wear.

### LBM

_12301 Madison Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 14: Cocktail at LBM](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/LBM-coktail-768x1024.jpg)

Punch-style cocktail at LBM

![Image 15: LBM metal Viking bar in Lakewood](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/LBM-bar-768x1024.jpg)

LBM bar

I would perhaps argue that **LBM** is just as much of a restaurant as a cocktail bar, but it identifies itself as a cocktail bar first, hence why it’s on this list! Located in Lakewood, LBM is a Viking-inspired bar with a self-described Norse aesthetic, loud metal music, and inventive cocktails.

I LOVE this spot, and often take visitors here for the unique vibe.

Most cocktails here cost $15.

*   **What to order:**They always have rotating seasonal cocktails alongside a list of classics (I usually like any of their punch-style drinks). See the **[current LBM drink menu](link_32)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**LBM is open Monday-Saturday evenings, and they don’t take reservations unless you have a group of 6+.
*   **Good to know:**LBM also serves excellent food – their burger is probably my favorite burger in Cleveland!

### Western Reserve Distillers

_14221 Madison Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 16: Western Reserve Distillers patio](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/IMG_4122-800x600.jpg)

Outside Western Reserve Distillers

![Image 17: Western Reserve Distillers cocktail](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/IMG_4107-450x600.jpg)

WRD cocktail and tasting flight

**Western Reserve Distillers** is a family-owned organic craft distillery that was founded in 2014. The Lakewood distillery creates small-batch spirits, using grains from local Ohio farms. They have a bar and nice outdoor patio in the summer where you can try cocktails made from their award-winning spirits including vodka, gin, and bourbon.

Specialty cocktails here average around $14.

*   **What to order:**They have a really extensive menu of everything from margaritas to mojitos. They have a big Old Fashioneds (Elliot’s favorite), and I always like trying something off their seasonal menu. See the **[full Western Reserve Distillers menu](link_33)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**WRD is open Tuesday-Saturday evenings, plus for lunch on Friday and Saturday. You can **[make reservations online](link_34)** (but they aren’t generally required).
*   **Good to know:** Western Reserve Distillers also has a full restaurant, and hosts **[fun events](link_35)** and cocktail classes.

### Bar 32

_100 Lakeside Ave E, Cleveland_

If it’s a fancy bar with a view you’re seeking, **Bar 32** is a good option.This cocktail bar is located on the 32nd floor of the Hilton Cleveland Downtown hotel, and has both indoor and outdoor seating with Lake Erie and Cleveland views.

*   **What to order:**There’s a smaller cocktail menu here, and it changes seasonally. Everything tends to be visually pretty as well as tasty. You can see the **[current Bar 32 menu](link_36)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Bar 32 is open Tuesday-Saturday evenings, and they do not accept reservations.
*   **Good to know:**The bar sometimes closes for private events, so double check online before you go.

### And more!

A few spots not included because I still need to visit them:

*   **Quintana’s Speakeasy –**_2200 S Taylor Rd, Cleveland Heights_ – “Hidden” upstairs from a local barbershop!
*   **The Whiskey Bar –**_2767 Euclid Heights Blvd, Cleveland Heights_ – A small, cozy bar with a huge whiskey selection.

* * *

## Restaurants that are also known for their cocktails

There are so many restaurants in Cleveland that also do great cocktails, but here are 3 that I go back to again and again.

_2448 Fairmount Blvd, Cleveland_

### Get to know Cleveland Traveler

# Johnny's Bar  
On Fulton

## Classic Italian Cuisine

## A City Legacy With A New Cleveland Vibe

[RESERVATIONS](link_9)

## Johnny's Bar - winner  
of many Cleveland  
Restaurant Awards

We are proud of our heritage, and thankful for the many accolades we’ve received during our tenure. Recognized by the **Distinguished Restaurants of North America** for rigorous standards, culinary mastery, hospitality and ambiance. _**Wine Spectator**_ acknowledged Johnny’s Bar with “one of the Midwest’s most extensive wine collections. And _**The New York Times**_ hailed Johnny’s Bar as “A Classic Cleveland Dining Spot.”

[Awards](link_2)

![Image 3](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/cellar2-1024x971.jpg)

### Wine Excellence and   
Signature Cocktails

With a _Wine Spectator_ award-winning wine list, Johnny’s boasts a deeply curated cellar heavy on full-bodied Tuscan and Piedmontese reds, crisp Italian whites, and top-tier American vintages. Our mahogany bar serves up classic drinks with timeless flair—most notably our signature, ice-cold **Martinis** and stiff, expertly balanced **Old Fashioneds**, alongside refreshing guest favorites like their zesty **Moscow Mules.**

![Image 4: johnnys home sign2 300x300](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/johnnys-home-sign2-300x300-1.jpg)

### Cleveland's Original Speakeasy

For over 100 years, the **Santosuosso Family** has been a legacy the in Cleveland hospitality industry. The story of **Johnny’s Bar on Fulton** begins in 1924. With passage of the 19th amendment, the end of prohibition, and Elliot Ness liquor raids, the family’s grocery store is among the first establishments in the city licensed to sell liquor.

[Our Story](link_1)

![Image 5](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-main-dining-room.jpg)

### Top Rated Local Dining

With nearly 1,500 online reviews, our culinary and service teams are proud of our **Google 4.7** and **Open Table 4.8** ratings. We appreciate the support from our many frequent and seasonal Cleveland diners. We also invite a new generation of Northeast Ohio guests and special out-of-town visitors to enjoy the Johnny’s Bar experience.

[Reviews](link_3)

![Image 6: Long Bone Veal Chop - Johnny's Bar On Fulton](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/long-bone-veal-chop-johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-300x300.png)

### Our Menu

## Award-Winning  
Fine Dining

**Johnny’s Bar on Fulton** holds a legendary status in the Northeast Ohio culinary scene, having racked up decades of accolades:  
– _**Cleveland Magazine’s Silver Spoon Awards**_ – _**cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer’s A-List “Cleveland Classic”****Award**_.

##### Frequently Featured Entrees

###### Veal Stuffed Banana Peppers - 18.95

Hot Banana Pepper / Stuffed Veal / Marinara

###### Long Bone Veal Chop - 78.95

Tomato Concasse / Arugula / Aged Balsamic

###### Potato Crusted Grouper - MKT

Sauteed / Oven Baked / Lemon Butter

###### Classic Veal Parmesan - 42.95

Melted Mozzarella / Linguini Marinara

###### Johnny's Peppercorn Filet - 65.95

Peppercorn / Sherry / Cognac / Demi Glace

###### Veal Bolognese / House Pappardelle - 38.95

House-Made Noodles / Marinara / Pecorino Romano

###### Lake Erie Walleye Piccata - 38.95

Egg Battered / Caper Beurre Blanc

###### Sautéed Stuffed Calamari - 18.95

Fresh Herbs / Sherry / Marinara

[Full Dinner Menu](link_4)

### "Cleveland's Best Steak"

## Johnny's Peppercorn Filet

**The Legendary “Johnny’s Peppercorn Filet”:**Masterfully prepared and widely celebrated as**the best steak in Cleveland**, this tender cut features a rich cognac and sherry demi-glace.

[Best Filet](link_6)

[![Image 7](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-exterior-front-window-768x511.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-exterior-front-window-e1784936024805.jpg)

[![Image 8](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-date-night-1-768x505.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-date-night-1.jpg)

[![Image 9: Cleveland's Best - Steaks - Seafood - Spirits - Italian Cuisine](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/anotherheader.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/anotherheader.jpg)

[![Image 10](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-main-dining-room-guests-768x526.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-main-dining-room-guests-e1785314003993.jpg)

[![Image 11: Johnny's Bar On Fulton - Ladies Happy Hour - Cleveland](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-martini-bar-e1785314142364-768x562.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-martini-bar-e1785314180897.jpg)

[![Image 12](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/g-entrance-e1785314078513.jpg)](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/g-entrance-e1785314078513.jpg)

### Johnny's Bar Reviews

## Customer Comments  
4.8 Rating - Open Table

[Reviews](link_3)

![Image 13: johnnys home sign2 300x300](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/johnnys-home-sign2-300x300-1.jpg)

We love Johnny's. Food is always really good, service is outstanding. We love sitting in the garden behind the restaurant. We held a Christmas Party there, so good. Bar area is fun as well, we just love sitting in the restaurant area.

Judi

Cleveland

![Image 14](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/clevelands-best-steak-johnnys-peppercorn-filet.jpg)

Johnny’s never fails to perform above expectations! Every single time, without fail they deliver the best restaurant experience-anywhere. Peppercorn Filet Mignon is the best filet in the world. Exactly the same way every time.

Elleen

Los Angeles

[See Reviews](link_3)

![Image 15: Long Bone Veal Chop - Johnny's Bar On Fulton](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/long-bone-veal-chop-johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-e1785119101680-rr0504givxtymrryop5igflv2s5ma7z7xjkc5d48kg.png)

We’re always grateful that Johnny’s always tries to make a space for us when we make a reservation at the last minute! (Thanks Bo — also for the awesome wine selection as always). The Grilled Long Bone Veal Chop cannot be beat.

G

Cleveland

A Cleveland Classic, Johnny’s Bar On Fulton accepts bookings through Open Table. You may also call us directly during business hours for direct assistance.

### Johnny's Bar On Fulton

Since our bootlegging days during the Prohibition to our modern setting as a fine-dining restaurant, **Johnny’s Bar On Fulton** has been a family-owned establishment centered around serving the city we love with all the best. Cooking is serious business —   
an art form that requires attention to detail and a passion for the craft.

# About Johnny's Bar On Fulton

## A Cleveland  
Fine Dining  
Landmark

Over 100 Years Of Culinary Excellence

## The Legacy of Johnny's Bar:

## Over a Century of Cleveland History

For nearly a century, Johnny’s Bar on Fulton has redefined Cleveland’s culinary landscape. Tucked behind the unassuming facade of a classic westside neighborhood tavern lies an upscale, white-tablecloth Italian steakhouse steeped in prohibition-era history. Discover the perfect fusion of old-school grit and modern energy.

![Image 3](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-patio-historic.jpeg)

### From Louise’s Garden to Post-Prohibition Speakeasy

The story about Johnny’s Bar is the story of Cleveland itself. Our footprint dates back to the 1920s with _Louise’s Garden_, a neighborhood anchor that transitioned seamlessly into the post-prohibition era. When the country dried up, the westside adapted—and when prohibition ended, Johnny’s secured one of the very first liquor licenses issued in the city of Cleveland.

### Four Generations of the Santosousso Family

Today, the Santosousso family honors a 100-year legacy. Spanning four generations, from great-grandmother Louise’s early founding vision to today, the family has maintained Johnny’s status as a leading fine dining establishment. We’ve preserved the historic soul of the building while injecting a fresh, sophisticated vibe and energy that keeps Johnny’s vibrant for a new generation of diners.

![Image 4](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/santosuosso-family-cleveland-press-1970-e1785092190899.png)

* Historic Photos: Cleveland Press Collection  
Cleveland State University –  
Michael Schwartz Library

## Upscale Italian Fine Dining & The Best Steak in Cleveland

### White-Tablecloth Luxury in a Neighborhood Tavern Setting

Under the leadership of owner Bo Santosousso, Johnny’s Bar masterfully executes the ultimate culinary contrast. From the outside, we look like a welcoming, local neighborhood bar. Step through our doors, however, and you are transported into a world of white-tablecloth elegance, impeccable service, and a sophisticated, high-end dining experience.

![Image 5: johnnys-bar-on-fulton-happy-hour-couples-cleveland](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-happy-hour-couples-cleveland.jpg)

## The Legacy of Johnny's Bar:

### Iconic Menu Highlights & Time-Honored Recipes

Our menu is a reflection of Cleveland’s local grit, industry, and passion for exceptional food. Every dish relies on time-tested family secrets, including a century-old marinara recipe tracing back to our founders.

*   **The Legendary “Johnny’s Peppercorn Filet”:**Masterfully prepared and widely celebrated as**the best steak in Cleveland**, this tender cut features a rich cognac and sherry demi-glace.

*   **Signature Veal-Stuffed Banana Peppers:**A local legend, perfectly sautéed and blanketed in our traditional family sauce.

*   **Premium Long Bone Veal Chops:**Pounded, breaded, or stuffed with Asiago and shiitakes—crafted for true culinary enthusiasts.

[The Menu](https://johnnysonfulton.com/menu/)

[The Menu](https://johnnysonfulton.com/about-johnnys-bar/#)

![Image 6: Elliot Ness - Cleveland Safety Director - Outside Grocery Store](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/elliot-ness-meets-Clevelanders-outside-grocery-store-rri4cckvwxgupweelyb1r2fxcsdpa1per5h1aoc6po.jpg)

### A New Cleveland Vibe: The City's Original Speakeasy

### Post-Prohibition History, Bootlegging, and Eliot Ness

Long before it was a trend, Johnny’s was**Cleveland’s Original Speakeasy**. Our walls hold the secrets of the 1930s post-prohibition era, a time defined by bootlegging, Eliot Ness, and legendary westside liquor raids. Johnny’s provided a safe haven where locals could enjoy spirits and the camaraderie of family and friends away from prying eyes.

* Historic Photo: [Cleveland Press Collection](https://specialcollections.csuohio.edu/) – Cleveland State University – Michael Swartz Library

![Image 7: Johnny's Bar On Fulton - Ladies Happy Hour - Cleveland](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-martini-bar-e1785314180897.jpg)

### Modern Cocktails,  
Award-Winning Wine,  
& Ladies Happy Hour

Located just steps from the bustling [Ohio City](https://share.google/TfNrc5uKIZb0CZiN1) nightlife, the bar at Johnny’s blends vintage cool with modern mixology. Our professional mixologists, Lori and Linda, keep the conversation flowing and the craft cocktails pouring all night long.

*   **The Perfect Pour:**Indulge in our signature espresso martinis or explore our curated, award-winning wine selection featuring heavy-hitting Italian reds.

*   **Ladies Happy Hour – Tuesday – Thursday | 4:30 PM – 6:00 PM:** Join us for Cleveland’s premier weekday wind-down.  
Enjoy a lively new energy featuring upscale drink and menu specials starting at**only $20**.

[Happy Hour](https://johnnysonfulton.com/happy-hour/)

## Host Unforgettable Private Events & Celebrations

At Johnny’s Bar, we don’t just host dinners; we create memories. Your hosts, Bo and Sheila Santosousso, specialize in orchestrating flawless private events. Whether you are celebrating a milestone birthday, an anniversary, a graduation, or planning an intimate micro-wedding or rehearsal dinner, our team ensures a spectacular night out.

[Contact Us](https://johnnysonfulton.com/contact/)

We offer a variety of versatile, historic spaces tailored to the size and style of your gathering:

*   **Main & Side Dining Rooms:**Elegant white-tablecloth spaces perfect for traditional fine dining events.

*   **Intimate Private Venues:**Exclusive spaces dedicated to smaller, private parties of**12 guests or less**.

*   **The Lighted Patio:**A lush, beautifully lit outdoor oasis offering full fine-dining service under the stars.

*   **“Rent the House” Options:** For large corporate galas or grand life celebrations, you can reserve the entire historic restaurant.

## Cleveland’s Business Meeting  
& Corporate Lunch Leader

### A Century Of Distinction

# Cleveland Restaurant Awards

Johnny’s Bar On Fulton:  
From Prohibition Speakeasy  
To Culinary Landmark

## Critical Acclaim  
Local Distinction

For over a century,**Johnny’s Bar On Fulton** has received many restaurant awards and has stood as one of Northeast Ohio’s most revered culinary institutions. Known for its flawless white-tablecloth service, vintage Art Deco charm, and exceptional Northern Italian menu, Johnny’s has earned decades of critical acclaim from local, regional, and national dining critics. From prestigious culinary societies and national food guides to local reader polls, the restaurant awards and accolades received by Johnny’s Bar reflect an enduring dedication to excellence that few establishments in the Midwest can match.

[Reservations](https://johnnysonfulton.com/reservations/)

## Major Media Recognition &  
Restaurant Accolades

Throughout its storied history, Johnny’s Bar On Fulton has earned prestigious awards across every major dining category—from culinary execution and service to wine list depth and romantic atmosphere.

### Highest Ratings for  
Food & Service

In its iconic print and digital guides, the national**Zagat Survey**famously described dining at Johnny’s Bar as nothing short of “nirvana”. Highlighting the restaurant’s authentic Northern Italian offerings, Zagat praised Johnny’s as a “real experience” that evokes the sophisticated energy of top-tier New York fine dining establishments. For multiple years, Johnny’s maintained the highest Zagat ratings for food, service, and popularity in Cuyahoga County, earning coveted spots on Zagat’s lists for _America’s Best Restaurants_ and _Best Overall Service_.

![Image 3: cheers](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/cheers.jpg)

### Cleveland.com A-List:  
Voted a "Cleveland Classic"

In local polling by[Cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/), Johnny’s Bar On Fulton was officially inducted into the**A-List as a “Cleveland Classic” Restaurant**. In bestowing the award, critics noted that _“Johnny’s Bar on Fulton exudes overall excellence, creativity, exacting preparations, superior service, and an atmosphere that is distinctive and inviting.”_

### Cleveland Magazine: Multiple Silver Spoon Award Winner

As a staple of the local media landscape,**[Cleveland Magazine](https://clevelandmagazine.com/)**has repeatedly honored Johnny’s across decades of its annual**Silver Spoon Awards**. Featured in retrospective pieces such as[“Tried & True: Johnny’s Bar”](https://clevelandmagazine.com/articles/tried-true-johnnys-bar/)and celebrated in[“Johnny’s Bar on Fulton Celebrates 100 Years of Business”](https://clevelandmagazine.com/articles/johnny-s-bar-on-fulton-celebrates-100-years-of-business/), the publication routinely praises house signatures like the grilled long-bone veal chop, stuffed banana peppers, and hand-crafted Old Fashioneds.

## DiRoNA & Wine Spectator Honors

**Distinguished Restaurants of North America (DiRoNA):**Johnny’s Bar earned the prestigious DiRoNA Award, an honor reserved for fewer than 700 independent dining rooms across North America that meet rigorous standards for culinary mastery, hospitality, and physical ambiance.

**Wine Spectator Award of Excellence:**Recognized for curating one of the Midwest’s most extensive wine collections, Johnny’s wine program regularly receives top marks from _Wine Spectator_, specializing in rare Tuscan reds, Piedmontese vintages, and global reserve pairings.

## National Praise As  
Iconic Destination

The reputation of Johnny’s Bar extends far beyond Northeast Ohio. National media outlets and travel guides frequently cite Johnny’s as a must-visit destination for travelers, business executives, and culinary enthusiasts visiting Cleveland:

*   **_The New York Times:_**Hailed Johnny’s as _“A Classic Cleveland Dining Spot.”_

*   **_The Plain Dealer:_**Proclaimed the restaurant to be _“One of Cleveland’s finest dining destinations.”_

*   **_The Miami Herald:_**Designated Johnny’s as _“A Cleveland Classic.”_

*   **_Fox 8 & Cleveland Scene:_** Consistently named among the Top 5 Most Romantic Restaurants in Cleveland.

![Image 4: Cleveland Best Restaurants - Silver Spoon - Johnny's Bar On Fulton](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cleveland-best-restaurants-johnnys-bar-on-fulton-silver-spoon-award-753x1024.jpg)

Whether you are seeking an award-winning veal entree, planning an executive business meeting in our private Wine Room, or celebrating a milestone anniversary on our lush Courtyard Patio, Johnny’s Bar On Fulton invites you to partake in a century-old Cleveland tradition. Discover for yourself why food critics, industry experts, and generations of loyal patrons consistently name Johnny’s among Cleveland’s greatest restaurant achievements.

# The Best Cleveland Restaurants for a Special Occasion or Celebration

*   Post author:[Amanda](https://clevelandtraveler.com/author/cletraveler/)
*   Post category:[Food/Drink](https://clevelandtraveler.com/category/food-drink/)
*   Post last modified:January 27, 2026

Looking for the perfect place in Greater Cleveland to go out for a fancy meal to celebrate a birthday, anniversary, graduation, job promotion, or anything else worth celebrating?

Well, good news! We have a lot of them.

Cleveland is actually a big foodie city, and that extends to special occasion dining, too, whether you’re looking for an upscale steakhouse, delicious seafood, hand-made pasta, or something else entirely.

Here are my favorite special occasion restaurants around Cleveland, in no particular order. I’m including the best fine dining spots, followed by some places that I love for special occasions that are a little easier on the wallet.

## Top fine dining restaurants in Cleveland

_Note: Making reservations in advance is highly recommended (necessary, even) for most of these spots. And if you’re celebrating something special, be sure to let them know when you book, and again when you arrive!_

### Marble Room Steaks and Raw Bar

_623 Euclid Ave, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Steaks and seafood

**Price range:** 💸💸💸💸

![Image 3: Marble Room meal](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Marble-Room-meal-768x1024.jpg)

Meal at Marble Room

![Image 4: Marble Room cotton candy](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Marble-Room-cotton-candy-768x1024.jpg)

Cotton candy cloud

Marble Room is one of the more iconic fine dining restaurants in Cleveland. It’s located downtown on Euclid Avenue inside the former National City Bank building, which was originally built in 1893 by the sons of President James A. Garfield.

The inside of Marble Room oozes 1920s opulence, with huge marble columns, chandeliers, a gilded ceiling, and some features left over from the site’s banking days. Even though it feels like Marble Room has been around forever, it’s only been open as a restaurant since 2017!

Marble Room is known for its steaks and seafood. It does have a full raw bar with oysters, sushi, and even a caviar service, plus 10+ cuts of steak to choose from. Sides are meant to share. Find the **[Marble Room menu here](https://www.marbleroomcle.com/dinner-menu/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**The service here is absolutely impeccable, and if you’re celebrating a birthday or anniversary, they’ll bring out a complimentary fluff of cotton candy to mark the occasion. (You can designate a special occasion when you book a table.)

**Good to know:**Marble Room does not have a dress code, technically, but “upscale casual to dressy” attire is recommended to fit in with the space. Also, this is one place in Cleveland that tends to book up weeks if not months in advance, so plan accordingly.

![Image 5: Amanda and Elliot at Marble Room](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Marble-Room-couple-1024x768.jpg)

Out with Elliot at Marble Room for my birthday

* * *

### Il Venetian

_100 St Clair Ave NE, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Italian food, plus seafood

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

A great Italian spot in Cleveland is Il Venetian, located inside Key Tower. This upscale restaurant transports you to Italy (much of the decor, including the chandeliers, was imported from Venice), and is a really beautiful space with high ceilings and lots of natural light during the day.

The menu at Il Venetian features fresh seafood and pastas that are hand-made daily, plus more than 200 wines to choose from. They even make their own bread! Find the **[Il Venetian menu here](https://www.ilvenetian.com/dinner-menu/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**The service, food, and beautiful dining room all combine for a memorable place to share a meal.

**Good to know:** You can order the “Chef’s Trio” of pasta and sample 3 different types of pasta at once (minimum 2 people must order, and it costs $30 per person). Also, dressier attire is recommended here.

* * *

### Cordelia

_2058 E 4th St, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Unique takes on classic American dishes

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

Opened in 2022 and led by led by James Beard Award Finalist Chef Vinnie Cimino, Cordelia has quickly rocketed up to the top of my “best restaurants in Cleveland” list. The concept is simple: modern takes on Midwest “comfort food.” When I first went to Cordelia, I was told the vibe was “modern grandma,” and that totally tracks.

The dishes at Cordelia change slightly based on what local produce is in season, but you can always expect a variety of small plates and mains, many of which are made to share. You’ll always find a mix of vegetarian dishes and local meats, plus seafood fresh from Kate’s Fish at West Side Market. Find the **[Cordelia menu here](https://cordeliacle.com/our-menu)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**The vibes at Cordelia are so good, and I’ve never been disappointed by the food or drinks. It’s also located on lively E 4th St, which is a fun place to go out.

**Good to know:** They also do a chef’s tasting menu for $90 per person.

![Image 6: Cordelia exterior](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/IMG_9965-768x1024.jpg)

Cordelia on E 4th

* * *

### Casa La Luna

_2100 Superior Viaduct, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Italian food and city views

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

Formerly Luca Italian Cuisine, Casa La Luna is one of the most popular Italian restaurants in Cleveland. The award-winning spot sits up on the Superior Viaduct, serving up excellent skyline views alongside its Italian classics. They have a really nice patio in the warmer months, too.

You can’t go wrong with any of their pasta dishes here, and their veal dishes are also excellent. And don’t skip the tiramisu for dessert! Find the **[Casa La Luna menu here](https://www.lalunacleveland.com/menu)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**When you add the good food to the views over the Cuyahoga River and Cleveland skyline, you get the perfect setting for any special occasion.

**Good to know:** They also have an extensive wine list, with nearly 100 different wines to choose from.

* * *

### Cru Uncorked

_34300 Chagrin Blvd, Moreland Hills_

**Known for:**French-American cuisine

**Price range:** 💸💸💸💸

Down in Moreland Hills, Cru Uncorked also deserves a spot on this list. This French restaurant resembles a French chateau on the outside, and has a beautiful and sprawling outdoor patio space when the weather is nice. Dishes here are presented picture-perfectly, which makes it feel even more high-end.

The menu at Cru includes all the French classics like escargot, steak tartare, and Coq au vin, but you’ll also find things like lobster risotto, venison, and even a burger on the menu. They also have excellent cocktails and an extensive wine list. Find the **[Cru Uncorked menu here](https://cruuncorked.com/menu/#dinner)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**Everything about Cru Uncorked screams fine dining. There are four different dining rooms, each decorated with French antiques and artwork. The tables are spaced nicely, too, which makes it feel more intimate.

**Good to know:** There’s a lounge that’s open for drinks, but you really do need a reservation to dine here. Valet parking is complementary.

* * *

### Dante

_2247 Professor Ave, Suite C, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Modern American food with a Mediterranean twist

**Price range:** 💸💸💸 (or 💸💸💸💸 if you do the chef’s tasting menu)

This Tremont staple by Michelin Starred Chef Dante Boccuzzi is a cozy spot for delicious food in a space that also used to be a bank. The menu here is more varied, featuring everything from homemade pasta to seafood.

Dante offers both an a la carte menu and the option of doing a chef’s tasting menu. The tasting menu is 5 courses and costs $95. Find the full **[Dante menu here](https://danteboccuzzi.com/dante-tremont/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**If you want to book chef tasting menu for a special occasion, you can’t go wrong with this one!

**Good to know:** This is one of several Cleveland area restaurants owned by Dante Boccuzzi (there’s another on this list!), so be sure you’re making reservations at the correct one.

* * *

### Pier W

_12700 Lake Ave, Lakewood_

**Known for:**Seafood and Lake Erie views

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

If seafood is your preference, you can’t go wrong with Pier W, the premier fine dining location in Lakewood. Large picture windows look out over Lake Erie and towards the Cleveland skyline, making this a memorable spot to dine.

The menu here is seafood-heavy, featuring everything from oysters to shrimp to fish, and it’s all sourced directly from fishermen. They also have a few non-seafood dishes, for anyone craving the views but not the seafood. Find the **[Pier W menu here](https://pierw.com/menu/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**It’s hard to beat those Lake Erie views!

**Good to know:** Pier W is also well-known for its seafood-heavy Sunday brunch. The brunch is pricier, though, at $69 per person. Business casual dress is recommended for brunch or dinner.

* * *

### Jaja

_2050 Gehring Ave, Cleveland_

_Note: Jaja suffered damage from a car crash in 2024, and is currently closed. It has plans to reopen in early 2026._

**Known for:**Steaks, shared plates, and vibes

**Price range:** 💸💸💸, but could be 💸💸💸💸

![Image 7: Jaja interior design](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7221-768x1024.jpg)

Inside Jaja

![Image 8: Steak at Jaja](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7236-768x1024.jpg)

Steak at Jaja

When it comes to vibes, few restaurants on this list compare with Jaja. This restaurant in Ohio City has fun decor, Instagram-worthy dishes, and lots of natural light from all the windows — it even has a retractable glass roof!

The menu at Jaja is Argentinean steakhouse-inspired, so you’ll find plenty of meat on the menu (cooked on an impressive 20-foot wood-fired grill). But you’ll also find good veggie and fish dishes. All the plates are meant to be shared, so you can mix and match whatever sounds good to you. Find the full **[Jaja menu here](https://www.jajacleveland.com/dinner-menu)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**There’s no denying it’s a gorgeous restaurant, and I’m a fan of shared plates for a special night out, as it means you can try more things!

**Good to know:** They also have a great cocktail menu.

![Image 9: Bar at Jaja](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7250-1024x768.jpg)

The Jaja bar also serves all the vibes

* * *

### Ginko Restaurant

_2247 Professor Ave B, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Sushi

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

Another spot by Chef Dante Boccuzzi in Tremont, Ginko is for the Japanese and sushi lovers in Cleveland. The sleek red-and-black restaurant is built around a large bar, and serves up world-class sushi, nigiri, and even shabu shabu at dedicated tables.

Ginko also offers a 6-course chef-led omakase tasting menu, which is excellent for a special occasion. Find the **[Ginko menu here](https://danteboccuzzi.com/ginko-restaurant/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**It offers some of the best sushi in the city, and the special tasting menus are great for a memorable night out.

**Good to know:** If you’re looking for a wider range of Japanese option (sushi plus noodles, tempura, and more), check out **[Goma](https://gomarestaurant.com/goma-menu/)**, another Dante Boccuzzi spot downtown.

* * *

### L’Albatros

_11401 Bellflower Rd, Cleveland_

**Known for:**French-inspired fare

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

Located in the beautiful University Circle in an old carriage house on the campus of Case Western Reserve University, don’t overlook L’Albatros for a romantic night out or celebration. This restaurant by chef and restaurateur Zack Bruell has been around since 2008.

They’re known for their classic French brasserie vibes and food, plus a really nice patio area in the warmer months. Try a French classic like French onion soup, cassoulet, or duck confit. See the **[L’Albatros menu here](https://www.albatrosbrasserie.com/le-menu/dinner)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**French restaurants always feel fancy, don’t they? Plus, the service here is top-notch.

* * *

### EDWINS Leadership & Restaurant

_12383 Cedar Rd, Cleveland Heights_

**Known for:** Elevated French dishes

**Price range:** 💸💸 or 💸💸💸

EDWINS changed locations in 2025, moving from Shaker Square into the old NightTown building in Cleveland Heights. It may be in a new space, but the mission and food hasn’t changed. EDWINS isn’t just a restaurant — it’s also a non-profit organization begun by Brandon Edwin Chrostowski that offers training in the culinary and hospitality industries for formerly incarcerated adults.

People go to EDWINS for delicious traditional French dishes, from duck confit to côte de boeuf. EDWINS actually has more than one dining option: you can enjoy a more laid-back Brasserie setting, or their more high-end dining room. They also serve brunch and have a Cigar Bar. Find the **[EDWINS menus here](https://edwinsrestaurant.org/brasserie/)**.

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**Good food, good vibes, and a good mission! For a fancier experience, definitely book a table in the dining room.

**Good to know:**EDWINS has a new **[live music series](https://edwinsrestaurant.org/music/)**, which transforms the restaurant into a jazz club several nights per month.

* * *

## Other special occasion restaurants in Cleveland

Okay, so the above list includes slightly pricier spots that are considered more “fine dining” in terms of menus, space, and overall vibe. But I have a few additional restaurants that I LOVE for a special night out that don’t always carry quite the same price tag.

So here are 5 more spots to consider:

### STEAK

_2179 W 11th St, Cleveland_

**Known for:**Steaks, of course!

**Price range:** 💸💸💸

![Image 10: STEAK Cleveland](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/STEAK-Cleveland-1024x768.jpg)

Inside STEAK

![Image 11: STEAK bathtub cocktail](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/STEAK-bathtub-drink-731x1024.jpg)

My bathtub gin cocktail

STEAK Cleveland can come with a fine dining price (depending on what you order), but it doesn’t have a stuffy fine dining vibe AT ALL. This place is pure fun, making it a spot my husband Elliot and I love for a special occasion.

The vibe at STEAK is a little like a nightclub — it’s dark and mostly lit by neon signs, and there’s irreverence in a lot of its details, like the butcher-knife-shaped steak knives, and the cocktails the come in mini bathtubs.

What I love here is their prix-fixe menu, which includes popcorn to snack on, a salad to start with, a steak of your choosing, and bottomless waffle fries all for between $35 and $65 (depending on the steak). I actually think that’s very reasonable for that amount of food! They also have smash burgers and additional sides. See the **[STEAK Cleveland menu here](https://www.steakcle.com/menus)**.

(Also, they’ve gone mini-viral for their crazy desserts, including their sundae Ferris wheel, which is indeed served in a table top Ferris wheel.)

**Why it’s good for special occasions:**This spot is just fun — and the food is good! If you let them know you’re celebrating a birthday or anniversary, you’ll get a cookie shot for free for dessert.

* * *

### Amba

_1430 W 28th St, Cleveland_

**Known for:** Indian-inspired small plates

**Price range:** 💸💸

![Image 12: Meal at Amba](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Amba-1024x1024.jpg)

Meal at Amba

Amba is such an excellent addition to the Ohio City dining scene. The dimly-lit space has a bar and dining area, and serves up small plates packing big flavor. The idea is to share a variety of dishes, with most plates costing around $10-$15.

# Cleveland Wine Bars: The Best Places to Drink Wine in Cleveland

*   Post author:[Kat Weiss Butler](https://clevelandtraveler.com/author/katweiss/)
*   Post category:[Food/Drink](https://clevelandtraveler.com/category/food-drink/)
*   Post last modified:May 7, 2021

Happy hour is calling, and we must go! Whether you love reds, whites, or rosés, it is time to dive into the best wine bars in and around Cleveland!

While Cleveland is definitely known for [its amazing breweries](https://clevelandtraveler.com/cleveland-breweries/), when it comes to wine, there are also some pretty awesome spots to grab a glass of vino. Whether you are searching for a new [date night spot](https://clevelandtraveler.com/category/date-night/) or want to grab drinks with friends, this city has some fantastic wine bars to satisfy your cravings.

## 6 of the Best Wine Bars in Cleveland

If you are looking to do some wine tasting in Cleveland, here are our go-to spots.

### 1. Market Avenue Wine Bar

_2521 Market Ave., Cleveland_ _(Ohio City)_

![Image 3: Market Ave Wine Bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Market-Ave-Wine-Bar-1024x928.jpg)

Wine on the patio at Market Avenue Wine Bar

Perfect for a [date night in Ohio City](https://clevelandtraveler.com/cleveland-date-night-ohio-city/), this cozy spot is situated on the lovely cobblestone street of Market Avenue adjacent to W 25 th.

While you could sit inside on velvet chairs under romantic mood lighting, we love sitting outside in the summertime, as you’ll have fantastic views of the iconic West Side Market!

This spot is the perfect place to split a bottle of wine or try a glass or two from around the world like an Argentinian Malbec, California Chardonnay, or perhaps French Bordeaux. Pair it with one their hor d’oeuvres like baked Brie or olives, and you’ll feel like you’re sitting at a Parisian café enjoying your glass of vino.

Plus, if you are planning an event, they have party space available, too!

### 2. Flight

_5712 Detroit Ave., Cleveland (Gordon Square)_

![Image 4: Flight Cleveland](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/IMG_0070-1024x768.jpg)

Bubbly flight and cheese board

This newer Cleveland wine bar is quickly becoming a crowd favorite, and i’s easy to see why! While you could certainly get just a glass of wine, this spot is known for its fantastic wine flights.

Flight has 13 different wine flights on offer! Enjoy some bubbly with the _Let’s Get Fizzical_ with 3 tastings of sparking wine from France and Italy. Or try _The Italian Job_ for some phenomenal Italian whites.

My favorite is definitely the _Rainbow Nation._ I’m a big fan of South African wine, especially Chenin Blanc! Try that paired with a Cabernet Franc and a red blend, and you’ll feel like you’ve been transported to a sunny day in the Western Cape.

For real though, this place is a gem. Flight also has a wine shop to pick up a bottle for home (or you can drink it there for a fee), along with a really cute outdoor patio for those sunny summer days.

### 3. Toast

_1365 W 65th St., Cleveland (Gordon Square)_

Another great wine bar in Cleveland, this place in Gordon Square is a fantastic date night location. With many cocktails, a fabulous wine list, and perfectly shareable small plates, you’ll enjoy a post-work happy hour and unwind here.

![Image 5: Toast Cleveland](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/IMG_2298-768x1024.jpg)

Toast’s shareable plates are also top-notch.

Aside from their awesome rosé, as mentioned above, they have unique wines from around the world including an orange wine from the country of Georgia, many wines from Italy’s wine regions, and even a couple of selections from Maryland and Long Island.

They also label their wine list with organic, natural, sustainable, and biodynamic wines for those that are interested in knowing how the wine was produced.

### 4. CLE Urban Winery

_2180 Lee Rd, Cleveland Heights_

Located in the historic Cedar-Lee neighborhood in Cleveland Heights, this urban-style winery almost looks like a brewery at first glance. However, it is actually wine being made in those big vats!

This laid-back place offers brewery vibes, and they are known for naming their wines after Cleveland landmarks, neighborhoods, and traditions as well as giving back to the community.

This place isn’t just selling wine by the glass either! They also serve wine flights, a delicious wine slushie, and even wine cocktails.If you prefer to stick to regular vino, then the Rustbelt Rose or Murray Hill Pinot Grigio are sure to please.

### 5. Humble Wine Bar

_15400 Detroit Ave., Lakewood_

![Image 6: Pizza and wine at Humble Wine Bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Pizza-And-Wine-At-Humble-Wine-Bar-1024x843.jpg)

Wine and pizza – what a combo!

Who said pizza and beer are the way to go? Pizza and wine is pretty much the bomb dot com over at Humble Wine Bar in Lakewood.

With Neapolitan-style pizza, fabulous charcuterie and wine boards, and an extensive wine list, you’ll leave here feeling full and happy. We love this spot for a date night with dinner and drinks.

They have some fantastic pizza including fig and prosciutto, chorizo, and even a vegan sausage pizza. Pair it with world-class wine like a Grenache/Syrah from the Rhone Valley in France or a Sauvignon Blanc from the Marlborough Sound in New Zealand. Basically, if you are searching for fantastic pizza and wine to pair it with, this is the place.

Humble Wine Bar also has a nice patio area that’s also dog-friendly, meaning it’s a spot the whole family can enjoy.

### 6. Rocky River Wine Bar

_1313 Linda St., Rocky River_

If you travel further west, you’ll happen upon Rocky River Wine Bar. While this is a bit further from downtown, this Cleveland wine bar has an award-winning wine list.

You can also get brunch here to enjoy with wine or typical brunch drinks like a Bloody Mary or mimosa.

But no matter when you visit Rocky River Wine Bar, you’ll love their lengthy wine list including some Veuve Cliquot Champagne, a tawny port from Portugal, or even a glass of their ever-rotating rosé selection.

## Notable Wine Shops Where You Can Drink Wine in Cleveland

### 1. Rozi’s Wine House

_14900 Detroit Ave., Lakewood_

![Image 7: Rozis Wine House](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Wine-Tasting-at-Rozis-Wine-House-1024x768.jpg)

Drink while you shop!

I’ve been visiting this wine shop for a couple of years and absolutely love it. First of all, it has a fantastic shop to purchase wines from around the world. Second, if you prefer beer, this place also has an immense selection and the option to “make your own 6-pack.”

We have spotted many unique wines and great beers from around the world at this place! And they also sell gift baskets and plenty of beer and wine accessories.

The best part is that you can drink while shopping here thanks to their Front Porch Café. Or you could just sit and sip on their front porch area. They have some fantastic wines to try, like a great Pinot Noir from Oregon or even a Riesling from Germany.

### 2. Heinen’s of Downtown Cleveland

_900 Euclid Ave., Cleveland_

![Image 8: Wine at Heinens Downtown](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Wine-Tasting-at-Heinens-Downtown-1024x768.jpg)

I know what you’re thinking: can’t you pretty much buy wine at any old grocery store? Well, yes. But there is your run-of-the-mill grocery store, and then there is Heinen’s downtown.

Located inside the historic Cleveland Trust Co. building downtown, this place is not only an architectural gem, but also the perfect spot for happy hour wine tasting in Cleveland!

You can either get wine by the glass for a super-reasonable price during happy hour, or you can load up a card and check out dozens of wines on tap to fill your glass up with.

And they have an exhaustive selection of wine. From the rare and expensive to the everyday drinkable wine, you could spend hours here just tasting, shopping, and trying to figure out which wine you’d like to have next. They have wine from around the world and even from Ohio!

If you aren’t sure what kind of wine you like or want to branch out and try some new varieties without spending a lot of money, this is definitely a fantastic spot to go to. Plus, if you get hungry, the first floor has a lot of prepared foods for your dinner.

### 3. Little Birdie Wine Nest

_6060 Broadview Rd, Parma_

![Image 9: Little Birdie Wine Nest brunch board and mimosa flights](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/IMG_0638-1024x1024.jpg)

Mimosa flights and a brunch board

If you’re looking for a spot that offers a little bit of everything (and I do mean everything, from a wine store to a coffee bar to space for sip-and-paint events and even a yoga studio), then you need to head to Little Birdie Wine Nest in Parma.

The wine store section of the shop has a wide selection of wines to suit all tastes and price points. Their dine-in (or I guess we should say drink-in) menu includes pours of several different wines, along with sangrias and wine slushies.

They also have various flights you can order, from regular wine flights to wine slushie flights to the very popular mimosa flight. To go along with any of these, you can order a charcuterie board, or even a brunch board.

## **Tips for Wine Drinking**

Whew! I know these are all fantastic options for wine bars in Cleveland, but here are some key tips to know about drinking wine:

### 1. Don’t drink and drive.

I mean this goes without saying I suppose, but be responsible and either have a designated driver or get an Uber or Lyft home.

### 2. Key Regions/Wines to Note

I’m in the camp that if I plan to drink wine, I love to savor it. I love learning where the wine comes from, its flavor profile, and more. If you are of a similar mindset and nerd out over this stuff, or if you are starting to learn more about wine, here are some well-known wines on many menus and some key regions where the grapes grows best.

![Image 10: Sokol Blosser Winery in Oregon's Willamette Valley
](https://photos.smugmug.com/North-America/USA/Oregon/i-HBPCgWG/0/1f00ebec/XL/P6112010-XL.jpg)

Sokol Blosser Winery in Oregon’s Willamette Valley

*   **Pinot Noir**
    *   Willamette Valley, Oregon
    *   Santa Barbara and Sonoma Valley, California
    *   Burgundy, France
    *   Northern Italy
    *   Central Otago, New Zealand

*   **Cabernet Sauvignon**
    *   Napa Valley and Sonoma Valley, California
    *   Bordeaux, France
    *   South Australia
    *   Aconcagua Valley, Chile

*   **Chardonnay**
    *   Burgundy, France
    *   Sonoma Valley and Russian River, California
    *   Mendoza, Argentina
    *   Southern & Eastern Australia

*   **Sauvignon Blanc**
    *   Marlborough Sound, New Zealand
    *   Loire Valley, France
    *   Tuscany, Italy
    *   Casablanca and San Antonia Valley, Chile
    *   Western Cape, South Africa
    *   Napa Valley, California

*   **Riesling**
    *   Mosel Valley, Germany
    *   Alsace, France
    *   Finger Lakes, New York
    *   South Australia

*   **Pinot Grigio**
    *   Northern Italy
    *   Sonoma, California
    *   Willamette Valley, Oregon

![Image 11: Wine tasting in South Africa](https://photos.smugmug.com/Africa/South-Africa/i-dcTkngh/0/5dc60bfd/XL/P5100615-XL.jpg)

Wine tasting in South Africa

This isn’t an exhaustive list, but if you choose one of these wines from any of these regions, chances are it’ll be pretty good!

### 3. Know where to learn more

Want to learn more about wine? I love checking out apps like Vivino for wine ratings and reviews, and my favorite book for learning about wine is _[Windows on the World Complete Wine Course](https://amzn.to/39BtA7y)_ by Kevin Zraly.

When it comes to wine tasting in Cleveland, there are plenty of amazing places to enjoy a glass. From wines from around the globe to even in Ohio’s own backyard, you’ll enjoy these unique wine bars in Cleveland!
