# 10+ of the Best Cocktail Bars in Cleveland

*   Post author:[Amanda](https://clevelandtraveler.com/author/cletraveler/)
*   Post category:[Food/Drink](https://clevelandtraveler.com/category/food-drink/)
*   Post last modified:May 23, 2025

Cleveland is arguably a beer city, with **[40+ craft breweries](https://clevelandtraveler.com/cleveland-breweries/)** throughout the Great Cleveland area. The city does bars, breweries, and pubs very well – there’s literally something for everyone.

But what about spots for people who prefer cocktails to beer? Well, good news – Cleveland has plenty of cocktail bars, too!

Below is my list of the best dedicated cocktail bars in Cleveland, plus a few restaurants that also do notably great cocktails.

_**Note:**This list specifically focuses on cocktails and bars that primarily specialize in them. If you’re looking for mocktail options, **[I have another post for that](https://clevelandtraveler.com/mocktails-in-cleveland/)!**_

* * *

## Cleveland’s best cocktail bars

Here are the best cocktail bars in Cleveland, roughly listed in order of my favorites – though it admittedly does change from time to time, and you really can’t go wrong with any of these!

### Porco Lounge & Tiki Room

_2527 W 25th St, Cleveland_

![Image 3: Drinks at Porco Lounge & Tiki Room](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_9151-768x1024.jpg)

Tiki drinks at Porco

Located between the historic neighborhoods of Tremont and Ohio City in Cleveland, **Porco Lounge & Tiki Room** is a hidden oasis of a cocktail bar in a rather unassuming building along W 25th. The tiki vibes are strong here – and the drinks are even stronger! (Seriously, I think they make the strongest cocktails in the city.)

Porco will transport you to the South Pacific with its tiki decor and tropical cocktails, and it’s hands-down one of the best places to get a unique cocktail in Cleveland. Porco uses classic tiki cocktail recipes, made with fresh ingredients and house-made syrups.

Most of their cocktails are $18.

*   **What to order:**Tiki drinks, of course! My personal favorites are the Painkiller and Saturn, while my husband Elliot likes the Fog Cutter and Heart of Darkness. They also have a few shareable cocktails for groups, like the Scorpion Bowl. Find the **[full Porco menu](https://porcolounge.com/menu/)** here.
*   **Hours and reservations:**This spot is open Wednesday-Saturday evenings, and reservations are highly recommended. You can call, or **[reserve a table online](https://porcolounge.com/reservations/)**.
*   **Good to know:**Porco also offers food from Pinoy Fine Foods! Highly recommended, as these drinks are super strong.

### Cloak & Dagger

_2399 W 11th St, Cleveland_

![Image 4: Cloak & Dagger](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_1530-768x1024.jpg)

Inside Cloak & Dagger

![Image 5: Drinks at Cloak & Dagger](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/IMG_1539-768x1024.jpg)

Cloak & Dagger drinks

**Cloak & Dagger** is giving dark academia with its low-lit bar and literary theme. This cocktail bar is located in Tremont, and is easily one of the best in Cleveland in terms of both drinks and overall vibe.

Cloak & Dagger is also unique in that they release a new “book” (i.e. a new menu) each season with brand new drinks. Meaning you can visit this cocktail bar over and over and always find something new to try.

All cocktails here are $16.

*   **What to order:**The menu is always changing! But they always have a “Legends” section of their more popular and classic drinks. The Dagger Dagger and Rabbit’s Foot are favorites of ours. They can also make several of their cocktails non-alcoholic. See the current **[Cloak & Dagger menu](https://cloakanddaggercle.com/)** on their website.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Cloak & Dagger is open Tuesday-Sunday nights, and reservations are needed. You can **[make them online](https://www.opentable.com/restref/client/?corrid=ccb9ac08-8a95-4e9d-8dd1-928a7308b601&lang=en-US&ot_source=Restaurant%20website&restref=1083529)** through OpenTable.
*   **Good to know:**They also have a small menu of all-vegan bar snacks.

### Amazonia

_1640 Hopkins Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 6: Drink at Amazonia bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Amazonia-1-450x600.jpg)

Such a pretty drink!

![Image 7: Inside Amazonia bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Amazonia-2-450x600.jpg)

Inside Amazonia

Listed on Google Maps as a pizza spot, **Amazonia** is also home to an incredible little speakeasy-style bar inside a converted house in Lakewood. The indoor bar space is dark and filled with antiques, trinkets, and the feeling of stepping into the attic collection of an old explorer.

The drinks here are inventive and delicious. Classic cocktails cost $13-$14, while themed specialty cocktails cost $16-$18.

*   **What to order:**The drink menu has changed since I visited, but definitely take a look at their specialty cocktail menu, which is always themed and thoughtful! See the **[full Amazonia menu](https://www.amazoniabar.com/menus)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Amazonia is open Tuesday-Sunday nights, and they don’t take reservations unless you have a large group.
*   **Good to know:** Amazonia has a great pizza menu, too, along with some small plates and a blackberry gelato that you really should try. It’s also connected to the patio at Hola Tacos.

### Society Lounge

_2063 E 4th St, Cleveland_

**Society Lounge** is a speakeasy-style bar downtown that is designed to take you back in time to the swanky social scene of decades past. Walk down the steps from E. 4th street into the newly-renovated elegant space, and enjoy specialty hand-crafted cocktails using fresh ingredients and homemade syrups.

Specialty drinks here are all $18.

*   **What to order:**My go-to is either the Burnin’ the Benjamins or Giggle Juice, while Elliot is all about the Legend of Bagger Vance. They also have mocktails See the **[full Society Lounge menu](https://societycleveland.com/)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Society Lounge is open Tuesday-Saturday nights, and they do technically take reservations, though it’s through their “**[private events](https://societycleveland.com/private-events/)**” page.
*   **Good to know:** Society Lounge is also known for transforming into the festive Miracle Pop-Up Bar during the Christmas season, which is one of the**[best holiday pop-up bars in Cleveland](https://clevelandtraveler.com/cleveland-christmas-pop-up-bars/)**.

### Flower on Freeman

_2102 Freeman Ave, Cleveland_

![Image 8: Flower on Freeman bar interior](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Flower-on-Freeman-1-800x600.jpg)

Inside Flower on Freeman

![Image 9: Flower on Freeman charcuterie board](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Flower-on-Freeman-3-450x600.jpg)

Drinks and Gold Board for 2

Brand new in 2025, **Flower on Freeman** easily made it onto this list after just one visit. The bright bar in Duck Island (not far from West Side Market in Ohio City) feels both fancy and whimsical, with a colorful interior and a nice little patio space.

Drinks here average around $17, with a few more expensive ones. Mocktails are $7-$11.

*   **What to order:**The hand-crafted drinks here are beautiful and unique; I really liked the Pocket Full of Posey, while Elliot enjoyed the Smoked Blossom. They also have some unique mocktails on the menu. See the **[full Flower on Freeman menu](https://www.floweronfreeman.com/menu)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**They’re open Monday-Saturday nights, and currently are not taking reservations, but that could change.
*   **Good to know:**Flower on Freeman also serves some small plates, and the Gold Board (for either 2 or 4 guests) might be the most beautiful cheese + charcuterie board I’ve ever been served.

### Velvet Tango Room

_2095 Columbus Rd, Cleveland_

![Image 10: Velvet Tango Room bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7265-768x1024.jpg)

Velvet Tango Room front bar

![Image 11: Drinks at Velvet Tango Room](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/IMG_7261-768x1024.jpg)

Drinks at VTR

Just around the corner from Flower on Freeman, **Velvet Tango Room** is one of Cleveland’s longest-standing craft cocktail bars, having opened in 1996. More than 25 years later, this cozy and intimate cocktail bar is still one of the best places to grab a drink in Cleveland.

Inside, you’ll find a wood-paneled bar and an absolutely massive cocktail list. All drinks here are $20 (except during Happy Hour Monday-Friday), and are made to order.

*   **What to order:**There are so many cocktails to choose from. Under each type of alcohol on the menu you’ll find “Classics,” “Contemporary Classics,” and then “VTR Originals,” which you’ll only find at this bar. Last time I went I had an India Lime Fizz (a VTR gin original), and it was so good. Find the **[full Velvet Tango Room menu](https://www.velvettangoroom.com/menus/)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Velvet Tango Room is open 7 days a week, including late afternoons on Sundays. They do take reservations, and you can **[make them online](https://www.velvettangoroom.com/reservations/)** through OpenTable.
*   **Good to know:**Their dress code is “business casual.” You can often catch live jazz music here, and they also opened a back patio last year, which is open weather-permitting.

### Vault

_2017 E 9th St, Cleveland_

![Image 12: Vault cocktail bar old vault door](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Vault-1-800x600.jpg)

Vault is literally inside old vaults!

![Image 13: Drink at Vault cocktail bar](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Vault-2-450x600.jpg)

Drink at Vault

If it’s upscale you’re looking for, head to **Vault**inside the Metropolitan at the 9 hotel in downtown Cleveland. This swanky cocktail bar is located in old bank vaults (hence the name) beneath the Cleveland Trust Co Rotunda.

If you want to drink in a historic spot with lots of gilded details, it’s hard to beat this one. All the drinks here are hand-crafted, and most cost $20+.

*   **What to order:**There are about 20 drinks on the menu here, including local takes on all the classics. I like the Safety Deposit, and Elliot once tried the AZ85 (a bourbon cocktail), of which they only sell 10 per night. See the **[full Vault menu](https://www.vault9cle.com/menu)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:** They are only open Friday and Saturday nights, and they do not take reservations.
*   **Good to know:**You enter this one through the Metropolitan at the 9 hotel, and while there’s no published dress code, it IS a fancier place, and you’ll find most people in at least business casual wear.

### LBM

_12301 Madison Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 14: Cocktail at LBM](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/LBM-coktail-768x1024.jpg)

Punch-style cocktail at LBM

![Image 15: LBM metal Viking bar in Lakewood](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/LBM-bar-768x1024.jpg)

LBM bar

I would perhaps argue that **LBM** is just as much of a restaurant as a cocktail bar, but it identifies itself as a cocktail bar first, hence why it’s on this list! Located in Lakewood, LBM is a Viking-inspired bar with a self-described Norse aesthetic, loud metal music, and inventive cocktails.

I LOVE this spot, and often take visitors here for the unique vibe.

Most cocktails here cost $15.

*   **What to order:**They always have rotating seasonal cocktails alongside a list of classics (I usually like any of their punch-style drinks). See the **[current LBM drink menu](https://www.lbmbar.com/drinks/)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**LBM is open Monday-Saturday evenings, and they don’t take reservations unless you have a group of 6+.
*   **Good to know:**LBM also serves excellent food – their burger is probably my favorite burger in Cleveland!

### Western Reserve Distillers

_14221 Madison Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 16: Western Reserve Distillers patio](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/IMG_4122-800x600.jpg)

Outside Western Reserve Distillers

![Image 17: Western Reserve Distillers cocktail](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/IMG_4107-450x600.jpg)

WRD cocktail and tasting flight

**Western Reserve Distillers** is a family-owned organic craft distillery that was founded in 2014. The Lakewood distillery creates small-batch spirits, using grains from local Ohio farms. They have a bar and nice outdoor patio in the summer where you can try cocktails made from their award-winning spirits including vodka, gin, and bourbon.

Specialty cocktails here average around $14.

*   **What to order:**They have a really extensive menu of everything from margaritas to mojitos. They have a big Old Fashioneds (Elliot’s favorite), and I always like trying something off their seasonal menu. See the **[full Western Reserve Distillers menu](https://thedistilleryatwrd.com/lakewood-lakewood-western-reserve-distillers-food-menu)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**WRD is open Tuesday-Saturday evenings, plus for lunch on Friday and Saturday. You can **[make reservations online](https://tmt.spotapps.co/reservations?spot_id=83167&callback_url=http%3A%2F%2Fthedistilleryatwrd.com%2F&_gl=1%2a17pjn6w%2a_ga%2aMTEzMTAwNjYzNC4xNzQ3NDI1MzQy%2a_ga_VG24VK2VKT%2aczE3NDc0MjUzNDEkbzEkZzEkdDE3NDc0MjU2NzAkajAkbDAkaDA.%2a_ga_RLN3RJHM3K%2aczE3NDc0MjUzNDIkbzEkZzEkdDE3NDc0MjU2NzIkajAkbDAkaDA.&_ga=2.223970898.852016026.1747425342-1131006634.1747425342)** (but they aren’t generally required).
*   **Good to know:** Western Reserve Distillers also has a full restaurant, and hosts **[fun events](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/western-reserve-distillers-17383859126)** and cocktail classes.

### Bar 32

_100 Lakeside Ave E, Cleveland_

If it’s a fancy bar with a view you’re seeking, **Bar 32** is a good option.This cocktail bar is located on the 32nd floor of the Hilton Cleveland Downtown hotel, and has both indoor and outdoor seating with Lake Erie and Cleveland views.

*   **What to order:**There’s a smaller cocktail menu here, and it changes seasonally. Everything tends to be visually pretty as well as tasty. You can see the **[current Bar 32 menu](https://www.bar32cle.com/menu)** online.
*   **Hours and reservations:**Bar 32 is open Tuesday-Saturday evenings, and they do not accept reservations.
*   **Good to know:**The bar sometimes closes for private events, so double check online before you go.

### And more!

A few spots not included because I still need to visit them:

*   **Quintana’s Speakeasy –**_2200 S Taylor Rd, Cleveland Heights_ – “Hidden” upstairs from a local barbershop!
*   **The Whiskey Bar –**_2767 Euclid Heights Blvd, Cleveland Heights_ – A small, cozy bar with a huge whiskey selection.

* * *

## Restaurants that are also known for their cocktails

There are so many restaurants in Cleveland that also do great cocktails, but here are 3 that I go back to again and again.

### The Fairmount

_2448 Fairmount Blvd, Cleveland_

![Image 18: Cocktails on the Fairmount patio](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/IMG_0823-768x1024.jpg)

Fairmount patio cocktails

The Fairmount is a restaurant and bar serving upscale pub fare and a variety of cocktails on the east side. It has a cozy interior and a beautiful outdoor patio for enjoying the weather on a sunny afternoon. Menus here change seasonally, and they always have patio specials during the warmer months. **[See their menu here](https://www.thefairmount.net/menu)**.

### All Saints Public House

_1261 W 76th St, Cleveland_

![Image 19: All Saints Public House patio](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/IMG_8223-1024x768.jpg)

All Saints patio

Over in Detroit/Shoreway, All Saints Public House is a restaurant and bar with a full menu, cocktails, an outdoor patio (it has one of the **[best patios in Cleveland](https://clevelandtraveler.com/best-cleveland-patios/)**!), and frequent live music. They always have excellent seasonal cocktails – **[see their menu here](https://allsaintspublichouse.com/drinks/)**.

### Rood

_17001 Madison Ave, Lakewood_

![Image 20: Rood Food cocktails](https://clevelandtraveler.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/IMG_4143-450x600.jpg)

Cocktails at Rood

Known for its modern, inventive cuisine, Rood is a restaurant that turns into a “late night pie bar” after hours. You can enjoy craft cocktails throughout the day, plus fresh homemade pies for when you’re craving something sweet. **[See their current menu here](https://www.eatatrood.com/menu)**.

We are proud of our heritage, and thankful for the many accolades we’ve received during our tenure. ### Wine Excellence and   
Signature Cocktails

With a _Wine Spectator_ award-winning wine list, Johnny’s boasts a deeply curated cellar heavy on full-bodied Tuscan and Piedmontese reds, crisp Italian whites, and top-tier American vintages. Our mahogany bar serves up classic drinks with timeless flair—most notably our signature, ice-cold **Martinis** and stiff, expertly balanced **Old Fashioneds**, alongside refreshing guest favorites like their zesty **Moscow Mules.**

![Image 4: johnnys home sign2 300x300](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/johnnys-home-sign2-300x300-1.jpg)

### Cleveland's Original Speakeasy

For over 100 years, the **Santosuosso Family** has been a legacy the in Cleveland hospitality industry. The story of **Johnny’s Bar on Fulton** begins in 1924. With passage of the 19th amendment, the end of prohibition, and Elliot Ness liquor raids, the family’s grocery store is among the first establishments in the city licensed to sell liquor.

[Our Story](https://johnnysonfulton.com/about-johnnys-bar/)

![Image 5](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-on-fulton-cleveland-main-dining-room.jpg)

### Top Rated Local Dining

## Fulton Road and the West Side Bar Tradition

Cleveland's West Side has long maintained a bar culture that runs parallel to, and largely indifferent to, whatever is happening in the Flats or along East Fourth Street. The neighbourhood tavern model here is not a revival or a design concept; it is simply what survived. Johnny's Bar on Fulton, at 3164 Fulton Rd in the Old Brooklyn area, operates within that tradition. The address places it in a residential stretch where bars earn their regulars through consistency rather than programming, and where the room itself tends to communicate something before a single drink arrives.

Walking into a West Side neighbourhood bar of this type, the sensory register is immediate and legible: dim lighting calibrated to conversation rather than Instagram, a bar leading that has absorbed decades of evenings, and a crowd that already knows each other's orders. These are rooms built around familiarity, and Johnny's fits that description. The atmosphere is the product of time rather than design intent, which gives it a credibility that newer, concept-driven spaces on the East Side or in Ohio City spend considerable effort trying to manufacture.

## The Cocktail Programme in Context

Cleveland's cocktail scene has developed unevenly across the city's neighbourhoods. Downtown and Ohio City have attracted bars that invest in technical programmes, sourced spirits, and the kind of menu architecture you find at places like Acqua di Dea or [Blue Sky Brews](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/blue-sky-brews-cleveland-bar). The West Side neighbourhood bar operates in a different register entirely. Here, the cocktail programme, such as it is, tends to prioritise approachability and value over technique. Classic builds, spirit-forward pours, and beer-and-shot combinations dominate. This is not a limitation so much as a different set of values about what a bar is for.

That distinction matters when placing Johnny's within the broader Cleveland drinking map. The bar does not position itself against the craft cocktail tier occupied by the Velvet Tango Room, which has been Cleveland's most recognised standard-bearer for serious cocktail craft since the early 2000s. Johnny's operates on a different axis: the neighbourhood institution that measures quality in reliability and in the kind of crowd that returns weekly rather than occasionally. Compared to the programmatic bars covered in [our full Cleveland restaurants guide](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/cities/cleveland), Johnny's represents the category that most visitors overlook and most locals depend on.

Nationally, the gap between programme-driven bars and neighbourhood taverns has widened as the craft cocktail movement matured. Operations like [Kumiko in Chicago](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/kumiko), [Jewel of the South in New Orleans](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/jewel-of-the-south-new-orleans), and [Julep in Houston](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/julep-houston) have defined one end of the American bar spectrum, where technique, sourcing, and editorial intent drive every pour. [Bar Leather Apron in Honolulu](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/bar-leather-apron-honolulu), [ABV in San Francisco](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/abv), and [Superbueno in New York City](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/superbueno-new-york-city) each represent variations on that programme-led model, as does [The Parlour in Frankfurt](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/the-parlour-frankfurt-on-the-main) in the European context. Johnny's Bar on Fulton sits at the other end of that spectrum, where the value proposition is social continuity rather than craft distinction.

## Old Brooklyn as a Neighbourhood

Old Brooklyn is one of Cleveland's more stable residential neighbourhoods on the West Side, a stretch of modest housing stock, long-operating businesses, and a demographic mix that has shifted but retained working-class roots. The bar-to-resident ratio in Old Brooklyn reflects that history: these are establishments that serve the people who live within walking distance, not destination venues pulling from the metropolitan area. Johnny's on Fulton is embedded in that geography.

That neighbourhood context shapes the experience in practical ways. The crowd on a Friday evening will include people who have been coming for years, if not decades. New visitors will be immediately identifiable, which is not unwelcoming so much as accurate. Bars like this run on social memory, and the ideal way to engage with them is to understand you are entering someone else's regular spot rather than a public-facing hospitality venue designed to accommodate the uninitiated. The bar shares this character with venues like [Beachland Ballroom and Tavern](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/beachland-ballroom-tavern-cleveland-bar) and [Brewnuts](https://www.enprimeurclub.com/bars/brewnuts-cleveland-bar), each of which has a defined community relationship that precedes any editorial attention.

## The Legacy of Johnny's Bar:

## Over a Century of Cleveland History

For nearly a century, Johnny’s Bar on Fulton has redefined Cleveland’s culinary landscape. Tucked behind the unassuming facade of a classic westside neighborhood tavern lies an upscale, white-tablecloth Italian steakhouse steeped in prohibition-era history. Discover the perfect fusion of old-school grit and modern energy.

![Image 3](https://johnnysonfulton.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/johnnys-bar-patio-historic.jpeg)

### From Louise’s Garden to Post-Prohibition Speakeasy

The story about Johnny’s Bar is the story of Cleveland itself. Our footprint dates back to the 1920s with _Louise’s Garden_, a neighborhood anchor that transitioned seamlessly into the post-prohibition era. When the country dried up, the westside adapted—and when prohibition ended, Johnny’s secured one of the very first liquor licenses issued in the city of Cleveland.

### Four Generations of the Santosousso Family

Today, the Santosousso family honors a 100-year legacy. Spanning four generations, from great-grandmother Louise’s early founding vision to today, the family has maintained Johnny’s status as a leading fine dining establishment. We’ve preserved the historic soul of the building while injecting a fresh, sophisticated vibe and energy that keeps Johnny’s vibrant for a new generation of diners.

Step through our doors, however, and you are transported into a world of white-tablecloth elegance, impeccable service, and a sophisticated, high-end dining experience.

Adventures in dining Cleveland style

[![Image 1: Cleveland Rocks, Cleveland Eats](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/05/cropped-cropped-cleveland.jpg)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/ [link_0])

# The Velvet Tango Room

[![Image 2: vtr](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/vtr.jpg?w=225&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/vtr.jpg)The Velvet Tango Room (or VTR) was just named one of the ‘[Best 150 bars in America](link_1)‘ (hint: it’s no. 90) – and for good reason. I love the VTR. Proprietor Paulius Nasvytis is just coolness personified, and the bartenders there really know how to shake a cocktail. The VTR opened in 1996 in a building that was once a speakeasy. It is located on Columbus Road on Duck Island, just a block or two from the West Side Market and the RTA station in Ohio City.

There are more than 80 cocktails on the menu. They serve classics like Manhattans, the Flip, Tom Collins, Sazerac, the Highball, the Ramos Gin Fizz, the Old Fashioned, and sours like the Pisco Sour and the Amaretto di Saronna[![Image 3: IMAG1751](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1751.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1751.jpg) as well as their own house creations like the India Lime Fizz (which Michael Symon talked about on the Food Channel’s [The Best Thing I Ever Drank](link_2)), the Lady in White, the Apricot Lady, the Cleveland Rose, and the Rust Belt. There is a drink to match every taste and mood.Every cocktail is completely fresh and made from scratch. Each cocktail uses the finest ingredients, the juice is squeezed as they make your drink, and mixers like bitters are made in-house. The ice cubes are made in a special [![Image 4: 100_0395](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/100_0395.jpg?w=200&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/100_0395.jpg)machine to be 1.25″ square and are frozen at -30 degrees, so that they stay cold longer and dilute the cocktail less. The cherries are imported from Italy. Once you taste them you will never eat maraschino cherries again. They’re delicious!

My favorites include the Lady in Red (vodka blended with the Tango Room’s own red wine reduction and adorned with marinated grapes), the India Lime Fizz (a rich, creamy, and powerful cocktail that combines gin, rum, flora India limes, vanilla, and a whole egg), the Moscow Mule (in the metal cup of course), and the Pisco [![Image 5: mule](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/mule.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/mule.jpg)Sour.

Even if you are a hater of eggnog, their version will change your mind. It is the third drink photo here. It is so dense it casts a shadow on the cocktail napkin. Paulius whips it up during the holidays with fresh cream and eggs, brandy and dark rum. I had it during the holidays, when Paulius makes gallons of it and runs out, but they are happy to make it for you any time.

If [![Image 6: IMAG1753](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1753.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1753.jpg)you can’t decide they offer cocktail flights. As the menu explains, the “flights are groupings of three signature cocktails designed to create a harmonious progression of flavor experiences. Each cocktail’s flavor profile and finish, gently introduces and compliments the next one in the series. The opening cocktail is full-sized, followed by a slightly smaller tasting size cocktail before the final coup-de-grace, another full-size cocktail.” It’s a great way to try several at once. I’ve had the White, Light and Spicy (Lady in White, Rangpur Gimlet, and Dark ‘n’ Stormy) and the Fruits, Herbs and Spices (Lady in Red, Lady in White, and Bourbon Daisy).

The joint is classy [![Image 7: 1929284_89667701349_7751357_n](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/1929284_89667701349_7751357_n.jpg?w=300&h=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/1929284_89667701349_7751357_n.jpg)from start to finish, but it isn’t pretentious. There is a dress code (no shorts, t-shirts, or anything disreputable), but as you can see in the photo to the right they don’t ban jeans. The customers are friendly and not at all pretentious.

The ceiling has bullet holes from its speakeasy days. The bar and back bar are made of refinished mahogany. There is a sitting room with a grand piano where live jazz musicians play. The back room is tucked away in a hallway and to get to it you have to walk through a mirrored door in the coatroom. [![Image 8: lastword](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/lastword.jpg?w=225&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/lastword.jpg)You need reservations for the back room, and there is a two drink minimum. The backroom has buttery soft leather chairs and sofas and a fireplace for the winter months and a great patio for the summer months. There is another baby grand piano in the back room for special events. You can check out the [photos on their website](link_4).

The food is limited, but high quality. You can order savories like Warm Olives and Almonds, Speck on Rye (which I highly recommend), an Artisanal Cheese board, Swine and Cheese (local goat cheese with Courvoisier fig sauce [![Image 9: IMAG1598](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1598.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/imag1598.jpg)and a mound of prosciutto and crackers), or a Charcuterie plate or sweets like gelato, chocolate truffles, chocolate fondue, and Bananas Foster. We were lucky enough to be treated by Paulius to his Crepe Suzette, flambeed table side. It was a treat for the eyes and the taste buds.

There is no other place in Cleveland serving fine cocktails like the VTR. They serve cocktails and only cocktails, so check out the menu before you go to make sure you like what they are selling. There is no beer, shots or wine served here. The drinks are pricey ($18 for one drink), but they are only $10 during Happy Hour. The Happy Hour at the VTR runs from 4:30-7 pm on weeknights (my friends usually meet there on Fridays). There are no reservations in the front. It’s first come, first served. There are sometimes free nibbles put out during happy hour, but don’t count on them. As one Yelper said, “It doesn’t have to be a “special occasion” for a stop at VTR. VTR is its own occasion and can make any day better.”[![Image 10: collage-2015-05-01](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/collage-2015-05-01.jpg?w=300&h=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/collage-2015-05-01.jpg)

# Where I Hang: Paulius Nasvytis, Owner of the Velvet Tango Room

![Image 3](link_51)[Jason Beudert](link_52)April 2, 2014 July 28, 2025

### Share this:

*   [Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window)Email](mailto:?subject=%5BShared%20Post%5D%20Where%20I%20Hang%3A%20Paulius%20Nasvytis%2C%20Owner%20of%20the%20Velvet%20Tango%20Room&body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.clevescene.com%2Fnews%2Fwhere-i-hang-paulius-nasvytis-owner-of-the-velvet-tango-room-4172887%2F&share=email&nb=1)

*   [Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window)Bluesky](https://www.clevescene.com/news/where-i-hang-paulius-nasvytis-owner-of-the-velvet-tango-room-4172887/)

![Image 4: Picture_7.png](https://i0.wp.com/media2.fdncms.com/clevescene/imager/where-i-hang-paulius-nasvytis-owner-of-the-velvet-tango-room/u/original/4173158/1396474329-picture_7.png?resize=225%2C229&ssl=1)

When he’s not hanging around the Velvet Tango Room, the quintessential craft cocktail bar he created over 17 years ago, VTR’s master of ceremonies Paulius Navytis stays close to home.

“I have lived in the Warehouse District for ten years now,” he says. “I love living downtown. It has really blossomed into a real neighborhood.”

“The Greenhouse Tavern is one of my favorites. Chef Jonathan Sawyer has a passion for food that really shows,” he says. And when it comes to sushi, Nasvytis says nobody does it like Ginko. “There are no comparisons anywhere” he says.

The West Side Market’s famed Frank’s Bratwurst also makes the short list. “I can eat their brats for breakfast, lunch and dinner — all on the same day.”

When he does leave downtown, Americano in Bratenahl is his choice. “Vytauras Sasnauskas is one of Cleveland’s most unknown and truly passionate and talented chefs.” And for those other times when a trip out of downtown is not in order and he simply wants to walk somewhere for a bite and a drink, it’s usually to the Map Room. “The beer is always cold, they make a legit pizza and they have sauerkraut balls, which should be a staple in Cleveland bars and restaurants,” he says.

We agree.

## [In Memorium: Walter Hyde](link_1)

It’s been a month. I thought I was ready. I wasn’t. I promised his sister I would post this memorial video though. We miss you, Walter.

[https://jill-sommer.com/Walter.mp4](link_2)

The Cleveland food scene and its close-knit chefs suffered a major loss on October 16th. Walter Hyde of Now We’re Cooking, Swingo’s, Giovanni’s, The Annex, Fat Casual BBQ, Tavern of Solon, Fahrenheit-Charlotte, Sterle’s and most recently [Ice Ice] Daisy’s on Fleet died of a heart attack after a smoked prime rib pop-up with Penny Barend Tagliarina at Terrestrial Brewery. We are all reeling from the loss. His creativity was boundless. Who else could turn a cheese ball into a legendary appetizer? He and Scott could roast a delicious pig. His smoked prime rib and kind heart made him a legend. Everything he touched was delicious. [Walter Hyde](https://www.facebook.com/groups/586823648119308/user/1525133440/?__cft__[0 [link_3]]=AZW_B4J1Exry5XaZUNmFkQMDoEmcDHJBP09nG49eZ6apKQesUekDB3C0lx4uYNiRJ--eVkz8Uj0jLG0D7ap8-yFXIuFFdXVrS6wEl47rTpgynPlIcu3I8flRWleWxqwbN5iiGFnQd2fXKKIfF3-Mufcn&__tn__=-]K-R), you will be missed. I’m heartbroken.

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/imag3494.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/imag3494.jpg)

Jeff Jarrett and Walter at Dinner in the Dark at Sterle’s

Legendary appetizer by Walter Hyde – cheeseballs, BBQ and pickle

## [Sourwood Public House to Open in Former Deagan’s Kitchen Spot in Lakewood](link_49)

 “It’s Southern but with global influences,” says Leo Hines. “We’re taking the Southern cuisine that you think about and kind of twisting it into something different.” 

![Image 4: Avatar photo](https://www.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/cropped-doug-at-never-say-dive-scaled-1-80x80.jpg)by[Douglas Trattner](link_50)[October 5, 2026 October 5, 2026](link_49)

Posted in[Food & Drink](https://www.clevescene.com/category/food-drink/)
## [First Look: Olive Room Now Open at Intro in Ohio City](link_51)

 “It has always been more of an extension of Jaja and now it’s a completely different bar experience.” 

![Image 6: Avatar photo](https://www.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/cropped-doug-at-never-say-dive-scaled-1-80x80.jpg)by[Douglas Trattner](link_50)[October 2, 2026 October 2, 2026](link_51)

## [Sazani Oceana in Shaker Square to Close After This Weekend](link_52)

 “Unfortunately, the current economic realities of operating a restaurant made continuing unsustainable.” 

![Image 8: Avatar photo](https://www.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/IMG_2865.jpg-80x80.jpg)by[Vince Grzegorek](link_53)[October 2, 2026 October 2, 2026](link_52)

# In Memoriam

[![Image 2: in-memoriam](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam.jpg?w=300&h=161)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam.jpg)

This page is the home for my posts about restaurants that have closed.

* [Carrie Cerino’s](link_1) shut pages its doors after 57 years. They have definitely earned their retirement!

* I’m crushed about this closure. Amanda and Josh, the owners of [Lilly Handmade Chocolates](link_2), announced they had taken jobs with a CBD chocolate shop and were not reopening after the Christmas break. I will miss the delicious chocolate and amazing beer, wine and cocktail and chocolate pairings.

* Michael Symon’s brother-in-law Michael Herschman closed [Lopez](link_3) on New Year’s Day and is reopening as Mojo World Eats & Drink, his “Asian-inspired tapas bistro” that shut down in 2003. It’s the end of an era for this institution that was created by Rick Bayliss. It went through several transitions, but this is a huge one, going from Mexican to Asian.

* I was very sad to hear about the closure of [Polpetta](link_4), Adam Bostwick’s creative outlet. We had just been there for their Christmas Dinner in early December, and it was delightful. I hope Adam lands on his feet, and I will be sure to follow. I like his quirky humorous plays on food.

* [Hodge’s](link_5) closed in October 2019. The closing is a result of the Driftwood Group (Scott Kuhn and Chris Hodgson) wanting to keep their focus on Playhouse Square locations.

* Beloved Czech restaurant [Marta’s](link_6) closed at the end of September 2019 when Marta decided to retire. I got to go one last time, but was unable to order my favorite dish. Now there is nowhere in Cleveland to enjoy authentic Czech bread dumplings. But I wish her well and hope she enjoys her well-earned retirement. Her regulars will miss her.

* [Jack Flaps](link_7) closed suddenly in July 2019. Business had started to falter, so it wasn’t all that much of a surprise. I am really going to miss the Breakfast Bahn Mi.

* [Sterle’s Slovenian Country House](link_8) closed with a whimper after 60 years in business. They claimed they weren’t closing and would be available for large groups and events, but that is the last we’ve heard from them and the chef Natasha Pogrebinsky started selling fried chicken at The South Side in Tremont.

* [Zoss the Swiss Baker](link_9) closed on March 31, 2019. I am going to miss the Apfel im Schlafrock, the Palmiers, the Semmli, the Bretzel, the ham and cheese croissants and the Nussecken. Sounds like I will miss every single thing they made. He’s landed at EDWINS Bakery, teaching the culinary students there his magical ways, so things haven’t died with the closure of the bakery.

* [Akira Hibachi](link_10) in Solon closed its doors on February 2, 2019. Anna decided to retire. This was my go-to restaurant when I lived in Solon. I was there at least once a week. I am sad. They had the best Iidako (baby octopus) nigiri.

* I wrote about [Koko Cafe](link_11) and it closed quietly around that same time. Koko Bakery is still open though.

Advertisement

* [Brasa Grill Steakhouse](link_12) closed its doors in November 2018. I will miss those delicious skewers of meat and amazing salad bar.

* [Trentina](link_13) closed its doors in January 2019. I have mixed feelings about it. It was nice for a splurge, but it was so super loud with bad acoustics that I just wasn’t motivated to return.

* The [Happy Dog at the Euclid Tavern](link_14) closed in November 2018. The Happy Dog on Detroit is still open.

*   [Noodlecat](link_15) in all its forms has closed – downtown closed first, it moved to Crocker Park and opened up a stand in the West Side Market, and now both Crocker Park and the WSM locations are closed.

* The Hot Sauce Williams location on Carnegie closed, but the Lee Road and Superior Road locations are still open for business. (The one on Superior is now called Hot Sauce Legacy BBQ).

* It was a dark day for me when [Coquette Patisserie](link_16) closed its doors. Britt got a full-time job and they shuttered the place. I miss it terribly.

* [Dan’s Dogs](link_17) in Medina closed, then reopened, and now it is closed once again.

* [Cork & Cleaver Social Kitchen](link_18) closed so that Brian and Adam could focus on their new baby, Polpetta, which they hope to spin into a meatball-themed chain.

* [Graffiti: A Social Kitchen](link_19) closed in October 2017. They wanted to focus on their meatball idea, Polpetta.

* [Noodlecat](link_15) is still at Crocker Park, but it isn’t the downtown location that is featured here.

* [Ribsticks](link_20) on Cedar Road closed within less than a year. I will miss their delicious sides. Those Bourbon peaches were amazing!!

* [Santorini Greek Taverne](link_21) on W. 9th has closed.

* [Crop Kitchen](link_22) has unfortunately closed in 7/2016. The location is rather unfortunate with no street presence and no sign allowed.

* I just learned [Heimatland](link_23) closed. One less German restaurant in the Cleveland area. That’s sad.

* [Il Bacio](link_24) in Little Italy is now Nora. The owner of Il Bacio moved back to Sicily.

* The [Grovewood Tavern](link_25) announced it was closing, effective immediately, on August 10, 2015. Some of my most memorable meals ever were here. Their Mad Men Spirit Dinner will forever live in my memory as one of the greatest meals I’ve ever had. I am really going to miss this place. It was magical.

* [Chop It Salad Co.](link_26) closed on May 1, 2015. I will miss my go-to salad place.

* [Jezebel’s Bayou](link_27) has changed its format and is no longer serving New Orleans fare. If you need a fix try [Baptiste & Dupree Cajun Grill](link_28) or [Bourbon Street Barrel Room](link_29).

* Of all the restaurants that have closed in the past I am most gutted about the [Saigon Grille](link_30). They closed in June 2014 to go on holiday for a month and never reopened. I tried to go in late July and there was a boat blocking the door. I drove by today, on October 14th, 2014, and a nail salon has moved into the space. I went here very regularly for lunch and will miss their amazing grilled pork bahn mi. You are gone, but you are certainly not forgotten by me, Saigon Grille.

Advertisement

* [The Katz Club Diner](link_31) closed due to arson. Doug plans to continue to use the kitchen there for catering, but I’m afraid they won’t be reopening as a full-service brick and mortar restaurant. I will miss the bar car and cherish my memories of the diner!

* After more than two decades of attracting an endless stream of loyal customers and a procession of celebrities and power brokers, John Q’s Steakhouse served its last meal on June 15, 2013.

[![Image 3: IMG_20130530_192631](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20130530_192631.jpg?w=300&h=224)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20130530_192631.jpg)

* [Babushka’s Kitchen](link_32) has closed. Where will I find awesome kolatschke and their numerous kinds of pierogi now?

* [Mekong River](link_33) appears to have shut its doors (as of at least 10/2/2013), and a sign is heralding the coming of “Lotus Thai House.” I will miss the tangerine tilapia.

* [Charkha](link_34) has closed. I will miss the affordable lunch buffet.

* [Accent](link_35) closed. The location did not pan out as promised, and it never really attracted the crowds. It’s a shame. They had a unique idea. I for one will miss the smoked turkey wing. Crop Kitchen is a welcome addition at that location and have inherited the Robata Grill and Josper Oven.

* [Fat Casual BBQ](link_36) in Macedonia has closed and lovers of their Smoked Prime Rib will mourn the loss.

* Le Oui Oui Cafe closed when the owners of Luchita Express on Euclid skipped out in the middle of the night (Denajua shared the space with them). The chicken chutney crepe was fantastic, but the chocolate mousse knocked my socks off! We miss you, Denajua!

| [![Image 4: IMG_20110331_124121](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110331_124121.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110331_124121.jpg) | [![Image 5: IMG_20110331_125830](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110331_125830.jpg?w=300&h=224)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110331_125830.jpg) |
| --- | --- |

* [Istanbul Grill](link_37) abruptly shut its doors in February. The restaurant reopened as [Dervish Grill](link_38) in late March and will continue to serve Turkish fare.

* [Carnegie Kitchen and Dining](link_39) closed, and I will miss their PB&J French toast.

* [Frank & Pauly’s](link_40) in Mentor closed because the owner wanted to retire.

* [Henry’s at the Barn in Avon](link_41) was a personal favorite and I miss it.

Advertisement

* Melange had an awesome goat cheese fondue

[![Image 6: IMG_20110719_163332](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110719_163332.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110719_163332.jpg)

* [Palookaville Chili](link_42) closed for the summer in June 2013 and the owner decided not to reopen it on September 1. It will be missed. It’s now Jack Flaps.

* [Romanini’s](link_43) in Aurora had a really nice patio but terrible parking.

* Viva Fernando had the most amazing paella

[![Image 7: IMG_20110705_201415](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110705_201415.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/img_20110705_201415.jpg)

## [In Memorium: Walter Hyde](link_1)

It’s been a month. I thought I was ready. I wasn’t. I promised his sister I would post this memorial video though. We miss you, Walter.

[https://jill-sommer.com/Walter.mp4](link_2)

The Cleveland food scene and its close-knit chefs suffered a major loss on October 16th. Walter Hyde of Now We’re Cooking, Swingo’s, Giovanni’s, The Annex, Fat Casual BBQ, Tavern of Solon, Fahrenheit-Charlotte, Sterle’s and most recently [Ice Ice] Daisy’s on Fleet died of a heart attack after a smoked prime rib pop-up with Penny Barend Tagliarina at Terrestrial Brewery. We are all reeling from the loss. His creativity was boundless. Who else could turn a cheese ball into a legendary appetizer? He and Scott could roast a delicious pig. His smoked prime rib and kind heart made him a legend. Everything he touched was delicious. [Walter Hyde](https://www.facebook.com/groups/586823648119308/user/1525133440/?__cft__[0 [link_3]]=AZW_B4J1Exry5XaZUNmFkQMDoEmcDHJBP09nG49eZ6apKQesUekDB3C0lx4uYNiRJ--eVkz8Uj0jLG0D7ap8-yFXIuFFdXVrS6wEl47rTpgynPlIcu3I8flRWleWxqwbN5iiGFnQd2fXKKIfF3-Mufcn&__tn__=-]K-R), you will be missed. I’m heartbroken.

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/imag3494.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/imag3494.jpg)

Jeff Jarrett and Walter at Dinner in the Dark at Sterle’s

## [DiCillo Tavern – Fish Fry Friday #1 2021](link_7)

![Image 6: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/capture.jpg?w=400)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/capture.jpg)

  
From Google StreetView

After finishing my invoicing for the month I was ready for a fish fry last night. I referred to my shortlist, and the first on the list was also one of the closest to me. DiCillo Tavern is located on Mayfield Road in Mayfield, close to Golden Gate. It sticks out in the sea of strip malls because it is an old house. It’s got this good quality hole in the wall vibe going for it. In fact, it reminds me of the old Suds MacGuire in Olmsted Falls – an old house that was a dive bar/restaurant and had killer fish fries. DiCillo has been serving their famous “Whaler” fish fry dinner since 1933. The fish fry is take-out only this year, daily from 4 to 8 p.m.

[![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_175514-1.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_175514-1.jpg)

I headed out shortly after 5 and arrived there at 5:45. I had tried to call in my order, but no one answered the phone. The parking lot was packed with big trucks. I got one of the last easy-to-access parking spaces (the trucks were not parked straight so there were gaps). I was surprised to see so many vehicles and expected a long wait. I was pleased to see the bar side was packed with patrons (no masks as far as I could see, but they were in a separate room), while the restaurant side was hopping with take-out pick-ups. I placed my order and was told it would be about a half an hour. I had planned to sit in my car, but I was told I could sit in the socially distanced restaurant area while I waited. By the time my order was ready I was not the only person sitting around the restaurant, but we were all masked and sitting at tables divided with plexi-glass.

[![Image 9](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184356-1.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184356-1.jpg)

I was surprised when my order was only $24. I had ordered the Fisherman’s Sampler ($18), which contained a “mini” Whaler, a couple pieces of perch, and a couple fried shrimp. I ordered the pierogi as a side dish ($6) and the clam chowder ($6). She had added the pierogi as my side, so I didn’t pay extra for them. I slipped her a couple bucks as a tip and was on my way home. I had to play parking Jenga to leave because two cars had blocked the exit row and two other cars were parked along the side with their flashers on.

[![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184803.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184803.jpg)

As to the fish fry itself, it was delicious. The only down side was the pierogi, which I would not be surprised were Mrs. T’s. Luckily I didn’t end up paying extra for them. The clam chowder had a thicker consistency than most milk-based chowders and it was chock full of clams and potatoes. I think the consistency might have come from the potatoes breaking down. I really enjoyed it.

![Image 11](https://photos.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/DiCillo-Tavern-Fish-Fry.jpg)

The Whaler – from the DiCillo Tavern Facebook page

The fried fish and shrimp were delicious. Perfectly fried and overcooked or dry. I can see why the Whaler is so popular because that particular piece of fish is stunning. It is a large portion with firm white meat inside. The perch were okay. They were flatter and consistent, which leads me to believe they are frozen, not fresh. But perch is perch and adored by many here in Cleveland. I also adored the coleslaw. It had a nice horseradish bite to it and was really creamy. If I go back again (and let’s be honest, I just might) I’ll order a Whaler and a huge side of coleslaw. If you are on the east side, you can’t go wrong with DiCillo’s. But order early. They ran out of chowder at 6:30.

**Contact Info:**

DiCillo Tavern  
6088 Mayfield Road  
Mayfield Heights, OH 44124  
(440) 442-2755

## [Polpetta](link_10)

![Image 13: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[![Image 14](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/o.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/o.jpg)Polpetta is the brain child of restauranteurs Brian Okin and Adam Bostwick of Cork & Cleaver and Graffiti: A Social Kitchen fame. I have had some amazing meals from these two chefs. They closed the two popular restaurants to focus on the Polpetta concept, which relies heavily on the theme of “balls.” The decor is heavy on old meat grinders, which are used as the door handle and light fixtures, and artwork with cleverly-hidden balls in them.[![Image 15](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_181541.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_181541.jpg)

They launched the Polpetta concept at Porco when Walter Hyde was cooking in the tiny kitchen there. That was where I had my first taste of Sunday Supper, which I personally think is the best spaghetti and meatballs I have had in Cleveland. Usually restaurant spaghetti and meatballs are bland, but the meatballs here are well-seasoned and paired with a herbaceous pomodoro red sauce. The pasta was al dente and easy to twirl. When I told my server that I think they are the best spaghetti and meatballs in Cleveland he told me about a woman from Little Italy who came in and was vocally critical of everything, but once she had the Sunday Supper she was quiet and said she would be back. He said she’s been back at least seven times. I agree, Nonna.

[![Image 16](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/imag0597.jpg?w=169)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/imag0597.jpg)

Porco version[![Image 17](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160342.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160342.jpg)

Polpetta version

[![Image 18](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/20181120_191131.jpg?w=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/20181120_191131.jpg)Once they opened their restaurant on Detroit Road in Rocky River it was on my list of places to try, but it took a while to make my way over there. I finally met a group of friends there for a nice meal, and that night I accidentally ordered what I think is the best thing on the menu, the Spinach and Meatball Dip. It features mini-meatballs in a spinach-parmesan-roasted tomatoes bechamel sauce and fun little pita dippers. This dip is Chef Adam at his best. It is rich and lush, and I could have eaten the whole thing by myself and regretted it. Everyone at the table adored it, and we practically licked the serving plate clean.

[![Image 19](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_194803.jpg?w=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_194803.jpg)I was less impressed by my entree choice that evening. I ordered The Adam, which features chicken meatballs, Thai peanut sauce, and fried rice. I love Adam’s fried rice, which I first enjoyed as spam fried rice at a pop-up at Toast several years ago. It was then included on the menu at Graffiti, and I happily ordered it several times. Unfortunately the Thai peanut sauce was too bitter that night. I was expecting a nice, creamy Thai peanut sauce, and I think it had too much hot sauce in it that night. My friend Nancy loves his Thai peanut sauce, so apparently it was an anomaly. Luckily I had eaten a ton of the appetizer, so I didn’t go away hungry. But I knew they could do better based on past experience.

[![Image 20](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160333.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160333.jpg)I left wishing I had ordered the Grandma Bos, which is a chicken paprikash featuring chicken meatballs, paprikash sauce, and herbed spaetzle. When I ordered it the server asked if I wanted sour cream on top. Yes, please. This was a satisfying dish. The chicken meatballs were nicely seasoned, albeit a little denser than I had hoped. Overall the meatballs here are very dense, but at least they won’t fall apart. The herbed spaetzle are not the traditional (i.e., bland) German spätzle I am used to, but I liked the herb flavor profile and the pan-fried crispiness held up well against the paprikash sauce. I would order this again and again.![Image 21](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20181120_230714.jpg?w=170)If you like paprikash you will like this dish.

I ordered the Cereal Balls for dessert, which are made from several different cereals molded into rice krispie-like balls served with milk panna cotta and fresh berries and bananas. I first enjoyed Adam’s panna cotta at a grill evening on the Graffiti patio, so I was looking forward to that magic being recreated. He used cereal milk for that one, but the Polpetta panna cotta just uses milk so it was not as magical – even though it was tasty.

[![Image 22](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_211820.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_211820.jpg)

The OG Fat Kid

If you want a dessert that will bowl you over, order the Fat Kid 3.0, which features fried cookie dough balls, ice cream, chips, candy and fun. I got to taste the OG Fat Kid at a Graffiti Throw Back dinner at Polpetta a couple of months ago. That one was outrageously good and featured french fries, which was a fun pairing with the ice cream and chocolate and nerds. It is definitely a dessert to share though.

[![Image 23](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_193254.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_193254.jpg)

### Contact info:

 19900 Detroit Road  
 Rocky River, OH 44116  
 (216) 860-4474

## [Koko Cafe](link_12)

![Image 25: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png)  
[![Image 26](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/o.jpg?w=288)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/o.jpg)Alas, Koko Cafe has closed. We hardly knew ye. Koko Bakery is still open.

I have been a big fan of Koko Bakery on Payne Avenue for a while now. I would go there for their multitude of hot and room temperature savory and sweet buns (and to buy frozen steam buns to make at home), bubble tea, smoothies, shaved ice, and gorgeous desserts, but never really got around to ordering their hot entrees, which seemed like an afterthought in the small place with maybe 9 tables in the place. When the news broke that they were expanding next door to offer hot food in a larger sit-down restaurant that seats 40 I was excited.

The first time I went to check it out shortly after it opened I was supposed to meet a friend [![Image 27](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131906.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131906.jpg)who forgot, so I ordered some dumplings and an entree to enjoy by myself. I loved the dumplings and wasn’t too excited by the entree. I love the dumplings so much that I keep ordering them. I was intrigued by the idea of pork and leek, and I really enjoy the combination so I keep ordering it. I prefer dumplings pan-fried over steamed, because I like a bit of [![Image 28](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132155.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132155.jpg)toothsome bite to them. My entree that day was the Triple Mushrooms with Chicken. On paper it sounds awesome, and it would be without the American-style frozen vegetables they use. I was extremely off-put by the corn kernels, peas and carrots of it all. I am not used to Asian food with vegetables I grew up eating in TV dinners.

[![Image 29](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132345.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132345.jpg)[![Image 30](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/koko.jpg?w=225)](

The Witch Doctor opens soon

Matt Luebbert and brothers Charlie and Michael Eby have been working on the [Witch Doctor](https://www.instagram.com/witchdoctorcle/?hl=en) (3314 Broadview Rd.) space in Old Brooklyn for two years since purchasing the building on Broadview Rd.

“It was time well spent,” says Charlie. “We do very much like where it is now.”

The result of those labors is a cocktail lounge like no other, which guests can begin enjoying when it opens on Sept. 2. What the owners casually describe as a “botanically-themed bar” is, in fact, a serious bar program that blends meticulously formulated ingredients into one-of-a-kind concoctions and dispenses them in a whimsical, comfortable lair.

Luebbert, a member of the US Bartenders’ Guild and former bar manager at Rood in Lakewood, prepares a dizzying variety of tinctures, infusions, syrups, cordials, bitters and spirits from a wide assortment of botanicals that he purchases from local apothecaries.

“Once I started making things by hand, I started making dang near everything by hand,” he explains. “That evolved into making vermouths and compound cordials and bitters.”

Whereas another bartender might reach for a bottle of high-quality grenadine, Luebbert crafts his own from fresh pomegranate. Same goes for the orgeat syrup, Herring-style cherry cordial, curacao and sweet vermouth. The Witch Doctor even has its own versions of gin, rum, tequila and vodka. Each functional cocktail is said to aid some facet of wellness, such as reducing stress, boosting immunity, aiding digestion, fighting inflammation or a combination thereof.

“We want things to taste good, cocktails that everyone can enjoy and that are drinkable,” says Luebbert. “But something that will be different from what you normally find. We want things to be a little weird and different. You can get Maker’s Mark, Jim Beam and stuff like that anywhere. I want people to come here and try new things.”

“A little weird and different” is an apt description for the venue as well. Guests seated at the bar will spy an apothecary’s cupboard stocked with dried plants, herbs, roots and spices. Just past the barroom, the space opens into a cavernous cathedral-like area that feels like a Norse drinking hall. A third room is imbued with a warm and cozy glow from newly installed stained-glass windows and is appointed with graceful Rococo-style furniture.

“I’d describe it as mystical, cabin-in-the-woods with medieval tavern vibes,” says Luebbert.

“Or if you stumbled out of the bayou in New Orleans,” adds Charlie.

# Koko Cafe

![Image 2: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png?w=840)  
[![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/o.jpg?w=288&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/o.jpg)Alas, Koko Cafe has closed. We hardly knew ye. Koko Bakery is still open.

I have been a big fan of Koko Bakery on Payne Avenue for a while now. I would go there for their multitude of hot and room temperature savory and sweet buns (and to buy frozen steam buns to make at home), bubble tea, smoothies, shaved ice, and gorgeous desserts, but never really got around to ordering their hot entrees, which seemed like an afterthought in the small place with maybe 9 tables in the place. When the news broke that they were expanding next door to offer hot food in a larger sit-down restaurant that seats 40 I was excited.

The first time I went to check it out shortly after it opened I was supposed to meet a friend [![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131906.jpg?w=300&h=170)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131906.jpg)who forgot, so I ordered some dumplings and an entree to enjoy by myself. I loved the dumplings and wasn’t too excited by the entree. I love the dumplings so much that I keep ordering them. I was intrigued by the idea of pork and leek, and I really enjoy the combination so I keep ordering it. I prefer dumplings pan-fried over steamed, because I like a bit of [![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132155.jpg?w=300&h=170)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132155.jpg)toothsome bite to them. My entree that day was the Triple Mushrooms with Chicken. On paper it sounds awesome, and it would be without the American-style frozen vegetables they use. I was extremely off-put by the corn kernels, peas and carrots of it all. I am not used to Asian food with vegetables I grew up eating in TV dinners.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132345.jpg?w=364&h=206)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_132345.jpg)[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/koko.jpg?w=225&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/koko.jpg)

I then organized a dinner for my foodie friends, which allowed me to try a lot more from the menu. Needless to say I am now a fan.

They offer some interesting dim sum options, such as rice noodle rolls and steam buns. I am not a fan of rice noodle rolls. You either really like them or really dislike them. I don’t like the texture and find them bland; however, my friends who are huge fans of rice noodle rolls raved about them. They tried the shrimp and the dried radish rice noodle rolls and enjoyed them a lot.

[![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_185614.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_185614.jpg)

Dried radish rice roll noodles[![Image 9](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190238.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190238.jpg)

Cucumbers with chili sauce is always a must
[![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190235.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190235.jpg)

Shrimp rice roll noodles[![Image 11](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190408.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_190408.jpg)

Steam buns

Advertisement

That was the day I ordered what has become my favorite dish there – the Singaporean Style Fried Vermicelli. It has a nice curry flavor that is not overpowering, and the vermicelli is a great consistency. They have a wide range of fried noodle and fried rice dishes on the menu that go beyond the usual chicken and shrimp offerings – including a Barbecue Pork Fried Rice, which sounds intriguing. If you like salted fish there is a Salted Fish & Chicken Fried Rice as well.

[![Image 12](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130850.jpg?w=300&h=170)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130850.jpg)

Koko Bakery is especially known for its bubble tea, so I suggested my Meetup tea group meet at the Cafe for bubble tea and a meal. Bubble tea is a Taiwanese tea-based drink invented in the 1980s. Recipes contain tea of some kind, flavors (milk and non-milk, fruit and non-fruit) and sugar. Toppings, such as chewy tapioca balls, popping boba, fruit jelly, grass jelly, agar jelly, and puddings are often added.

[![Image 13](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_184110.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_184110.jpg)

Thai Iced Tea Bubble Tea[![Image 14](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131001.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180718_131001.jpg)

Iced Hong Kong Milk Tea
[![Image 15](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130157.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130157.jpg)

My go-to bubble tea is melon with fruit jellies instead of boba[![Image 16](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_184118.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180809_184118.jpg)

This might be mango – I love the contrast of black boba and yellow tea

Advertisement

We had a range of diners – from a very picky/non-Asian food fan to someone with some major dietary issues/needs. Both were happy with their choices. The picky eater ordered the Sesame Chicken and was very pleased with it. She raved about how moist and flavorful the chicken was. She shared a bite with me, and I liked it so much I ordered it the next time I went. The vegan/no-oil diner ordered a soup and was absolutely thrilled with the quality and the variety of vegetables in the soup. Everyone else enjoyed their meals as well. I just didn’t know them well enough to ask to photograph their food :-).

[![Image 17](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_131144.jpg?w=170&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_131144.jpg)

Special order vegetable soup – no noodles, no oil[![Image 18](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130939.jpg?w=349&h=198)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/img_20180901_130939.jpg)

Sesame chicken

They have a great online ordering system as well. I was craving several different entrees at once one night, so I ordered online and drove to pick it up. My meal was waiting for me as I walked in, and I was able to turn around and drive home. Most gratifying was the fact that nothing had been left out – including all the accoutrements that I had specified they could leave out when I ordered it (soy, mustard and duck sauce packets for the egg rolls).

Koko Cafe is a welcome addition to the Asia Town neighborhood. There is something here for everyone – from basic Chinese-American dishes to more intriguing choices we haven’t seen anywhere else. It is also super-affordable. The soups, congees and dumplings are all around $8, the rice noodle rolls are $3, steam buns are $3.50, and most entrees range between $10-13.

I just wish someone would create a separate Yelp page for the Cafe, because the cafe reviews/photos co-mingle with the bakery.

# [Cleveland Rocks, Cleveland Eats](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/)

Adventures in dining Cleveland style

[![Image 1: Cleveland Rocks, Cleveland Eats](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/05/cropped-cropped-cleveland.jpg)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/)

## [Captain Tony’s Pizza &Pasta](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/10/02/captain-tonys-pizza-pasta/)

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg)

I have been aware of Captain Tony’s Pizza & Pasta since I moved to the Heights 16 years ago, and I’m frankly irritated I haven’t tried it until now. We have a dearth of decent pizza places. Yes, we have Vero and Pizza Bogo, but there aren’t a lot of decent delivery spots. I usually drive to Lyndhurst to get a pizza from Jet’s. It’s not life-changing pizza, but it definitely hits the spot and is better than, say, Domino’s or Pizza Hut.

I was stuck at home on an all-day Zoom call for 3 days, so was unable to go to the grocery store. When I have these classes I usually order something through DoorDash and make the order large enough to eat over several days. My go-to is usually Chinese, but I was in the mood for pizza and checked to see what my choices were in my area. Captain Tony’s is located on Shaker Square (the southeast corner), so it is close enough to pop in and pick up an order if I wasn’t stuck at home. When I saw some of their unique offerings I decided to give it a try. It is apparently a small chain based out of Rochester, NY that started expanding in 1985, but it is the only location in Ohio. There is even one in London and Dubai, but, again, it is still a very small chain with only a couple of locations. Can it even be considered a chain if it’s the only location in Ohio?

The first pizza that caught my eye was the seafood pizza. It features a white garlic sauce that is topped with crabmeat, mozzarella, Romano, and cheddar cheese. I have to say I am so hooked I’ve ordered it several times now. It just hits the spot and the white garlic sauce is delicious paired with the crabmeat and cheeses. It also reheats really well in the air fryer.

[![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg)

My go to at any pizza place is a supreme, and the Captain’s Classic fits the bill perfectly. It is topped with pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, green peppers, onion, and cheese. If a pizza place does a supreme well, I know that their pizzas are good. They are generous with the toppings, and I was impressed to see that the mushroom were actual fresh mushrooms.

[![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg)

The Honey Mustard Chicken pizza also caught my eye because I love honey mustard, but I wasn’t as impressed with that one compared to the other two pizzas. It just tasted a little lackluster. Maybe I was expecting more honey mustard, but it was just ok.

[![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg)

Since I’m on my meatball sub quest I had to order the meatball sub. Huge fail. Not only were the meatballs tiny, but they were overwhelmed by the bread and didn’t have enough sauce or cheese. In fact, their buns are kind of lackluster but are used for their gourmet garlic bread (essentially garlic bread with cheese and a fresh tomato slice and a small container of marinara to dip it in) and regular garlic bread. Snore. It’s a huge pass for me. I also suspect the meatballs were of the frozen variety because they were pretty tasteless. Huge pass.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg)

I found out about the garlic bread when I ordered the lasagna. The lasagna was delicious, and the serving size was great (especially for the price). I enjoyed it over two days.
