## [Amici Restaurant and Lounge](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/09/18/amici-restaurant-and-lounge/)

[![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_164840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_164840.jpg)

I’ve become a fan of Amici’s pop-up bars. I first heard about it with their Christmas bar. Amici is an Italian restaurant on the Strongsville/North Royalton border. They have great Italian food, which is available in the restaurant as well as their bar in their Event Center next door (entrance in photo). The owners decorate their bar with a lot of passion. The decorations start in the hallway, with wall hangings and statues. They have candles hanging from the ceiling and homemade chests stacked on the bar for the Harry Potter pop-up and lots of tiki and Hawaiian decorations for the tiki pop-up.

My niece is a huge Harry Potter fan, so going to their Harry Potter pop-up with her was a must. They serve an abbreviated yet still quite extensive menu, but they also serve fun specialized cocktails that match the vibe of the bar. I ordered the Melonum Mystica, which featured watermelon and melon schnapps, lemon and lime juice and simple syrup and was in a fun bottle I could have kept. I love melon liquors, so I really enjoyed this. My niece ordered the Delirium, which featured vodka and a butterfly pea flower infusion that changes color when you add fresh lemon juice. We all enjoyed the Butterbeers, which we enjoyed for dessert because it features vanilla vodka, butterscotch schnapps and cream soda.

![Image 11](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_165733.jpg)![Image 12](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_165234.jpg)![Image 13](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_182115.jpg)

I couldn’t decide what to order food-wise, but ended up getting the meatball sub (The Meatball Grimoire) since I’m on a quest to enjoy meatball subs lately too. The meatball sub was phenomenal. The meatballs were large and tasty and topped with Amici’s marinara sauce and a nice helping of mozzarella and parmesan. The parmesan really gave it the edge. Just a really great sub – one of my top choice so far.

[![Image 14](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_175128.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_175128.jpg)

My niece enjoyed her Grand Hall Chicken Parm sandwich, and her boyfriend enjoyed The Crown Jewel Amici Burger (which is a 1/2 pound burger topped with grilled salami, mozzarella, LTO, and the house Italian dressing). No photos of those. Sorry.

![Image 15](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_190401.jpg)![Image 16](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_171202.jpg)

[![Image 17](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_181243.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_181243.jpg)

I then wanted to meet youngest niece to celebrate her turning 21 (since the bar only allows patrons who are 21+) at the summer tiki bar pop-up. She was unfortunately sick over her birthday, so we met up when oldest niece and her boyfriend were back in town. I wanted them to enjoy some nice cocktails since they are in college and probably don’t shell out for the fancy stuff. You can’t get fancier than tiki drinks. Youngest niece was blown away by her drink, which came in a small sand bucket (the Luau Lemonade I think?). It was plentiful, and I don’t think she even finished it but she was quite ‘chatty’ by the end. My Bahama Mama (coconut rum, white rum, pineapple and orange juice and grenadine) came in a plastic glass I could keep, which I gave to the boyfriend for his frat house bar. I enjoy tiki cocktails that feature fresh juice. Unfortunately my first choice (pina colada) wasn’t available that evening. Oldest niece’s once again changed colors, but this time it was the glass itself and not the drink.

![Image 18](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_180003.jpg)![Image 19](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_180008.jpg)

![Image 20](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_184514.jpg)![Image 21](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_184539.jpg)

## [Tuna Melt Quest](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/09/04/tuna-melt-quest/)

I enjoy a good tuna melt. Tuna melts have gotten really popular as a plot point in Heated Rivalry, so I’ve decide to document my years of enjoying a tuna melt. Unfortunately a lot of my favorites have closed, but I’ll include them as an “In Memorium” at the end. I’m always open to suggestions, so feel free to add a comment recommending your favorite here and I’ll check them out.

My current favorite is served at Chelo’s Kitchen in South Euclid. They only serve it for lunch during Lent. It has grilled onions and American and Swiss cheese. The tuna is briefly grilled on the flat top, and the rye bread is perfectly grilled as well. Rye bread is my favorite, but as you will see I don’t mind other breads if done well.

[![Image 23](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/20240223_114138-e1774657284878.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/20240223_114138-e1774657284878.jpg)

Luna Bakery may bill it as a tuna panini, but it is essentially a tuna melt. It has become my second favorite tuna melt now. It is a nice tuna salad topped with tomato and cheddar cheese. I was offered the choice of multigrain or Italian bread and chose Italian. I also had the choice of quinoa, chips or fruit as a side. The chips were a nice kettle chip, which is a favorite splurge of mine. The panini was delicious, nice and buttery with crispy bread. I didn’t even mind the chunks of celery, which I usually prefer a little smaller. I will definitely be going back. I’ve always enjoyed Luna. Their nest egg is amazing, and the crepes and coffees are delicious. I’m happy the flagship bakery is one so close to me in Cleveland Heights.

[![Image 24](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260912_150525.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260912_150525.jpg)

Yours Truly also does a great tuna melt. It features two scoops of their tuna sitting on a tomato slice and topped with melted cheddar on a toasted English muffin. A tuna melt on an English muffin is in fact my preferred form of tuna melt, which will be explained under In Memorium. The tuna salad was warmed up just enough, and the cheese was nicely melted.

[![Image 25](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260109_125255.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260109_125255.jpg)

Lehman’s Deli got on my radar when I started my tuna melt quest (it was one of my first stops). People recommended it, saying Lehman’s tuna melt is up there among the best tuna melts in Cleveland. It was indeed fantastic. The tuna was warm, and the cheese was nicely melted. I paired it with a cup of Italian wedding soup, which is one of my all-time favorite soups, and a Lehman’s vanilla cream soda, which was a total treat. You don’t see cream soda much anymore. The Italian wedding soup was pretty much perfect – with just the right amount of meatballs, pasta and spinach (escarole is ideal, but spinach is a perfectly fine substitute and more commonly found in most non-Italian restaurants). I also like starting the meal with a couple of their deviled eggs.

![Image 26](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152351.jpg)![Image 27](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152358.jpg)

Dominick’s Deli has a great tuna melt too. It is more tuna than tuna salad mayo-wise. The thing that makes it stand out is the bread – it’s fantastic. A crunchy roll that is split in half and broiled. And the tomatoes lined on top were great too. I tried to eat it as a sub, but it deserves the knife and fork service if you don’t want messy hands. Because it will squeeze out the sides and create a lovely mess.

[![Image 28](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260518_141056.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260518_141056.jpg)

The tuna melt at Nectar of the Tupelo in Euclid s extremely flavorful. It is a wet tuna melt that has finely diced jalapeno in it. I was taken aback when I read about the jalapeno, but I enjoyed the flavor it added. The fresh tomatoes were also a great addition and added a lovely freshness.

[![Image 29](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/20260428_142508-1.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/20260428_142508-1.jpg)

Davis Bakery is now the last Jewish deli standing in Cleveland. People always recommended I tried the tuna there, so I did. I love that it includes diced hardboiled egg. I’ve had the tuna melt twice and enjoyed it both times. You order at the deli counter. They have a dining area, or you can get it to go to enjoy at home or in your car. It is nicely warmed. It comes with a tasty cookie and a crisp pickle spear.

56 Social serves their tuna melt on marble rye, which is not my favorite rye (I’m a seeded fan), but it will do in a pinch. The tuna melt is made with house-made albacore tuna salad that is topped with heirloom tomato slices and Swiss and grilled on the marble rye. It was tasty. I just don

## [Captain Tony’s Pizza &Pasta](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/10/02/captain-tonys-pizza-pasta/)

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg)

I have been aware of Captain Tony’s Pizza & Pasta since I moved to the Heights 16 years ago, and I’m frankly irritated I haven’t tried it until now. We have a dearth of decent pizza places. Yes, we have Vero and Pizza Bogo, but there aren’t a lot of decent delivery spots. I usually drive to Lyndhurst to get a pizza from Jet’s. It’s not life-changing pizza, but it definitely hits the spot and is better than, say, Domino’s or Pizza Hut.

I was stuck at home on an all-day Zoom call for 3 days, so was unable to go to the grocery store. When I have these classes I usually order something through DoorDash and make the order large enough to eat over several days. My go-to is usually Chinese, but I was in the mood for pizza and checked to see what my choices were in my area. Captain Tony’s is located on Shaker Square (the southeast corner), so it is close enough to pop in and pick up an order if I wasn’t stuck at home. When I saw some of their unique offerings I decided to give it a try. It is apparently a small chain based out of Rochester, NY that started expanding in 1985, but it is the only location in Ohio. There is even one in London and Dubai, but, again, it is still a very small chain with only a couple of locations. Can it even be considered a chain if it’s the only location in Ohio?

The first pizza that caught my eye was the seafood pizza. It features a white garlic sauce that is topped with crabmeat, mozzarella, Romano, and cheddar cheese. I have to say I am so hooked I’ve ordered it several times now. It just hits the spot and the white garlic sauce is delicious paired with the crabmeat and cheeses. It also reheats really well in the air fryer.

[![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg)

My go to at any pizza place is a supreme, and the Captain’s Classic fits the bill perfectly. It is topped with pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, green peppers, onion, and cheese. If a pizza place does a supreme well, I know that their pizzas are good. They are generous with the toppings, and I was impressed to see that the mushroom were actual fresh mushrooms.

[![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg)

The Honey Mustard Chicken pizza also caught my eye because I love honey mustard, but I wasn’t as impressed with that one compared to the other two pizzas. It just tasted a little lackluster. Maybe I was expecting more honey mustard, but it was just ok.

[![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg)

Since I’m on my meatball sub quest I had to order the meatball sub. Huge fail. Not only were the meatballs tiny, but they were overwhelmed by the bread and didn’t have enough sauce or cheese. In fact, their buns are kind of lackluster but are used for their gourmet garlic bread (essentially garlic bread with cheese and a fresh tomato slice and a small container of marinara to dip it in) and regular garlic bread. Snore. It’s a huge pass for me. I also suspect the meatballs were of the frozen variety because they were pretty tasteless. Huge pass.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg)

I found out about the garlic bread when I ordered the lasagna. The lasagna was delicious, and the serving size was great (especially for the price). I enjoyed it over two days. I will definitely be ordering it again when I’m in the mood for lasagna. I don’t make it myself because lasagna is one of my biggest trigger foods that I can’t stop eating. Smaller portions mean I don’t eat the entire pan.

[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_193840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_193840.jpg)

I don’t know if I will order through DoorDash though when I can just pop over to Shaker Square and run in to pick up my order. It may be years late, but it is definitely going on my regular rotation now. Captain Tony’s is open seven days a week, Monday thru Thursday from 11 AM-9 PM, Friday from 11 AM-10 PM, Saturday from 12 noon-10 PM and Sundays from 12 noon-8 PM.

## [Tuna Melt Quest](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/09/04/tuna-melt-quest/)

I enjoy a good tuna melt. Tuna melts have gotten really popular as a plot point in Heated Rivalry, so I’ve decide to document my years of enjoying a tuna melt. Unfortunately a lot of my favorites have closed, but I’ll include them as an “In Memorium” at the end. I’m always open to suggestions, so feel free to add a comment recommending your favorite here and I’ll check them out.

My current favorite is served at Chelo’s Kitchen in South Euclid. They only serve it for lunch during Lent. It has grilled onions and American and Swiss cheese. The tuna is briefly grilled on the flat top, and the rye bread is perfectly grilled as well. Rye bread is my favorite, but as you will see I don’t mind other breads if done well.

[![Image 23](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/20240223_114138-e1774657284878.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/20240223_114138-e1774657284878.jpg)

Luna Bakery may bill it as a tuna panini, but it is essentially a tuna melt. It has become my second favorite tuna melt now. It is a nice tuna salad topped with tomato and cheddar cheese. I was offered the choice of multigrain or Italian bread and chose Italian. I also had the choice of quinoa, chips or fruit as a side. The chips were a nice kettle chip, which is a favorite splurge of mine. The panini was delicious, nice and buttery with crispy bread. I didn’t even mind the chunks of celery, which I usually prefer a little smaller. I will definitely be going back. I’ve always enjoyed Luna. Their nest egg is amazing, and the crepes and coffees are delicious. I’m happy the flagship bakery is one so close to me in Cleveland Heights.

[![Image 24](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260912_150525.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260912_150525.jpg)

Yours Truly also does a great tuna melt. It features two scoops of their tuna sitting on a tomato slice and topped with melted cheddar on a toasted English muffin. A tuna melt on an English muffin is in fact my preferred form of tuna melt, which will be explained under In Memorium. The tuna salad was warmed up just enough, and the cheese was nicely melted.

[![Image 25](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260109_125255.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20260109_125255.jpg)

Lehman’s Deli got on my radar when I started my tuna melt quest (it was one of my first stops). People recommended it, saying Lehman’s tuna melt is up there among the best tuna melts in Cleveland. It was indeed fantastic. The tuna was warm, and the cheese was nicely melted. I paired it with a cup of Italian wedding soup, which is one of my all-time favorite soups, and a Lehman’s vanilla cream soda, which was a total treat. You don’t see cream soda much anymore. The Italian wedding soup was pretty much perfect – with just the right amount of meatballs, pasta and spinach (escarole is ideal, but spinach is a perfectly fine substitute and more commonly found in most non-Italian restaurants). I also like starting the meal with a couple of their deviled eggs.

![Image 26](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152351.jpg)![Image 27](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152358.jpg)

Dominick’s Deli has a great tuna melt too. It is more tuna than tuna salad mayo-wise. The thing that makes it stand out is the bread – it’s fantastic. A crunchy roll that is split in half and broiled. And the tomatoes lined on top were great too. I tried to eat it as a sub, but it deserves the knife and fork service if you don’t want messy hands. Because it will squeeze out the sides and create a lovely mess.

[![Image 28](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260518_141056.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/20260518_141056.jpg)

The tuna melt at Nectar of the Tupelo in Euclid s extremely flavorful. It is a wet tuna melt that has finely diced jalapeno in it. I was taken aback when I read about the jalapeno, but I enjoyed the flavor it added. The fresh tomatoes were also a great addition and added a lovely freshness.

[![Image 29](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/20260428_142508-1.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/20260428_142508-1.jpg)

Davis Bakery is now the last Jewish deli standing in Cleveland. People always recommended I tried the tuna there, so I did. I love that it includes diced hardboiled egg. I’ve had the tuna melt twice and enjoyed it both times. You order at the deli counter. They have a dining area, or you can get it to go to enjoy at home or in your car. It is nicely warmed. It comes with a tasty cookie and a crisp pickle spear.

![Image 30](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/tunamelt.jpg)![Image 31](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/20240604_144903.jpg)

56 Social serves their tuna melt on marble rye, which is not my favorite rye (I’m a seeded fan), but it will do in a pinch. The tuna melt is made with house-made albacore tuna salad that is topped with heirloom tomato slices and Swiss and gr

# Grovewood Tavern and Wine Bar

[![Image 2: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png?w=300&h=38)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png)
[](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png)The Grovewood [![Image 3: 101_0683](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/101_0683.jpg?w=300&h=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/101_0683.jpg)Tavern and Wine Bar is hidden away in a North Collinwood neighborhood. In fact, your first thought when you are looking for it will be “Am I in the right place?” Tucked in the middle of a residential neighborhood just off I-90 (Hint: it’s best to get off at E. 182nd street), the Grovewood has been consistently serving outstanding food and drinks. This is probably one of my favorite restaurants in Cleveland and only 17 minutes from me by car, but I don’t think to go here as often as I should.

[![Image 4: group1](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/group1.jpg?w=300&h=248)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/group1.jpg)I first discovered the Grovewood in 2009, back when I was still running a dining out group through Meetup.com. Someone had recommended it, and we enjoyed an outstanding meal. Every subsequent visit I have made, whether I’m sitting on the patio or in the dining room, has been outstanding.

When you walk up to and into the restaurant, you can see the chefs cooking through the front window. There is a small, cozy bar area behind the hostess station, and the dining room is to the right. The inside feels like a comfy little neighborhood joint, with white Christmas “fairy” lights and quirky lamps hanging down from the ceiling and interesting pictures on the walls.![Image 5: 101_0681](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/101_0681.jpg?w=300&h=225)

They have an outstanding selection of wine and cocktails as well as a changing menu of beers on tap. The servers are very knowledgeable about the food, wine and beer.

Several friends and I met for dinner recently and enjoyed another fantastic meal. Several of my friends are vegetarians, so they were thrilled that the Grovewood has really expanded its offerings for vegetarians and vegans. The first time we were there they only had ![Image 6: IMAG0935](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/imag0935.jpg?w=169&h=300)one or two entrees to choose from. C. raved about the Curried Butternut Pasta featuring roasted cubes of butternut squash with coconut milk, cilantro and lime over pasta, while R. loved the Vegan Beanburger, featuring a huge herb-scented, mixed bean patty, fried crispy and served with arugula, fresh cucumbers, tomato, and Monterey Jack cheese, with house-cut Yukon fries and herbed mayo.

Advertisement

As for me, I ordered the Grilled Mini Brie and Pear Salad and the Grovewood Chicken Sandwich topped with sliced, grilled apples; caramelized onions; Brie and toasted almonds, accompanied by house-cut Yukon fries and herbed mayo. I could have done without the toasted almonds, but this sandwich was delicious. The house-cut fries were delicious as well, especially dipped in the herbed mayo and the house-made ketchup (nicely spicy but not too spicy – no Heinz served here!). I will definitely order it again.![Image 7: LobsterRav](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/lobsterrav.jpg?w=300&h=197)

This time around we shared the Belgian Chocolate Lava Cake and the Caramel Pecan Cake. Both were paired with vanilla ice cream, and were delectable. My dining companions dove into these so fast I was unable to get pictures. However, I have to say my absolutely favorite dessert in Cleveland is served here – Burnin’ Down the House, a chocolate swan filled with fresh berries and flambéed table side (for two), with two dishes of vanilla ice cream. It is one impressive dessert![![Image 8: BigTuna](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/bigtuna.jpg?w=300&h=235)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/bigtuna.jpg)

You really can’t go wrong ordering anything off the menu here. From the Yakitori to the Seared Tuna Loin (pictured here) to the Ohio City Pasta and gnocchi to the burger, everything I have had here has been outstanding.

The only thing I am not a fan of is the bread service. The bread is very flavorful, but somewhat dry. They serve it with a dipping sauce with olive oil, roasted garlic cloves and balsamic vinegar that just doesn’t work. The sauce doesn’t blend well, and you can’t really taste the balsamic. But on the bright side that just leaves more room for the rest of the food.[![Image 9: IMAG0933](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/imag0933.jpg?w=169&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/imag0933.jpg)

I attended a Mad Men Spirit Dinner here back in 2010 that I still remember fondly. People dressed in reminiscent dress, which was a lot of fun. The spirit dinner was hosted by North American Spirits and featured nostalgic cocktails such as a Manhattan made with bacon-infused bourbon (not the most stellar cocktail of the evening, but certainly the most unique) or a pear mule paired with complementary courses. It was outstanding from start to finish. In fact, I made the grilled brie salad with pear vinaigrette for Christmas that year (they gave us some recipes to take home with us). It received rave reviews from my family. If you get a chance to attend one of the spirit, beer or wine dinners you should definitely do it! Reservations are a must, and they tend to sell out quickly.![Image 10: Swan Aflame](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/swan-aflame.jpg?w=300&h=281)

# Amici Restaurant and Lounge

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_164840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_164840.jpg)

I’ve become a fan of Amici’s pop-up bars. I first heard about it with their Christmas bar. Amici is an Italian restaurant on the Strongsville/North Royalton border. They have great Italian food, which is available in the restaurant as well as their bar in their Event Center next door (entrance in photo). The owners decorate their bar with a lot of passion. The decorations start in the hallway, with wall hangings and statues. They have candles hanging from the ceiling and homemade chests stacked on the bar for the Harry Potter pop-up and lots of tiki and Hawaiian decorations for the tiki pop-up.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DYixcaDNSpa/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

My niece is a huge Harry Potter fan, so going to their Harry Potter pop-up with her was a must. They serve an abbreviated yet still quite extensive menu, but they also serve fun specialized cocktails that match the vibe of the bar. I ordered the Melonum Mystica, which featured watermelon and melon schnapps, lemon and lime juice and simple syrup and was in a fun bottle I could have kept. I love melon liquors, so I really enjoyed this. My niece ordered the Delirium, which featured vodka and a butterfly pea flower infusion that changes color when you add fresh lemon juice. We all enjoyed the Butterbeers, which we enjoyed for dessert because it features vanilla vodka, butterscotch schnapps and cream soda.

Advertisement

![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_165733.jpg)![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_165234.jpg)![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_182115.jpg)

I couldn’t decide what to order food-wise, but ended up getting the meatball sub (The Meatball Grimoire) since I’m on a quest to enjoy meatball subs lately too. The meatball sub was phenomenal. The meatballs were large and tasty and topped with Amici’s marinara sauce and a nice helping of mozzarella and parmesan. The parmesan really gave it the edge. Just a really great sub – one of my top choice so far.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_175128.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_175128.jpg)

My niece enjoyed her Grand Hall Chicken Parm sandwich, and her boyfriend enjoyed The Crown Jewel Amici Burger (which is a 1/2 pound burger topped with grilled salami, mozzarella, LTO, and the house Italian dressing). No photos of those. Sorry.

![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_190401.jpg)![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260519_171202.jpg)

[![Image 9](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_181243.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_181243.jpg)

I then wanted to meet youngest niece to celebrate her turning 21 (since the bar only allows patrons who are 21+) at the summer tiki bar pop-up. She was unfortunately sick over her birthday, so we met up when oldest niece and her boyfriend were back in town. I wanted them to enjoy some nice cocktails since they are in college and probably don’t shell out for the fancy stuff. You can’t get fancier than tiki drinks. Youngest niece was blown away by her drink, which came in a small sand bucket (the Luau Lemonade I think?). It was plentiful, and I don’t think she even finished it but she was quite ‘chatty’ by the end. My Bahama Mama (coconut rum, white rum, pineapple and orange juice and grenadine) came in a plastic glass I could keep, which I gave to the boyfriend for his frat house bar. I enjoy tiki cocktails that feature fresh juice. Unfortunately my first choice (pina colada) wasn’t available that evening. Oldest niece’s once again changed colors, but this time it was the glass itself and not the drink.

Advertisement

![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_180003.jpg)![Image 11](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_180008.jpg)

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DbrXLTwtf3m/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

I enjoyed the lasagna, which Amici is known for, while youngest niece was thrilled she could safely eat gluten-free at an Italian restaurant by ordering her meal with gluten-free penne. She ordered the Alfredo and enjoyed it. Oldest niece got the Hawaiian chicken bowl and loved it, while the boyfriend had another tasty burger. Everyone had a great time.

![Image 12](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_184514.jpg)![Image 13](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260804_184539.jpg)

Advertisement

I may eventually eat at the restaurant, but as long as the pop-up bars are so much fun I think I might keep enjoying my rare evenings there. Christmas pop-up here I come! Amici is open from 11 am to 10 pm every day but Sunday.

# Saigon Grille on Superior Avenue East

[![Image 2: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png?w=300&h=38)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[![Image 3: IMG_20120227_150257](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_150257.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_150257.jpg)I’m going to take a controversial stand – I prefer Saigon Grille over Superior Pho. I seem to crave pho on Mondays, when Minh Anh and Superior Pho are closed. A few weeks ago I was craving a banh mi, so I hit Google and searched for a restaurant that offered them. Number 1 Pho was open, but they only serve pho – not banh mi. The restaurant one door over from it did and was open all day from 10 a.m. to midnight, which was great [![Image 4: IMG_20120227_143645](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_143645.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_143645.jpg)because I was eating a late lunch at 2 p.m. After eating at Superior Pho today and ordering a similar pho and banh mi meal I can unequivocally say that I prefer the banh mi at Saigon Grille over Superior Pho (although the meal at Superior Pho was about $5 cheaper). Both restaurants serve outstanding pho, but if you want an outstanding banh mi I suggest you try Saigon Grille’s and see if you agree.

Saigon Grille is a small unassuming storefront right near Superior Pho and Number 1 Pho. Parking is available in the back off E. 31st street (caution: one way street), but I parallel parked on E. 31st and walked down to the cheerful door. I’m glad I did, because they have a little shrine right inside the door with incense, candles and a roll on a plate. It lent some major atmosphere to the place.

[![Image 5: IMG_20120227_144207](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144207.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144207.jpg)I was quickly seated, and the waitress quickly brought me a glass of water. I ordered my banh mi (A7) and P22 (Pho Tai Nam, which is rice noodle soup with eye round steak and well done flank steak). Since Saigon Grille serves Vietnamese and Thai cuisine, I ordered one of my favorite beverages (a Thai ice tea) to drink and was surprised to see that they served it as a bubble tea.

[![Image 6: IMG_20120227_144230](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144230.jpg?w=224&h=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144230.jpg)The banh mi was heavenly. You can choose between pork, chicken or ham, but if you don’t specify you get pork. Unless you are Jewish I don’t know why anyone would order anything but the pork. The grilled, charred smokiness combined really well with the bright and fresh vegetables. The bread was crusty without being difficult to bite into. It was, frankly, a little bit of heaven. I prefer the roll at Superior Pho, but since the sandwich contents themselves are so delicious I’ll happily eat it.

Advertisement

The pho was also delicious. I dressed it with the Thai basil, bean sprouts and squirt of fresh lime wedge that accompanies pho at any restaurant you order it. The soup was perfectly prepared. The noodles weren’t overcooked, and there was just enough meat to enjoy with every bite. I can still taste the lime. The serving was plentiful and I ended up taking over half of it home with me to enjoy that evening.

[![Image 7: IMG_20120227_144212](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144212.jpg?w=300&h=224)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/img_20120227_144212.jpg)

# Captain Tony’s Pizza &Pasta

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20260927_153704.jpg)

I have been aware of Captain Tony’s Pizza & Pasta since I moved to the Heights 16 years ago, and I’m frankly irritated I haven’t tried it until now. We have a dearth of decent pizza places. Yes, we have Vero and Pizza Bogo, but there aren’t a lot of decent delivery spots. I usually drive to Lyndhurst to get a pizza from Jet’s. It’s not life-changing pizza, but it definitely hits the spot and is better than, say, Domino’s or Pizza Hut.

I was stuck at home on an all-day Zoom call for 3 days, so was unable to go to the grocery store. When I have these classes I usually order something through DoorDash and make the order large enough to eat over several days. My go-to is usually Chinese, but I was in the mood for pizza and checked to see what my choices were in my area. Captain Tony’s is located on Shaker Square (the southeast corner), so it is close enough to pop in and pick up an order if I wasn’t stuck at home. When I saw some of their unique offerings I decided to give it a try. It is apparently a small chain based out of Rochester, NY that started expanding in 1985, but it is the only location in Ohio. There is even one in London and Dubai, but, again, it is still a very small chain with only a couple of locations. Can it even be considered a chain if it’s the only location in Ohio?

The first pizza that caught my eye was the seafood pizza. It features a white garlic sauce that is topped with crabmeat, mozzarella, Romano, and cheddar cheese. I have to say I am so hooked I’ve ordered it several times now. It just hits the spot and the white garlic sauce is delicious paired with the crabmeat and cheeses. It also reheats really well in the air fryer.

[![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180840.jpg)

Advertisement

My go to at any pizza place is a supreme, and the Captain’s Classic fits the bill perfectly. It is topped with pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, green peppers, onion, and cheese. If a pizza place does a supreme well, I know that their pizzas are good. They are generous with the toppings, and I was impressed to see that the mushroom were actual fresh mushrooms.

[![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_180531.jpg)

The Honey Mustard Chicken pizza also caught my eye because I love honey mustard, but I wasn’t as impressed with that one compared to the other two pizzas. It just tasted a little lackluster. Maybe I was expecting more honey mustard, but it was just ok.

[![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194330.jpg)

Since I’m on my meatball sub quest I had to order the meatball sub. Huge fail. Not only were the meatballs tiny, but they were overwhelmed by the bread and didn’t have enough sauce or cheese. In fact, their buns are kind of lackluster but are used for their gourmet garlic bread (essentially garlic bread with cheese and a fresh tomato slice and a small container of marinara to dip it in) and regular garlic bread. Snore. It’s a huge pass for me. I also suspect the meatballs were of the frozen variety because they were pretty tasteless. Huge pass.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260824_163709.jpg)

I found out about the garlic bread when I ordered the lasagna. The lasagna was delicious, and the serving size was great (especially for the price). I enjoyed it over two days. I will definitely be ordering it again when I’m in the mood for lasagna. I don’t make it myself because lasagna is one of my biggest trigger foods that I can’t stop eating. Smaller portions mean I don’t eat the entire pan.

[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_193840.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_193840.jpg)

I don’t know if I will order through DoorDash though when I can just pop over to Shaker Square and run in to pick up my order. It may be years late, but it is definitely going on my regular rotation now. Captain Tony’s is open seven days a week, Monday thru Thursday from 11 AM-9 PM, Friday from 11 AM-10 PM, Saturday from 12 noon-10 PM and Sundays from 12 noon-8 PM.

[![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194207.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260902_194207.jpg)

## [Raddell’s Slovenian Sausage Shop](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/07/24/raddells-slovenian-sausage-shop/)

[![Image 2](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122541.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122541.jpg)

Raddell’s Sausage has been a Cleveland staple for over four generations. It is located in the historic Waterloo Rd. & Collinwood neighborhood just off I-90 at the E. 152nd exit. Raddell’s is known for its homemade Slovenian smoked sausage and other European-style meats. When I was there someone asked for their rice sausage (which was only available frozen that day), and they also make Boudin, which can be hard to find here. While people come from all over to grab some smokies and sausages from 8-5 Mon, Tues & Wed, 8-4 Thur & Fri, and 8-3 on Sat, this modest deli is also a great place to grab a hearty lunch from 11-2 (every day but Sunday, when they are closed). The sandwiches are tasty and affordably priced. I got there shortly before noon, and there were only a couple of cars in the lot. However, when I left, the parking lot was packed and several guys were eating sandwiches in their cars and trucks.

[![Image 3](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122857.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122857.jpg)

The newest generation is doing a great job with their social media. Their [reel](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1046366971673645) featuring the Chicken Caprese Sub, which was the sandwich of the month in July, piqued my interest and I knew I had to check it out. The goofy humor of the dropped knife and making the bruschetta topping was charming.

[![Image 4](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122901.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_122901.jpg)

The sub certainly did not disappoint. The chicken sausage was super flavorful, and I loved the freshness of the tomato bruschetta and fresh basil. Their sub rolls are most likely Orlando rolls, because they sell Orlando bread there. My counter guy missed putting on a drizzle of Balsamic, but I was able to quickly remedy that at home. It was a delight from start to finish.

[![Image 5](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_125513.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_125513.jpg)

However, the other subs are just as tasty. I’ve been on a quest to try meatball subs (more on that in another post in the future), and their meatball sub wowed me. The meatballs are deliciously flavorful and soft in a tasty sauce and pillowy soft roll (ignore the weird flatness on top of the meatballs – that came from the paper and carryout container). This was a pleasure to bite into from start to finish. At only $10.99 it is a total deal. And I am addicted. I was craving one the next day.

[![Image 6](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_125713-1.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_125713-1.jpg)

The regular sausage sandwich is a total deal at $6.49. You can choose either a smoked Slovenian, bratwurst, or andouille sausage and can add other toppings if you’d like. I got the Slovenian sausage and topped it with the obligatory Bertman’s mustard and kraut. Divine!

[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_130000.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_130000.jpg)

Also, their #1 seller is the Big Billy, which is huge and quite filling. It features a jumbo sized house made smoked Slovenian sausage, and I of course got it with sauerkraut and stadium mustard. Despite how large the sausage is (a foot long) it was a really juicy delight and not overcooked and dry at all. I understand why it is the top seller.

[![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260729_135710.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260729_135710.jpg)

No lunch is complete without a side or two. They sell my favorite Sweet Maui Onion potato chips, so that is always a win. And the macaroni salad is really creamy and has visible chunks of pepper in it. I really enjoyed it.

![Image 9](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_130333.jpg)![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260720_130438.jpg)

While I was there I picked up a small Apple Strudel from their freezer and a container of Walnut and Apricot Kiflis. The Kiflis are not as soft as kolachky, but are tasty with a cup of coffee. I haven’t dug into the Apple Strudel yet, but I am confident it will be great. They are also known for their Potica, which is a traditional Slovenian walnut nut roll.

[![Image 11](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260721_124625.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260721_124625.jpg)

They sell Milka chocolate bars and quite a few other well-curated European items, so I know that whoever is doing the buying has good taste. The Croatian dark chocolate bar is an absolute must-try!

[![Image 12](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260729_133116.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/20260729_133116.jpg)

## [Lehman’s Deli](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/04/18/lehmans-deli/)

[![Image 14](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_153827.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_153827.jpg)

Lehman’s Deli and Bakery is a deli on Detroit Road in Westlake. Lehman’s Country Store started in the 1940’s and has evolved into Lehman’s Deli. It has been operating as a deli since 1983. Lehman’s serves coffee and tea, baked goods, soups, salads, and hot and cold sandwiches. In fact, Lehman’s makes over 140 different soups (several soups a day and they change every day – you can also buy quarts from the cooler) and nearly 100 different sandwiches. They also say you can invent your own sandwiches as long as they have the ingredients on hand. You can also just get half a sandwich if you want. Lehman’s cooks its own roast beef, corned beef, pastrami, chicken breast and turkey breast and bakes almost all of the desserts. It serves Cleveland Bagels and Rising Star Coffee.

![Image 15](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_150724.jpg)![Image 16](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/o.jpg)

The place is split into two different entities – the deli counter and the bakery/coffee bar and dining area. If you want a coffee or baked good take the entrance on the right. The deli counter and coolers are to the left. My doctor is just down the road, so I order on my phone from the parking lot and drive there to pick it up. I may have to chill in my car for a few minutes, but I have also been known to go into the bakery and grab a coffee.

![Image 17](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152351.jpg)![Image 18](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_152358.jpg)

Lehman’s got on my radar when I started my tuna melt quest. People recommended it, saying the Lehman’s tuna melt is up there among the best tuna melts in Cleveland. It was indeed fantastic. The tuna was warm, and the cheese was nicely melted. I paired it with a cup of Italian wedding soup and a Lehman’s vanilla cream soda, which was a total treat. You don’t see cream soda much anymore. The Italian wedding soup was pretty much perfect – with just the right amount of meatballs, pasta and spinach (escarole is ideal, but spinach is a perfectly fine substitute and more commonly found in most non-Italian restaurants).

![Image 19](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240916_163351.jpg)![Image 20](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240916_163851.jpg)

I ordered a turkey reuben on my next visit and paired it with a bag of chips and an order of deviled eggs. The eggs were a little tougher than I like, but the filling was great. The turkey reuben had a decent amount of smoked turkey along with sauerkaut and Thousand Island dressing on grilled rye. And the bread was perfectly grilled. I also really enjoyed the Calypso Island Wave Lemonade, which blends pineapple, banana, mango, passion fruit and orange with the tartness of lemonade.

[![Image 21](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_161331.jpg?w=864)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20240313_161331.jpg)

They also offer a nice selection of sub sandwiches. The one pictured here is the Italian sub, but I’m intrigued by the idea of a clam strip sub (“super sized clam strips on a grilled hoagie roll with tartar sauce, lettuce & tomato”). The Poor Boy also sounds tasty with bologna, hard salami, American cheese, shaved ham, onion, pickle, tomato, lettuce, cole slaw & mayo. I grew up calling them hoagies, but I like the addition of cole slaw. The Italian sub could easily be held up against any Italian sub. It features hard salami, Provolone cheese, shaved ham, pepperoni, onion, tomato, pickle & lettuce that is topped with zesty Italian dressing. It had a nice zesty punch to it between the Italian dressing and the salami and pepperoni.

[![Image 22](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20250313_171220.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/20250313_171220.jpg)

I’m looking forward to my next doctor’s visit in March so I can explore more of the menu. The deli is open 6 days a week (Monday through Friday from 7 am to 8 pm, Saturday from 7 am to 5 pm and closed on Sunday), while the bakery is open 7 days a week (from 6-4 Monday through Friday, 7 am to 5 pm on Saturday and 7 am to 1 pm on Sunday).

### Contact info:

24961 Detroit Road  
Westlake, OH 44145  
(440) 871-3445

## [Fish Fryday #7 2026: Johnny’s on Fulton and the Donauschwaben German-American Club](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2026/04/04/fish-fryday-7-2026-johnnys-on-fulton-and-the-donauschwaben-german-american-club/)

[![Image 24](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_131044.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_131044.jpg)

We’ve made it to Good Friday and the end of the Lenten season. I had every intention of writing a slightly unhinged post for today’s lunch, because I had decided to drive to Woodmere for the tuna sub at Jersey Mike’s. The one in Woodmere is the only one in the area worth going to, because their subs are delicious compared to the boring output at, say, South Euclid. I don’t know if it is because their oil and vinegar is tastier or they use a decent amount, but I can tell the difference (after having the same sub two days in a row from both locations). In any event, last night Johnny’s on Fulton posted on Facebook that today was the last day for their Friday fish lunch. I haven’t been to Johnny’s on Fulton in years (and usually am there to enjoy the backyard seating) and their photo intrigued me, so my plans changed.

[![Image 25](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_123554.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_123554.jpg)

Johnny’s on Fulton is about as old-school Cleveland Italian as you can get. It’s been in business for 100 years, having been renamed Johnny’s in 1952. Before it was Johnny’s Bar on Fulton, it was Louise’s Gardens, a grocery store started by the current owner, Bo Santosuosso’s grandmother, in 1924. Since then, four generations of the family have worked at the fine-dining location, making it what it is today.

[![Image 26](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_124559.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_124559.jpg)

I arrived at 12:30 and after climbing a couple small stairs rimmed in yellow and entering the establishment, I was greeted by a couple guys sitting at the bar telling me “she’ll be right back” to seat me and was then after a minute or so escorted to a table in the back of the dining room up a cute little Art Deco-ish stair. I sat with my back to the wall and immediately sank into the banquette booth so deep that I was almost lying down. Since I was there to eat and not wear my food I moved to the chair opposite the wall. With my back to the wall, I enjoyed hearing a table of Cleveland police officers enjoying their lunch.

![Image 27](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_124033.jpg)![Image 28](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_125208.jpg)

I ordered the fish fry, which came out so fast my head spun. The server explained that they have them queued and ready to go. The lunch special is served until 3, when the close to prep for dinner. The fish was good, hot, well-breaded and fried, but the star of the show was the French fries. They were really tasty. I didn’t enjoy the cole slaw as much, because I found it to be pretty bitter. I was going to order a glass of white Bordeaux with my lunch because that is my absolute favorite, but the shipment hadn’t arrived yet and they were out of it. She talked me into a small split of prosecco paired with Chambord for a tasty Kir Royale. Since it was the last fish fry of the season I decided to splurge and celebrate it. The meal cost me $41 plus an $8 tip. Pretty pricy, but I was splurging at a historic restaurant in Cleveland so it was okay.

[![Image 29](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_182600.jpg?w=768)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_182600.jpg)

I was very excited to go to the Donauschwaben tonight. I grew up a mile from the Club in Olmsted Falls. My parents were members, and we swam and played tennis there a lot. I celebrated many a swim birthday party at the Club, swimming in the pond with the fish and the snapping turtle. I remember the old farmhouse with the rickety floors where they used to host the fish fries, special dinners and Oktoberfest. My sister and I worked the parking lot during the Oktoberfest, being paid in pitchers of beer as underage teens and directing folks to park on the soccer fields. My how times have changed, with the paved parking lot, the new chalet, and the pond being fenced in with no swimming due to liability issues. I taught German to fourth graders there back in 2020 before and during the pandemic. The Donauschwaben is in my veins. I’ve been to the fish fries there so many times, but never documented my visits or can’t find the photos of the ones I did. It was high time to change that.

![Image 30](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_182642.jpg)![Image 31](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_183100.jpg)![Image 32](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/20260403_183254.jpg)

Since I had a larger lunch than I had originally planned I decided not to hit the evening fish fry at the Donauschwaben German-American Club when it opened at 4:30. # Where I Hang: Paulius Nasvytis, Owner of the Velvet Tango Room

![Image 3](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/8e3bf55d651a6eccd7505a0fc07132096eb778daec5af869a5fd0cbc9b6f4d51?s=96&d=mm&r=g)[Jason Beudert](https://www.clevescene.com/author/jason-beudert/)April 2, 2014 July 28, 2025

![Image 4: Picture_7.png](https://i0.wp.com/media2.fdncms.com/clevescene/imager/where-i-hang-paulius-nasvytis-owner-of-the-velvet-tango-room/u/original/4173158/1396474329-picture_7.png?resize=225%2C229&ssl=1)

When he’s not hanging around the Velvet Tango Room, the quintessential craft cocktail bar he created over 17 years ago, VTR’s master of ceremonies Paulius Navytis stays close to home.

“I have lived in the Warehouse District for ten years now,” he says. “I love living downtown. It has really blossomed into a real neighborhood.”

“The Greenhouse Tavern is one of my favorites. Chef Jonathan Sawyer has a passion for food that really shows,” he says. And when it comes to sushi, Nasvytis says nobody does it like Ginko. “There are no comparisons anywhere” he says.

The West Side Market’s famed Frank’s Bratwurst also makes the short list. “I can eat their brats for breakfast, lunch and dinner — all on the same day.”

When he does leave downtown, Americano in Bratenahl is his choice. “Vytauras Sasnauskas is one of Cleveland’s most unknown and truly passionate and talented chefs.” And for those other times when a trip out of downtown is not in order and he simply wants to walk somewhere for a bite and a drink, it’s usually to the Map Room. “The beer is always cold, they make a legit pizza and they have sauerkraut balls, which should be a staple in Cleveland bars and restaurants,” he says.

We agree.

# Witch Doctor, a Botanically Themed Cocktail Lounge, Opens in Old Brooklyn in September

 “We want things to be a little weird and different,” says Matt Luebbert. “You can get Maker’s Mark, Jim Beam and stuff like that anywhere. I want people to come here and try new things.”

The Witch Doctor opens soon

Matt Luebbert and brothers Charlie and Michael Eby have been working on the [Witch Doctor](https://www.instagram.com/witchdoctorcle/?hl=en) (3314 Broadview Rd.) space in Old Brooklyn for two years since purchasing the building on Broadview Rd.

“It was time well spent,” says Charlie. “We do very much like where it is now.”

The result of those labors is a cocktail lounge like no other, which guests can begin enjoying when it opens on Sept. 2. What the owners casually describe as a “botanically-themed bar” is, in fact, a serious bar program that blends meticulously formulated ingredients into one-of-a-kind concoctions and dispenses them in a whimsical, comfortable lair.

Luebbert, a member of the US Bartenders’ Guild and former bar manager at Rood in Lakewood, prepares a dizzying variety of tinctures, infusions, syrups, cordials, bitters and spirits from a wide assortment of botanicals that he purchases from local apothecaries.

“Once I started making things by hand, I started making dang near everything by hand,” he explains. “That evolved into making vermouths and compound cordials and bitters.”

Whereas another bartender might reach for a bottle of high-quality grenadine, Luebbert crafts his own from fresh pomegranate. Same goes for the orgeat syrup, Herring-style cherry cordial, curacao and sweet vermouth. The Witch Doctor even has its own versions of gin, rum, tequila and vodka. Each functional cocktail is said to aid some facet of wellness, such as reducing stress, boosting immunity, aiding digestion, fighting inflammation or a combination thereof.

“We want things to taste good, cocktails that everyone can enjoy and that are drinkable,” says Luebbert. “But something that will be different from what you normally find. We want things to be a little weird and different. You can get Maker’s Mark, Jim Beam and stuff like that anywhere. I want people to come here and try new things.”

“A little weird and different” is an apt description for the venue as well. Guests seated at the bar will spy an apothecary’s cupboard stocked with dried plants, herbs, roots and spices. Just past the barroom, the space opens into a cavernous cathedral-like area that feels like a Norse drinking hall. A third room is imbued with a warm and cozy glow from newly installed stained-glass windows and is appointed with graceful Rococo-style furniture.

“I’d describe it as mystical, cabin-in-the-woods with medieval tavern vibes,” says Luebbert.

“Or if you stumbled out of the bayou in New Orleans,” adds Charlie.

Generously proportioned tables in the main room were constructed from beefy live-edge timber. The crew laid white oak floors throughout much of the space. Even at capacity of 75 guests the bar will feel airy and uncrowded.

The menu, a feathery deckled-edge parchment affair, ticks off cocktails called Blood Oath, Anna Felactic, Imhotep, Brimstone and Baba Yaga. Those beverages are served in elegant glassware, often of the mix-and-match vintage variety. Further down the menu is the “Medicine Cabinet,” where patrons can discover the building blocks that go into the various components.

“I want to make sure people know what goes into it because who knows what types of allergies people might have, but also to help people identify the source of some of the flavors,” Luebbert explains.

And finally, there will be a comprehensive list of the botanicals used in the beverage program.

Chef John Hagerty, formerly of Green Kitchen and Never Say Dive, is in the process of opening a new spot immediately next door to the Witch Doctor. The two businesses will collaborate on a food menu that will be served in the bar, says Charlie.

“I expect it to be more of an eclectic American fare,” he notes.

The Witch Doctor will be open Wednesday through Saturday evenings.

## [In Memorium: Walter Hyde](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2021/11/21/in-memorium-walter-hyde/)

It’s been a month. I thought I was ready. I wasn’t. I promised his sister I would post this memorial video though. We miss you, Walter.

[https://jill-sommer.com/Walter.mp4](https://jill-sommer.com/Walter.mp4)

The Cleveland food scene and its close-knit chefs suffered a major loss on October 16th. Walter Hyde of Now We’re Cooking, Swingo’s, Giovanni’s, The Annex, Fat Casual BBQ, Tavern of Solon, Fahrenheit-Charlotte, Sterle’s and most recently [Ice Ice] Daisy’s on Fleet died of a heart attack after a smoked prime rib pop-up with Penny Barend Tagliarina at Terrestrial Brewery. We are all reeling from the loss. His creativity was boundless. Who else could turn a cheese ball into a legendary appetizer? He and Scott could roast a delicious pig. His smoked prime rib and kind heart made him a legend. Everything he touched was delicious. [Walter Hyde](https://www.facebook.com/groups/586823648119308/user/1525133440/?__cft__[0]=AZW_B4J1Exry5XaZUNmFkQMDoEmcDHJBP09nG49eZ6apKQesUekDB3C0lx4uYNiRJ--eVkz8Uj0jLG0D7ap8-yFXIuFFdXVrS6wEl47rTpgynPlIcu3I8flRWleWxqwbN5iiGFnQd2fXKKIfF3-Mufcn&__tn__=-]K-R), you will be missed. I’m heartbroken.

## [DiCillo Tavern – Fish Fry Friday #1 2021](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2021/02/27/dicillo-tavern/)

![Image 6: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[![Image 7](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/capture.jpg?w=400)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/capture.jpg)

  
From Google StreetView

After finishing my invoicing for the month I was ready for a fish fry last night. I referred to my shortlist, and the first on the list was also one of the closest to me. DiCillo Tavern is located on Mayfield Road in Mayfield, close to Golden Gate. It sticks out in the sea of strip malls because it is an old house. It’s got this good quality hole in the wall vibe going for it. In fact, it reminds me of the old Suds MacGuire in Olmsted Falls – an old house that was a dive bar/restaurant and had killer fish fries. DiCillo has been serving their famous “Whaler” fish fry dinner since 1933. The fish fry is take-out only this year, daily from 4 to 8 p.m.

[![Image 8](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_175514-1.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_175514-1.jpg)

I headed out shortly after 5 and arrived there at 5:45. I had tried to call in my order, but no one answered the phone. The parking lot was packed with big trucks. I got one of the last easy-to-access parking spaces (the trucks were not parked straight so there were gaps). I was surprised to see so many vehicles and expected a long wait. I was pleased to see the bar side was packed with patrons (no masks as far as I could see, but they were in a separate room), while the restaurant side was hopping with take-out pick-ups. I placed my order and was told it would be about a half an hour. I had planned to sit in my car, but I was told I could sit in the socially distanced restaurant area while I waited. By the time my order was ready I was not the only person sitting around the restaurant, but we were all masked and sitting at tables divided with plexi-glass.

[![Image 9](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184356-1.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184356-1.jpg)

I was surprised when my order was only $24. I had ordered the Fisherman’s Sampler ($18), which contained a “mini” Whaler, a couple pieces of perch, and a couple fried shrimp. I ordered the pierogi as a side dish ($6) and the clam chowder ($6). She had added the pierogi as my side, so I didn’t pay extra for them. I slipped her a couple bucks as a tip and was on my way home. I had to play parking Jenga to leave because two cars had blocked the exit row and two other cars were parked along the side with their flashers on.

[![Image 10](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184803.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/20210226_184803.jpg)

As to the fish fry itself, it was delicious. The only down side was the pierogi, which I would not be surprised were Mrs. T’s. Luckily I didn’t end up paying extra for them. The clam chowder had a thicker consistency than most milk-based chowders and it was chock full of clams and potatoes. I think the consistency might have come from the potatoes breaking down. I really enjoyed it.

![Image 11](https://photos.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/DiCillo-Tavern-Fish-Fry.jpg)

The Whaler – from the DiCillo Tavern Facebook page

The fried fish and shrimp were delicious. Perfectly fried and overcooked or dry. I can see why the Whaler is so popular because that particular piece of fish is stunning. It is a large portion with firm white meat inside. The perch were okay. They were flatter and consistent, which leads me to believe they are frozen, not fresh. But perch is perch and adored by many here in Cleveland. I also adored the coleslaw. It had a nice horseradish bite to it and was really creamy. If I go back again (and let’s be honest, I just might) I’ll order a Whaler and a huge side of coleslaw. If you are on the east side, you can’t go wrong with DiCillo’s. But order early. They ran out of chowder at 6:30.

## [Polpetta](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2019/08/03/polpetta/)

![Image 13: in-memoriam-graphic](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/in-memoriam-graphic.png)

[![Image 14](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/o.jpg?w=300)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/o.jpg)Polpetta is the brain child of restauranteurs Brian Okin and Adam Bostwick of Cork & Cleaver and Graffiti: A Social Kitchen fame. I have had some amazing meals from these two chefs. They closed the two popular restaurants to focus on the Polpetta concept, which relies heavily on the theme of “balls.” The decor is heavy on old meat grinders, which are used as the door handle and light fixtures, and artwork with cleverly-hidden balls in them.[![Image 15](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_181541.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_181541.jpg)

They launched the Polpetta concept at Porco when Walter Hyde was cooking in the tiny kitchen there. That was where I had my first taste of Sunday Supper, which I personally think is the best spaghetti and meatballs I have had in Cleveland. Usually restaurant spaghetti and meatballs are bland, but the meatballs here are well-seasoned and paired with a herbaceous pomodoro red sauce. The pasta was al dente and easy to twirl. When I told my server that I think they are the best spaghetti and meatballs in Cleveland he told me about a woman from Little Italy who came in and was vocally critical of everything, but once she had the Sunday Supper she was quiet and said she would be back. He said she’s been back at least seven times. I agree, Nonna.

[![Image 16](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/imag0597.jpg?w=169)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/imag0597.jpg)

Porco version[![Image 17](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160342.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160342.jpg)

Polpetta version

[![Image 18](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/20181120_191131.jpg?w=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/20181120_191131.jpg)Once they opened their restaurant on Detroit Road in Rocky River it was on my list of places to try, but it took a while to make my way over there. I finally met a group of friends there for a nice meal, and that night I accidentally ordered what I think is the best thing on the menu, the Spinach and Meatball Dip. It features mini-meatballs in a spinach-parmesan-roasted tomatoes bechamel sauce and fun little pita dippers. This dip is Chef Adam at his best. It is rich and lush, and I could have eaten the whole thing by myself and regretted it. Everyone at the table adored it, and we practically licked the serving plate clean.

[![Image 19](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_194803.jpg?w=225)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/20181120_194803.jpg)I was less impressed by my entree choice that evening. I ordered The Adam, which features chicken meatballs, Thai peanut sauce, and fried rice. I love Adam’s fried rice, which I first enjoyed as spam fried rice at a pop-up at Toast several years ago. It was then included on the menu at Graffiti, and I happily ordered it several times. Unfortunately the Thai peanut sauce was too bitter that night. I was expecting a nice, creamy Thai peanut sauce, and I think it had too much hot sauce in it that night. My friend Nancy loves his Thai peanut sauce, so apparently it was an anomaly. Luckily I had eaten a ton of the appetizer, so I didn’t go away hungry. But I knew they could do better based on past experience.

[![Image 20](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160333.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190712_160333.jpg)I left wishing I had ordered the Grandma Bos, which is a chicken paprikash featuring chicken meatballs, paprikash sauce, and herbed spaetzle. When I ordered it the server asked if I wanted sour cream on top. Yes, please. This was a satisfying dish. The chicken meatballs were nicely seasoned, albeit a little denser than I had hoped. Overall the meatballs here are very dense, but at least they won’t fall apart. The herbed spaetzle are not the traditional (i.e., bland) German spätzle I am used to, but I liked the herb flavor profile and the pan-fried crispiness held up well against the paprikash sauce. I would order this again and again.![Image 21](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20181120_230714.jpg?w=170)If you like paprikash you will like this dish.

I ordered the Cereal Balls for dessert, which are made from several different cereals molded into rice krispie-like balls served with milk panna cotta and fresh berries and bananas. I first enjoyed Adam’s panna cotta at a grill evening on the Graffiti patio, so I was looking forward to that magic being recreated. He used cereal milk for that one, but the Polpetta panna cotta just uses milk so it was not as magical – even though it was tasty.

[![Image 22](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_211820.jpg?w=223)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/img_20190520_211820.jpg)

The OG Fat Kid

If you want a dessert that will bowl you over, order the Fat Kid 3.0, which features fried cookie dough balls, ice cream, chips, candy and fun. I got to taste the OG Fat Kid at a Graffiti Throw Back dinner at Polpetta a couple of months ago. That one was outrageously good and featured french fries, which was a fun pairing with the ice cream and chocolate and nerds. It is definitely a dessert to share though.
