## [The Fairview Tavern](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/12/18/the-fairview-tavern/)

[![Image 49](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_135934.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_135934.jpg)

The Fairview Tavern in Fairview Park is a hole in the wall bar that serves great food. It is located in a strip mall on Lorain Road and is open every day of the year from 11 a.m. to 2:30 a.m. (and opens at 7 a.m. on Sundays). There is a basic menu, but the Blue Plate Specials and Chef’s Specials change weekly and a happy hour that runs from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. They also serve breakfast on Sundays from 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. If you live nearby that might be a fun option, but since I live 40 minutes away it isn’t one for me.

There is plenty of seating in the bar area, but I have always sat at the dining area at the back of the venue. There are plenty of tables that can accommodate any number of diners.

![Image 50](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_124559.jpg)![Image 51](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_124831.jpg)

The Friday special is their perch dinners. I met a chef friend here when we heard about their perch. They use real perch because it curled up perfectly. The perch filets are perfectly fried. They are $14 for 3 filets and $17 for 4. They come served with fries and slaw, but we were able to upgrade to pierogi, which were really well prepared. One of my friends ordered a perch sandwich on another visit. The sandwich only has 2 perch filets. It would have been perfect with 3. He ended up cutting the sub roll in half and only eating half a roll with both filets. So if you want a good perch sub ask to add another filet even if there is an additional charge.

[![Image 52](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_130549.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_130549.jpg)

The appetizers are also tasty. I have had the kielbasa coins, which were stellar, and another friend recently ordered the pepperoni rolls, which featured phyllo dough. He also raved about their fresh made pork rinds. So if an appetizer appeals to you by all means order it.

![Image 53](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_130026.jpg)![Image 54](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_122540.jpg)

My friends who live on the west side and appreciate a good bargain turned me on to the place. The Blue Plate Specials are $10 and include a generous side salad. They also haven’t charged us for non-alcoholic beverages. We initially met there for the Tuesday burger and pint special (for $10 – $8 for the burger and 2 for a domestic beer). The burger patties are generous and you can get whatever burger fixings you want.

[![Image 55](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_123814.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_123814.jpg)

The burgers and sandwiches are served with housemade kettle chips, which are quite tasty, but the star of the show is the chip dip. I ordered a Patty Melt most recently and was quite pleased with it. I ended up taking half of it home to eat later.

[![Image 56](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_123853.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_123853.jpg)

The clam chowder is great – with lots of big chunks of potato, clams, celery, etc. If it’s on the menu definitely get it. I ordered a bowl along with my Patty Melt. The serving was huge. The chowder was creamy and not at all lumpy. I enjoyed every bite.

[![Image 57](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_122304.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_122304.jpg)

The pizzas are also quite large. I haven’t tried one yet, but my friends who did enjoyed it. One ordered the Mediterranean and the one below is mushroom and pepperoni. The mushrooms are fresh and not canned, which is always appreciated. Both had several slices but had to get boxes for later. I will probably order one the next time I go and none of the Blue Plate Specials appeal to me.

[![Image 58](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_124024.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251003_124024.jpg)

The schnitzel and spätzle were quite nice on another visit. They were supposed to come with a lemon basil sauce, but the waitress happily substituted brown gravy instead when my friends asked for the sauce on the side because it was extremely lemony on a previous visit. It was a lot of ofod for only $10 0 with two pork cutlets and lots of fresh made spätzle.

[![Image 59](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20250926_130015.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20250926_130015.jpg)

The servers have all been friendly and accommodating every time I have been there. We tip generously when we order the Blue Plate Specials because they run around a lot for a $10 tab, bring out salads and then the entrees, refilling our beverages (which they don’t charge for), etc.

[![Image 60](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_124743.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20240315_124743.jpg)

It isn’t fine dining, but it is quite tasty for a hole in the wall bar. I’d go so far as to call it a diamond in the rough. And the food changes often enough that you won’t get bored. I’ve only been there for lunch, but the live music apparently can bring in the crowds. I can’t wait to try their clambake.

## [Baraona’s Bakery](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/10/08/baraonas-bakery/)

![Image 62](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250822_143459.jpg)![Image 63](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250822_143512.jpg)

Baraona’s Bakery is a family-owned bakery in Garfield Heights on Libby Road just off Lee Road that has been serving the Cleveland area since 1949. They are known for their cakes. It is being run by the third generation. The bakery was originally named Giaimo’s and was located at 119th and Kinsman. Baraona’s bakery moved to its current location in 1970.

[![Image 64](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250823_135708.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250823_135708.jpg)

It is THE place to buy cassata cake or strawberry whipped cream cake. Their cassata cake is known as the best in town among those in the know. Baraona’s finished with more than 49 percent of more than 5,000 votes cast making it Cleveland.com’s People’s Choice cassata cake award winner in 2023. Baraona’s sells an average of 200 to 250 Cleveland cassata cakes a week. Cleveland cassata cake is not like Italian cassata cake. The Italian cassata cake (only available by special order) features layers of sponge cake filled with ricotta cheese, chocolate chips and maraschino cherries, and iced in whipped cream, while the Cleveland cassata cake features layers of sponge cake filled with custard, strawberries in a glaze and iced in whipped cream. The strawberry whipped cream cake does not contain custard – just strawberries and whipped cream. I prefer the cassata cake, because I love a good custard. The whipped cream frosting is light and airy, the custard filling is creamy and delicious, and the strawberries are always fresh! Baraona’s signature cassata cake was my birthday cake this year and was just as good as I remembered. You can get flowers or sprinkles on their cakes, but I just went with a plain “Happy Birthday” since I was sharing the birthday party with another friend. Everyone loved it.

![Image 65](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250823_144513.jpg)![Image 66](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250823_142640.jpg)

They don’t usually sell the cakes by the slice, but you can always get them as a cupcake. The cassata cupcake is always a nice alternative.

[![Image 67](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/o.jpg?w=713)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/o.jpg)

They also make a variety of other mouth-watering, made-from-scratch bakery products like doughnuts, cookies, nut rolls, poppyseed rolls, cannolis, pastries, pies, cupcakes and turnovers. While I was in line to pick up my cassata cake, I chatted with several customers and ended up buying a chocolate chunk cookie and a slice of banana cake. Both were good, but that chocolate chunk cookie was one of the best I’ve had. The guy who recommended the cookies got a red velvet cookie. If you like coconut you’ll love the Almond Joy cookie. There is basically a cookie for everyone’s taste, and they are all great.

![Image 68](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250822_154940.jpg)![Image 69](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/20250822_164918.jpg)

I need to try their datenut cake to see if it is as good as Dick’s Bakery in Berea, which is my ride-or-die cake. I had a Dick’s datenut cake for my high school graduation years ago and have been known to buy the datenut cupcakes. If you like Italian baked goods like 7-layer bars, pignoli (a cookie made with almond paste, granulated sugar, and egg whites), Italian spritz cookies, cannolis, etc. you will find it here. I also bought a bunch of kolachky recently. They aren’t as light and fluffy as kolachky from a Eastern European bakery like Rudy’s or Michael’s. I got lemon, cheese, apricot and raspberry and passed on the nut filling. The cheesecake, however, was absolutely heavenly. No topping needed. It was creamy and delicious just plain.

## [Mary Yoder’s Amish Kitchen in Middlefield](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/08/13/mary-yoders-amish-kitchen-in-middlefield/)

[![Image 76](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_175248.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_175248.jpg)

Mary Yoder’s Amish Kitchen opened in 1987 and is owned by the Miller family. Located in Middlefield, which is apparently in the center of the fourth largest Amish community in the world, Mary Yoder’s features a full-service restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner; a bakery; a private banquet room; and a gift shop. It’s not necessarily Cleveland, but Cleveland-adjacent and close enough to be a fun road trip. In fact, I took a spontaneous road trip out there for the dinner buffet in July. I drove out there a lot when I lived in Solon. It’s about an hour’s drive from Cleveland Heights either down South Woodland or on 422 to 700 (scenic drive over LaDue Reservoir and down some side roads past Amish homes and farms). I also love driving there in the fall to enjoy the changing leaves (I recommend the hot apple cider in the fall – see photo below). It’s definitely a tourist location and a tourist restaurant. That being said, you will see locals dining here as well as the occasional Amish or Mennonites dining here (but to be fair I saw a table of them at Cowboy Food and Drink in Bainbridge last month).

[![Image 77](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_170551.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_170551.jpg)

Mary Yoder’s isn’t necessarily “amazing” food (like Der Dutchman or other restaurants near Millersburg and Berlin – and not to be confused with Mrs. Yoder’s), but it is extremely comforting fare. It has its good days and bad days – for example, the dressing that I usually adore was too salty last week. But the food is hearty and hits the spot. It’s made by Amish women in their kitchen, and the buffet ($17.99 for the dinner buffet and $12.99 for the salad bar) is constantly stocked from 11:30 am to close (8 pm) Monday through Saturday (the restaurant is closed on Sundays). There is also a breakfast buffet (for $12.99), but I have only had the breakfast buffet once and there are no photos from that visit. It opens at 6 am and is available until 11 am. If you have a hankerin’ for something not on the buffet, they have an extensive menu to choose from. Some favorites include the ham, pork chops, roast turkey or roast beef or a hot roast beef or turkey sandwich. They even have a trail bologna sandwich, which is just Troyer’s Trail Bologna and Middlefield Swiss on a fresh roll. Easy enough to buy and make at home by buying the Trail Bologna from the cooler in the gift shop and grabbing some Middlefield Swiss from Rothenbuhler Cheese Chalet (formerly Middlefield Cheese), but definitely a unique offering to order there (just be sure to pull off the plastic casing before biting in – true story). There is ample seating available, and it has a banquet room for large groups. When you walk in head to the front of the building to your left.

[](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_170305.jpg)![Image 78](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_170305.jpg)![Image 79](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/saladbar.jpg)

I adore a good old-fashioned salad bar, and the salad bar contains all my favorites – a nice selection of greens, hardboiled egg, peas, beets, red onion, tomato, cucumber, etc. There is always a decent wet salad or two to choose from. I love cottage cheese, broccoli salad or macaroni salad to pair on my salad, which allows me to use less salad dressing. It is always the highlight of the meal for me, which I then follow with a couple of selections on the lunch/dinner buffet for a couple of bucks more. I got a side of cottage cheese with a to go meal the other day and was amazed by how creamy and delicious their cottage cheese is. So much so that I called to find out who they get it from.

![Image 80](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20220714_182437.jpg)![Image 81](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/salad.jpg)

I usually only fill up one dinner plate with my choices, but others take several trips. The buffet offerings do vary by the day, but there is usually always baked or broasted chicken, mashed potatoes, dressing and a nice vegetable on offer. Not to mention a dessert or two like a pudding. Last week one patron was sad that only the “blue jell-o” was left. But you can always order a piece of their excellent pies if you have room (or get a piece to go to enjoy later at home). I always enjoy the broasted chicken and chicken or beef noodles. The mashed potatoes are hearty and tasty. Be sure to not take too much, because there are no to go containers for the buffet (well, technically there are, but they charge $7.99 per pound).

![Image 82](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_171954.jpg)![Image 83](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20220714_183949.jpg)![Image 84](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/dinner.jpg)

I went home with a butterscotch pie last week and special ordered a peach pie yesterday, which I picked up at the drive through window to the right of the building. I was in Burton for a tea, and it was only a ten-minute drive to Middlefield. I worked at Baker’s Square and am not a fan of pie crust (one summer I ate a piece of French Silk a day but would scoop out the filling and throw out the crust…), but I eat the crust on Mary Yoder’s Pies. That is a huge testament to them and makes me believe the crusts are homemade using lard or butter. The pies are pricy, but worth it. The whole butterscotch pie below was $16.99 and the whole peach pie (slice on the right) was $19.99. They last a while and are worth the quality of the ingredients.

![Image 85](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241023_135815.jpg)![Image 86](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20250713_162553.jpg)![Image 87](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20250713_162636.jpg)

They also serve family style dinners, which are a nice option if you have a group. You can choose one, two or three of their meats, and the dinners include beverages, the salad bar, mashed potatoes, gravy, dressing, a vegetable and homemade rolls (which are fluffy and yeasty). Everything is served in bowls to pass around. The price is per person depending on the meat selection (kids are a much lower per person price), and there is a minimum of 15 guests. Everyone at the table has to order it.

The gift shop is full of various tchotchkes that make a nice souvenir if you are a kid or a tourist. I always enjoy buying some fresh Amish baked goods like their breads or dinner rolls, cookies or pies. One of my friends swears by their raisin puffs (a kind of cookie). Order ahead if you want to ensure your favorites are available. The only doughnuts left at 4:30 on a Tuesday were their cream sticks.

![Image 88](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/o3.jpg)![Image 89](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20241022_165829.jpg)

Mary Yoder’s also caters to the local Amish community and has a hitching pad for the horse and buggies to the back of the parking lot. Watch out for horse and buggies on the roads too and give them a wide berth. The Whoa stop sign as you leave always cracks me up.

![Image 90](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20250712_153031.jpg)![Image 91](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/20220714_191957.jpg)

## [Crostata’s Pizzeria](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/05/01/crostatas-pizzeria/)

![Image 93](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_175924.jpg)![Image 94](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_181526.jpg)![Image 95](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_180953.jpg)

Crostata’s is a Quagliata family restaurant. The Quagliatas have 50 years of history in the restaurant business here in Cleveland. Crostata’s is a wonderful spot to enjoy Neopolitan-style pizza. I was most recently here on a Tuesday night, and it was full, which is very telling. The staff always makes you feel welcome. It is tucked in the middle of a semi-residential area and is located at the corner of Bishop Road and Wilson Mills Road.

[![Image 96](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_180152.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_180152.jpg)

The wine is served in juice glasses. I have become a fan of Sangiovese wine, so started off by ordering a glass of Sangiovese. The waitress also brought me a glass of water. As Wikipedia explains, “Sangiovese’s high acidity and moderate alcohol makes it a very food-friendly wine when it comes to food and wine pairings. One of the classic pairings in Italian cuisine is tomato-based pasta and pizza sauces with a Sangiovese-based Chianti. Varietal Sangiovese or those with a smaller proportion of the powerful, full-bodied Cabernet blended in, can accentuate the flavours of relatively bland dishes like meatloaf and roast chicken. Herb seasoning such as basil,thyme and sage play off the herbal notes of the grapes.” If you haven’t tried it you might want to give it a try.

![Image 97](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20220310_184508.jpg)![Image 98](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_184327.jpg)

I can recommend the soups. First of all, the Italian wedding soup is a great wedding soup, and the New England clam chowder was a special that I enjoyed during my most recent visit. The clam chowder was refreshing and had a lot of clams and potato chunks. The wood-fired bread stick that comes with the soup was a nice touch.

[![Image 99](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_180858.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_180858.jpg)

First off, if you like arancini then you have to order the arancini here. They are the best I have had. Arancini are Italian rice balls that are stuffed, coated with breadcrumbs and deep-fried. Crostata’s arancini are delicious. They have meat, mozzarella, and peas in them. Truly delicious with a great tomato/basil sauce. I ate one and saved the other for lunch the next day.

[![Image 100](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20220310_190319.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20220310_190319.jpg)

The first time I was here I ordered a pasta dish. They apparently make their pasta in house. It was okay, but if you want a truly outstanding meal order one of their pizzas. It is prepared in an authentic Italian style wood burning oven, which is a feature in the open kitchen behind the counter. The prices for the pizzas are also quite reasonable.

I’ve been here a couple times now and have tried a few of the pizzas. I love a good wood-fired Napolitano pizza. I love the char and appreciate being able to enjoy it with a knife and fork. The Quattro Stagioni has the four toppings, but they are mixed together on the pizza. The artichoke hearts were a little unwieldy to eat, but they were tender enough. I really enjoy the Margherita con Bufalo D.O.P., and the arugula-topped pizzas were really delicious as well.

![Image 101](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250311_182310.jpg)![Image 102](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20220310_185614.jpg)![Image 103](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20220310_185617.jpg)

## [Fish Fryday #4: Larder and The Berea Elks Lodge](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/03/29/fish-fryday-4-larder-and-the-berea-elks-lodge/)

Forgive me for posting this on Saturday, but a long chat with my best friend in Baltimore took precedence over writing about the absolutely perfect Fryday I enjoyed that day. As I noted last week, I had not enjoyed any pierogi with my fish fries yet this year, and I value a good pierogi just as much as a good fried fish. I set out to rectify this.

![Image 105](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_133328.jpg)![Image 106](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_125757.jpg)![Image 107](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_133233.jpg)

I had a delectable fried fish lunch at Larder Delicatessen & Bakery. Chef and owener Jeremy Umansky is a multi-year James Beard Award nominee, so I knew I was in for a good fish fry. Larder also has a vegan fish fry on offer, featuring fried tofu. The community table had some fun activities for kids (including a fun community cookbook from the kids who attend activities at Lake Erie Ink and some flash cards).

[![Image 108](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_125956.jpg?w=1024)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_125956.jpg)

I’d like to start off by saying that I absolutely hate the parking situation in Hingetown. And this was at around 12:30 and closer to 1. I had to drive around the block before I found an available spot near Larder – and that was because I was lucky enough that someone pulled out of their spot just as I was nearby. I lived in Germany, so I am a parallel parking pro but I know a lot of people who aren’t. The street parking situation is hit or miss. However, Larder posted that there is a parking garage at [@livechurchandstate](https://www.instagram.com/_u/livechurchandstate) that is just 20 steps from the building and is easy to access. I missed it. Consider that info filed for next time.

![Image 109](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/487466465_18398823841097708_5303517161191963825_n.jpg)![Image 110](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/485860783_18397622122097708_1020928614217191784_n.jpg)

Larder is open from 11am-6pm Tuesday thru Saturday. They stop serving hot food at 5:45 p.m. The place was packed when I got there shortly before 1, but it was manageable. I was able to place an order for the fish fry, gave the cashier my cash (and stumped him when I gave him enough to give me a $10 bill and change), was given my number and took a seat at a larger table that seems like a community table. At least we turned it into one. The group that sat down with me after I ordered had planned a trip to the Rock Hall, but had to pivot when the power went out and it closed for the day. We talked a bit about Minneapolis and chatted about the Rock Hall and Cleveland.

![Image 111](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_131219.jpg)![Image 112](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_131606.jpg)![Image 113](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_133228.jpg)

Of course I ordered the Lake Erie Fish Fry, which changes every week and this week featured fresh Lake Erie fish, fresh cut French fries, a biscuit, coleslaw made from red cabbage and the most delectable sauces. Larder gets its fresh fish out of Lake Erie from Kate’s Fish Market in the West Side Market. It seems that lunch is different from the dinner fish fry. I read somewhere that one of the fish are smelts, and the size and shape of the fish tend to lead me to believe that my lunch was fried smelt. Whatever it was it was delicious. I particularly enjoyed the sauces, and the fries were tasty as well. It was the perfect size for lunch. I was tempted to try the bread pudding or one of the tasty-looking desserts, but decided against it to save room for the evening.

![Image 114](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_181414.jpg)![Image 115](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_194021.jpg)![Image 116](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_181704.jpg)

As I said above, I knew I needed pierogi with my dinner. My friend who is an Elk suggested the Berea Elks Lodge, because they serve pierogi as well as a wide variety of changing offers. I knew where the Lodge was, because I used to drive past it all the time growing up. The fish fry is served from 6-8 p.m. I ended up heading there later in the evening to avoid the post-work traffic from the Cleveland Clinic. I got there at about 6:15 p.m. The Lodge has a smaller parking lot, but there were several parking lots nearby to handle to overflow. I initially tried to enter through the front doors, but they were locked. Apparently we had to enter through the back door and head down a stairwell to the basement. I think I was one of the last diners to show up. They were able to make room for me at the bar. They can only serve alcohol to Elks members, but that didn’t bother me. I ordered a lemonade and then later a Shirley Temple, which I haven’t had since childhood. They had just run out of the lobster ravioli, but the nice gentleman sitting next to me gave me a couple of suggestions, specifically the scallops, the salmon (Salmon Citron Chou-Fleur) and the ahi tuna nachos.

![Image 117](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_181803.jpg)![Image 118](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_181856.jpg)![Image 119](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_182046.jpg)

I ended up ordering the Scallop Symphony, which featured pan-seared scallops on a bed of crispy fried creamy polenta with southwestern corn and a roasted red pepper sauce as well as a side of pierogi (available as 2, 4 or 6 pierogi) and the Walleye Bites. The scallops won’t be available next week, so I thought it sounded fun. The fish and chips are always available. The scallops were delicious. The red pepper sauce had a bit of heat to it, but I did not find it that spicy at all compared to the Indian or Thai food I usually enjoy.

![Image 120](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_184517.jpg)![Image 121](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_190515.jpg)![Image 122](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_191741.jpg)

The pierogi and the Walleye Bites were definitely the stars through. They were both phenomenal. The pierogi were perfect and stuffed with the requisite potato and cheese filling and served with sauteed onions and sour cream. The pierogi were absolutely bursting with filling and with flavor. The Walleye Bites were also amazing. I could have eaten both of them as a meal and been happy very happy. The scent of the onions tormented me the whole drive home. There is no better smell than sauteed onions (well, maybe sauteed onions and mushrooms…)

![Image 123](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_190520.jpg)![Image 124](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_190703.jpg)![Image 125](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_190517.jpg)

The gentleman next to me had ordered the scallops and his wife ordered the salmon and they shared the cabbage and noodles, which they proclaimed was also delicious. When I saw her salmon I ordered one to go to eat later this weekend. I of course tried a bite of the salmon and asparagus with the lemon pepper sauce, and it was fantastic.

[![Image 126](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_182928.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250328_182928.jpg)

I was almost afraid to share this fantastic fish fry find, but the Exalted Ruler and my server/bartender assured me it was ok (I outed myself so that I could get their permission after I had received my food). The fish fry is staffed by volunteers (the kitchen team as well as servers, bussers, dish washers, and runners), and it isn’t like a church fish fry. I didn’t want to overwhelm them, but I also don’t think I have so much clout that there will be long lines. If you are a group of eight like the one last night you might have to wait, but they definitely can handle it. So if you want a fantastic fish fry with different choices than the usual fried fish, be sure to check it out! They will be offering it every Friday until April 18th. I’d rank this up there with St. Joseph’s Parish in Avon Lake and St. Gabriel in Concord for the variety of choices. And the pierogi is right up there with St. Josaphat, Pokrova, St. Vladimir and St. Andrew. I felt very welcome there and had a wonderful time. And I can’t wait to tuck into my leftovers tonight! This was two wonderful fish fries in one day! Best one this season so far.

## [Metroparks maple syrup event: Tree to Table brunch](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2025/03/23/metroparks-maple-syrup-event-tree-to-table-brunch/)

![Image 128](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_130515.jpg)![Image 129](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_105127.jpg)![Image 130](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_105138.jpg)

In addition to fish fries this time of year, I’m usually all about pancake breakfasts in March, but I’ve only been to one pancake breakfast so far this year. However, I attended a lovely brunch at the [Cleveland Metroparks](https://ohclevelandmetroparksweb.myvscloud.com/webtrac/web/splash.html?_csrf_token=cj031E0T0F053S2M1L3N2Q4K5X4B535B016A626H550E5P45655F1H5U6A4T4Y085R3X5E4W1B014K634P0I5Q4M5M4K045R4M5T57725R625B5W6U615X5E6Q0X5H4U5E) yesterday. I follow the Metroparks on Facebook in addition to getting their email newsletter and have attended several of their cooking classes in the past. I signed up for this event as soon as it was announced, and I’m glad I did because another attendee told me her mother wanted to go but waited four days only to find out it was sold out so she came on her own. The menu sounded amazing, and the price of $35 was good for the amount of food. They also offered vegetarian options, switching mushroom for the pork and tofu instead of the shrimp.

![Image 131](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_105133.jpg)![Image 132](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_105122.jpg)![Image 133](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_105325.jpg)

I had gotten a fish fry at the Emerald Necklace Marina during Covid and enjoyed it, so I knew the brunch would be a treat. I got there about 15 minutes before the 11 a.m. start time and was able to quickly check in, grab a maple-inspired cocktail using my provided drink ticket (I opted for coffee with Bailey’s and maple syrup) and grab a seat. I sat with a bunch of lovely people who made me feel welcome despite being by myself (again, I wasn’t the only one). One of the women had tried all three cocktails and stated that the Maple Syrup Mimosa was the best of the three, but they were all good. The other drink on offer was a Maple Syrup Old Fashioned, and there was a mocktail (below) as well as beer and wine to choose from.

![Image 134](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_111722.jpg)![Image 135](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_110419.jpg)![Image 136](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_110647.jpg)

The atmosphere was cozy on a cold and gray day. There was a fire burning in the fireplace, and there were three long tables to choose from. I chose a spot near the coffee. Priorities. There was a PowerPoint presentation running on a screen with lots of fun facts about maple syrup and maple sugaring.

[![Image 137](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_110125.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_110125.jpg)

To start, the servers came around with small shot glasses of sap water, which was a refreshing start. Sap water is more water-like than syrup-like, and the ‘sap water’ that is collected from maple trees is boiled down to make syrup. It takes 40 gallons of sap to make 1 gallon of syrup. There is a long tradition in Ohio of collecting sap that started with the Native Americans in the area. We were told that we are lucky enough to live in an area that is ideally suited for maple syruping. The snowy cold weather (and it started snowing a bit as I was driving to the event) after several days of warmer weather encourages the sap to flow from the roots to the leaves in the trees our area, and Ohio is ranked fifth in maple syrup production. We live in the 0.005% of the earth that produces sap and maple syrup (I’m fairly sure that percentage is correct, but I could be wrong – but it is a very miniscule percentage of the earth’s land). So our ‘Cleveland winters’ are good for maple syrup production.

![Image 138](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_111135.jpg)![Image 139](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_112009.jpg)

The starters were served quickly and professionally. The food was served on small biodegradable plates (it is the Metroparks after all). We started with homemade focaccia bread with a maple cinnamon butter, quickly followed by roasted butternut squash soup with goat cheese, chili-infused maple and pepita. Both were delicious. The bread was fluffy, yet tender and was a nice delivery for the butter. The butter was so good I made sure to eat it all, and the soup was excellent. Everything in the soup was extremely well balanced, with nothing overpowering the other ingredients. The crunchy pepita were an excellent foil to the creamy soup.

[![Image 140](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_114210.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_114210.jpg)

We weren’t sure what to expect with three entrees listed. Would they be served together on a plate or served individually? I was most looking forward to the roasted garlic and herb pork tenderloin, which ended up being the first entree served despite being second on the menu. It did not disappoint! The “spinach, bacon and apple bread pudding” was a fantastic complement to the pork, which was perfectly cooked. It was topped with a delectable cider and maple butter sauce and crispy fried onions. I’m glad they served it first because I still had room to enjoy every single bite of it. I picked a bit at the next entrees, and one of my fellow diners asked for a box for hers. There was not a single thing on the plate I did not enjoy. I would go to a restaurant to order it!

[![Image 141](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_115243.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_115243.jpg)

The brussels sprouts in the Sambal and Maple Shrimp entree was my favorite ‘bite’ in the second entree served, although the plump shrimp were also really great and not too sweet. Each diner was served three perfect shrimp. The vegetables were chopped very small and roasted together. The puffed rice were also fun, it was nicely seasoned, and the entire dish as a whole was quite tasty.

[![Image 142](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_121925.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_121925.jpg)

The Pain Perdu with poached apple and smoked bleu cheese with pecan crumble was also quite delightful. Essentially a small square of French toast, it was perfectly prepared and well balanced. Bleu cheese can be quite overpowering, but this was the perfect amount to cut through the eggy french toast and complemented the poached apple. You could definitely taste the fennel in the maple/fennel reduction that was drizzled over the pain perdu, but it was also not overpowering and just offered a hint of fennel.

[![Image 143](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_123632.jpg?w=840)](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_123632.jpg)

One of my tablemates had to leave to go see _& Juliet_ at the Playhouse, which is fantastic and I was so happy that she got to see it (and it turns out about four or five of my friends were also at that show yesterday from the posts of Facebook), but she was able to enjoy the pain perdu and the crème brulee before she had to leave early to make it on time. I gave her fiancé my business card because I enjoyed talking to them so much. The Maple Crème Brulee with berry sauce and whipped cream was a delightful finish to an excellent meal. We then enjoyed a presentation on the history of maple syruping and maple syruping in the Metroparks, complete with props like collection bags and buckets, filters and a yoke that they wore to carry buckets of sap (an lots of photos of kids wearing the yoke). I would not have been surprised to see me among the photos of kids learning about maple syrup, because my mother took my sister and I to many educational events at the Metroparks when we were little and I definitely remember maple syrup production being one of them. We are so lucky to have the Metroparks for all of the educational as well as recreational activities!

![Image 144](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_123643.jpg)![Image 145](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_123730.jpg)![Image 146](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/20250322_124604.jpg)

Hopefully they will offer this event again, because it was fantastic. Be sure to [follow the Metroparks on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/ClevelandMetroparks) or get their email newsletter. And sign up as soon as you see it, because it sells out quick. All of their cooking events are also a fun time (I’ve attended a pie iron class and a pot pie class, among others), so keep an eye out for their events. They offer lots of different free and fee-based events (crafts, hikes, recreational classes, camping trips, etc.) in addition to cooking and food events, so if you haven’t checked them out be sure to do so! The Cleveland Metroparks rocks! Don’t be afraid to attend on your own, because everyone was very friendly, and we chatted the whole time about various topics. I left shortly after 1:00 to meet some girlfriends at Sangria y Tapas (I ordered a sangria and soup) and was full the entire day. The entire day! This meal (and specifically the pork tenderloin) will definitely be among my Best Bites in 2025.

And be sure to check out the Cleveland Metropark fish fries! Guests can dine-in at Big Met or get carry-out at Sleepy Hollow and [Emerald Necklace Cafe](https://clevelandrocksclevelandeats.com/2020/06/12/fish-fry-friday-2020-emerald-necklace-marina-big-met-to-go/). Merwin’s Wharf will also have fish fry specials every Friday. The Fish Fry takes place on Fridays from 3 to 7 p.m. through April 11 this year.

# Americano Bistro to close Bratenahl Place restaurant on September 26

*   Updated: Sep. 15, 2015, 8:47 p.m.
*   |Published: Sep. 15, 2015, 7:47 p.m.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](link_3)

13yDININGb.jpg

Fans of the Crisp Calamari With Two Sauces, one of Americano Bistro's most popular appetizers, have only a few more days to enjoy the dish. The restaurant, located in One Bratenahl Place, Bratenahl, will close Saturday, Sept. 26.

A subscription is required to read this story.  
[Subscribe now to continue.](link_4)

_(Thomas Ondrey)_

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Americano Bistro, tucked away in a space on the ground level of One Bratenahl Place in one of Northeast Ohio's most exclusive addresses, will serve its final meals on Saturday, Sept. 26. "Our inability to secure a lease" has led to the closure, operator Cole Davis, president of VC Dining and Drinks Inc., said in a prepared statement.

Representatives for the condominium board would offer no comment for the decision not to offer another lease.

Vytauras Sasnauskas, Davis' former partner in the restaurant and Americano's chef, took to Facebook to express his feelings on the loss.

"Americano was my home, my baby and my 2nd family. I gave everything I've got over 7 years there," Sasnauskas wrote. He stepped away from the restaurant in January for personal reasons, he added.

But Sasnauskas will be back on the restaurant's patio later today, from 5 to 7 p.m., preparing the restaurant's signature hand-made pizzas. They're offered only on Tuesdays, on Americano's patio and in the bar and lounge areas - meaning that the last Americano's Pizza Cafe will be held Sept. 22.

MORE BY JOE CREA

[A farewell from Joe Crea, longtime food-and-dining critic for cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer May. 4, 2017, 1:50 p.m.](link_6)

[20 'Cleveland Classics' from the 2016 A-List Dining Guide: A photo tour Jun. 21, 2016, 1:00 p.m.](link_7)

In the statement, Davis indicated that he is seeking another location to "create another unique dining experience." Vytauras' Facebook posting invites old friends to come say goodbye and support the restaurant's staff.

Meanwhile, Davis and company intend to conduct a sale of the restaurant's collection of wine. Sales will be held from 5 to 7 p.m. Thursdays, September 17 and 24.

_**CLOSING Sept. 26:** Americano Bistro, 1 Bratenahl Place, Bratenahl; [americanocleveland.com,](link_8)216-541-3900. Bar and lounge hours are 4 p.m. to 12 a.m. Monday through Saturday. Dining room hours are 5 to 10 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday. Closed Sunday. When you arrive at the gated community, stop at the guard stand and tell the guard you're visiting the restaurant, and you'll be permitted entrance._

[Joe Crea](link_3)

[jcrea@cleveland.com](mailto:jcrea@cleveland.com)

# Arancini restaurant will replace Americano Bistro at One Bratenahl Place

*   Updated: Sep. 16, 2015, 5:24 p.m.
*   |Published: Sep. 16, 2015, 4:24 p.m.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](link_5)

50 Things

Arancini, balls of rice that are stuffed and deep-fried, lend their name to the new restaurant opening sometime in October at the One Bratenahl Place condominium complext in Bratenahl.

A subscription is required to read this story.  
[Subscribe now to continue.](link_6)

_(Lisa DeJong, The Plain Dealer)_

MORE BY JOE CREA

[A farewell from Joe Crea, longtime food-and-dining critic for cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer May. 4, 2017, 1:50 p.m.](link_8)

[20 'Cleveland Classics' from the 2016 A-List Dining Guide: A photo tour Jun. 21, 2016, 1:00 p.m.](link_9)

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Americano Bistro at[One Bratenahl Place](link_10) in Bratenahl will be replaced by a new restaurant, Arancini, early next month. Americano [will serve its final meals on Saturday, Sept. 26.](link_11) The restaurant's operators, VC Dining and Drinks Inc., announced the closing, saying their lease had not been renewed by the board of directors of the One Bratenahl Place Association.

The Bratenahl Place board broke the news on the new restaurant in a recent letter to tenants. "We have signed an agreement with a new operator who will take over beginning October 1, 2015," the board wrote in the letter. "The new restaurant, known as Arancini, will open for business following a brief closure in early October, while the operator and chef finalize their menu, inventory and staff."

One Bratenahl Place board members added that full details of the new restaurant's management team would be introduced at an open meeting of condominium occupants on Thursday, Sept. 24 and in a formal announcement.

# Last Meals Being Served at Americano in Bratenahl

![Image 3: Avatar photo](https://www.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/cropped-doug-at-never-say-dive-scaled-1-96x96.jpg)[Douglas Trattner](https://www.clevescene.com/author/dougtrattner/)September 16, 2015 August 12, 2025

### Share this:

For a restaurant as difficult to find as Americano – located beyond a gatehouse and inside an exclusive lakefront condo building that frowned upon signage and advertising – this wonderful little bistro managed to make a lot of diners very happy. The Euro-American bistro run by partners Cole Davis and chef Vytauras Sasnauskas had a good run, too, one which will cease following dinner service on September 26th after a little more than seven years.

Owner Davis explained that his inability to secure a long-term commitment with the condo board led him to the painful decision to close his first – but likely not last – restaurant.

“This is heartbreaking to us, as we have so enjoyed serving delicious meals and drinks to you over the past 7-plus years, and deeply wanted to continue,” Cole wrote to Americano’s Facebook followers. “Despite massive effort on both parts, the board has decided to go in a new direction with the restaurant.”

There is still time to show your support by dining at the restaurant (One Bratenahl Pl., 216-541-3900) before closing night. A great time to swing by might be for one of the popular Americano Pizza Café nights (Tuesday 5-7 p.m. weather permitting) or one of the Fantastic Big Wine Sales (Thursdays 5-7 p.m.).

Back in June, we broke the news of chef-partner Vytauras Sasnauskas’ plans to open Citizen Pie, a Neapolitan-style pizzeria and café across the street from the Beachland Ballroom in Collinwood. Sasnauskas’ partners in the venture are Claudia Young and Velvet Tango Room owner Paulius Nasvytis. The latest estimates place opening day in October.

# A farewell from Joe Crea, longtime food-and-dining critic for cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer

*   Updated: May. 04, 2017, 1:50 p.m.
*   |Published: May. 04, 2017, 12:50 p.m.

![Image 1](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/22610266-large.jpg)

Joe Crea

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/jcrea/ "Joe Crea, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- "Don't bury the lede." That's one of the most basic tenets of journalism - and I've been reminded of it many times.

So here it is. This is my last column for cleveland.com and, by extension, The Plain Dealer.

I'm leaving a job I've loved for most of my so-called adult life. Actually, since I was a kid. My first story was published in The Ford Flash, my junior high paper, when I was 12 years old. I've never quit, through high school and college, and 35 years of daily news publications. (And I've always said what I have to say publicly, using my own name and mug shot.)

Anyway, I've resisted announcing my departure -- really, even saying it out loud to friends -- because to do so makes it seem too real. So final.

Close friends, however, know the backstory.

About a year ago, I heard the words that would freak out just about any sane person.

"It's cancer. And you need to know that it's progressing rapidly."

Oh, swell.

So for starters, if you've been wondering why you haven't heard much from me and where I've disappeared to these last 12 or 13 months, it's the Seidman Cancer Center at University Hospitals. Their care has been extraordinary.

Without undue whining, it's fair to say that this has been the single worst year of my life: a parade of scans and X-rays and blood work, chemotherapy and radiation -- over and over. Four hospitalizations. Endless hours in waiting rooms, endless miles on the road. More blind alleys than a Moroccan market.

Cancer, I've discovered, is the gift that keeps on... taking. Every time you turn around it seems you're blindsided by a wholly unanticipated wrinkle or side effect.

Anyone who's ever strolled that thorny trail or has accompanied a loved one down that path is bound to agree: Cancer does, indeed, suck.

But it's also a rare, if weird, gift.

For starters, I quickly realized that how well-off I truly am. Like, at least I can grasp what's going on. I'm not a bewildered 6-year-old or someone forced to go it alone. Someone who can't afford aspirin, let alone health insurance allowing first-class oncology care. I have a beautiful wife who's been with me every step of the way, and a reliable car to get me back and forth. I'm surrounded by family, supported by bosses who haven't batted an eye, and cheered by friends who've checked in, brought soup, cheered and mocked me (good-naturedly, mostly) as only true friends can.

And I've been one of the lucky ones. At this moment in time I'm doing reasonably well. "Cautiously optimistic" is how my main doc frames it.

Of course, only a fool dares believe that he or she is "cured." Not where cancer is concerned. Seems there's always that other shoe, waiting to drop.

Undeniably, each day is a gift. Even the lousiest ones. (PS: I hope you'll join me in supporting and praying for everyone enduring this often seemingly endless battle.)

My cancer journey brought a crucial epiphany. No words are quite as sobering as those that one surgeon spoke. "If we can't get our arms around this thing, we're looking at four to 18 months..."

Whoa. Seriously? You talkin' to ME, doc?

That was when mortality threw a very harsh spotlight. Granted, each of us has his or her expiration date -- vague and unspecified. Maybe I'm wrong, but I believe everyone ought to be fortunate enough to get that kind of cosmic tap on the shoulder.

Gradually I realized that for all the usual excuses, pragmatic reasoning and foot-dragging, it's high time for doing all those things I've yammered on about. Spending more time with my family. Writing my essays, novels and other books. Seeing more of the world. Being a better friend, a better citizen.

Anyway, leaving your job isn't the same as retiring, right?

Stepping down from a wonderful position doesn't mean I've shelved the keyboard and tossed out my pen.

I'm already working on new stories and hope to continue to contribute to cleveland.com. There may even be a blog in my future.

For 18 years I've been a voice in the Northeast Ohio food and restaurant scene, and that has been a really good gig. I've reported on and have come to know, and respect -- and often like -- a great many chefs and restaurateurs.

There is boundless culinary talent in our region -- home cooks high among them -- not to mention the growers and other producers, the many bakers and brewers, farm markets, retailers, advocates... and yes, writers and other "foodies."

It truly has been an honor to cast a light on our region's burgeoning and ever-surprising dining scene. I've no intention of disappearing. I'll keep in touch. And I hope you will, too.

If you're up to it, I'd love for you to join me at 6 p.m. Wednesday, May 10, at Music Box Cleveland, where I'll be talking about "How Cleveland Became Such a Foodie Town," part of the Cleveland Stories Dinner Party Series, presented by the Cleveland History Center. (Admission is free, though a three-course meal is available for $20 per person. Dining reservations are required. Find out more on musicboxcle.com)

In any event, I've no intention of disappearing. Which reminds me of one of my all-time favorite song titles, from Dan Hicks and the Hot Licks: "How Can I Miss You If You Don't Go Away?"

So... thank you all for the boundless support, and for the constructive criticism. For the matzo ball soup, for the hospital-bedside kvetching, for the comfort of coffee, calls, cards and emails. For your friendship. For reading what I've had to share.

MORE BY JOE CREA

[20 'Cleveland Classics' from the 2016 A-List Dining Guide: A photo tour Jun. 21, 2016, 1:00 p.m.](link_9)

[20 best Italian restaurants in Greater Cleveland: 2016 A-List Dining Guide Jun. 14, 2016, 1:51 p.m.](link_10)

As with every aspect of life it really is... well, whatever you make of it. So my walk off ends with a favorite line from Dr. Seuss:

Don't cry because it's over. Smile because it happened.

# 20 'Cleveland Classics' from the 2016 A-List Dining Guide: A photo tour

*   Updated: Jun. 21, 2016, 1:00 p.m.
*   |Published: Jun. 21, 2016, 12:00 p.m.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/jcrea/ "Joe Crea, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Earning a["Cleveland Classics"](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2016/06/2016_a-list_20_classic_cleveland_restaurants_photos.html#0) designation on the[2016 A-List Dining Guide](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2016/06/clevelands_top_100_restaurants_the_complete_2016_a-list_photos.html) is a very special honor. But it's more than simply a spot on an honor roll. "Cleveland Classics" recognizes area eateries that are the true cornerstones of Northeast Ohio's culinary scene. These are long-standing businesses that, day in and out, satisfy diners' hunger for excellence: a combination of creative and well-executed cuisine coupled with polished service, inviting decor and a welcoming ambiance. And do so, year after year.

We're honored to be able to acknowledge the 20 restaurateurs that bring so much to the area's dining community. More than anything -- beyond the peerless dining experiences they provide -- it's a nod of appreciation for the high bar they set, the level of consistency they represent, the quiet contributions they make in supporting local charities and the ways so many mentor young chefs while helping to shape Greater Cleveland's future restaurant scene.  Longevity is only a facet of a truly "classic" restaurant. You might say staying classy is the real measure of their staying power.

Cleveland.com photographers Joshua Gunter and John Kuntz visited all of the restaurants on the 2016 "Classics" list, taking new photos of food, decor and more. Be sure to check out their work in the gallery above. For a complete rundown on the "Cleveland Classics" restaurants, with more photos, reviews & more, check out [the 2016 A-List Dining Guide.](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2016/06/clevelands_top_100_restaurants_the_complete_2016_a-list_photos.html)

Wing Week is going mobile! Click or scan below to download the app.

![Image 37](https://clevelandwingweek.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2024/07/Cleveland-Wing-Week-2024-300x300.jpg)

### Enter To Win

Use the official Cleveland Wing Week [mobile app](https://clevelandwingweek.com/#app) to check in to 4 participating restaurants and be entered into a drawing to win $250 in gift cards. No purchase necessary.

### Locations

### COMMANDMENTS

##### **1. THEY COULD RUN OUT**

We expect that the restaurants will be busy. So, if a place runs out toward the end of a shift, handle it like an adult, go back the next day, earlier, order your wings and thank them for working hard. Please be nice to our restaurants.

##### **2. THERE WILL LIKELY BE WAITS**

People have been taking about Wing Week for months. Don't be surprised if restaurants have waits. In fact, be surprised if they don't.

##### **3. TIP LIKE A PRO**

$10 brings out the cheap in all of us, so please tip at least 20%. The people who are serving you are working harder during Wing Week than an average week. A kind word will also be welcome - these people are our friends and neighbors.

#### **4. YOU SHOULD BUY A DRINK AND/OR OTHER FOOD**

Purchase of sides and extras are not a requirement, but we think it says a lot to those working hard to bring you an extraordinary experience. Grab some fries or a Great Lakes Brewing Company beer, and say thanks!

#### **5. CHECK SOCIAL MEDIA**

Restaurants will be encouraged to post their waits and remaining wings for the day on their social platforms. Also don't forget to share and tag your photos with #ClevelandWingWeek.

#### **6. DINE IN & TAKE OUT OPTIONS**

While Wing Week was designed to be dine in only, some restaurants may be offering take out options as well. Make sure to double check the Official Wing Week App to confirm which locations offer carry-out and which locations are dine-in only.

![Image 2: Image: Best of Cleveland 2014](https://media1.clevescene.com/clevescene/imager//best-of-cleveland-2014/u/magnum/4298231/boc_teaser.png?cb=1768934360)

Cleveland is a pretty damn great place to live. You know that in your heart, which is why you've stuck around and made yourself a nice life here, but every once in awhile it's nice to be reminded of that glorious fact. That's the mission of Best of Cleveland, the issue that we turn over to you, the reader. After all, who knows better what makes Cleveland so damn great.

This year, we asked you to help us identify Cleveland's royalty -- the ambitious people, the indispensable places, the bold ventures, the breathtaking developments, the luxurious services, the powerful leaders and the sumptuous feasts. We are all connected in these ventures in some way, and we are all -- each and every one of us -- royalty.

After weeks of voting, you crowned over 190 winners. Actual crowns would be far too expensive to give out, so instead we give you this free magazine, which you can fold up and wear like a crown if you're in the mood. It's worth its weight in gold, either way.

Enjoy, and thank you. We are forever humble and grateful,

Your devoted subjects at Scene.

![Image 4: Image: Welcome to Best of Cleveland 2015](https://media1.clevescene.com/clevescene/imager/welcome-to-best-of-cleveland-2015/welcome-to-best-of-cleveland-2015/u/magnum/4550545/boc_ig_cover_final.webp?cb=1768934359)

Made in Cleveland. It's a stamp of pride, it's a motto, it describes who we are and what we do. And it's a simple phrase that was the North Star for this issue.

Every year we roll out the Best of Cleveland, and every year the list of winners changes and evolves along with the city.

We took a look back at Best of Clevelands from years past in preparation for this edition, and while they are indelible nostalgic snapshots of a time and place we remember fondly, they are also reminders of just how far we've come since.

The dining scene has exploded. The arts scene has matured. Whole neighborhoods have popped up where little more than empty storefronts once existed. The brewery scene's scope is only rivaled by its quality. Young professionals are not only returning here, they are staying here without ever dipping out in the first place. The whole country, it seems, is finally in agreement that Cleveland is somewhere everyone should visit, if not settle down in permanently.

We made that happen. It was no accident.

We've always been a city of makers. It was steel and manufacturing at one point. That's still here, of course, but there's oh so much more. We've built something new entirely.

Best of Cleveland is our chance to recognize the people and businesses that drove that renaissance. And when we asked you to help us pick the best of the best, you didn't disappoint. Over four weeks of voting, tens of thousands of ballots were cast. Thank you for that. You know this city better than anyone else. You are, after all, what makes Cleveland.

Best of Cleveland Twenty Thirteen voting is officially over and in the books – this book, to be exact.

The people have spoken.

For five weeks, readers cast the vote – over 35,000 in all– to let their voices be heard.

You selected the people, places, things and ideas that are pushing Cleveland forward as we all look to the future and ask, “What’s next?”

From the chefs cranking out world-class food to the folks running our favorite dive bars, from new businesses to Cleveland landmarks and institutions, this is who you – the reader – voted as the winners of Best of Cleveland 2013. Enjoy.

# 20 best Italian restaurants in Greater Cleveland: 2016 A-List Dining Guide

*   Published: Jun. 14, 2016, 6:51 p.m.

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/jcrea/ "Joe Crea, cleveland.com")

![Image 1](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571348-standard.jpg)

Not too long ago, dinner at an Italian restaurant meant a platter of spaghetti big enough to feed an army, large green salads and a basket of crusty bread. You can still find plenty of reliable places that offer hearty Italian-American fare -- but today you're just as likely to find authentic and artfully composed regional cuisine from Tuscany, Milan, Bologna, even Compobasso and Calabria. These days, chefs with Italian heritage (or simply a penchant for the diverse nuances of dishes from the peninsula) offer a spectrum of flavors.

Here are 20 great restaurants from the 2016 A-List guide to to Northeast Ohio's Top 100 restaurants with Italian cuisine as a centerpiece on the menu. The 2016 list includes Aldo's, Bruno's, Cibreo, Corleone's, D'Agneses, DC Pasta Company, Eddie's Pizzeria Cerino, Flour, Giovanni's, Johnny's Bar, Johnny's Downtown, La Campagna, Lago, Lockkeepers, Luca, Michaelangelo's, Stino Da Napoli, Trentina and Vero Pizzeria.

**Best Italian Restaurants in Greater Cleveland**

Joe Crea

cleveland.com

**Aldo's**

[Aldo's Restaurant](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2010/04/aldos_in_brooklyn_a_comfortable_family-style_recipe_with_a_big_emphasis_on_fine_preparations.html), 8459 Memphis Ave., Brooklyn, 216-749-7060: Enthusiastic appreciation for well-executed Italian classics and an ever-changing menu of fresh dishes (especially seafood) make this small, noisy spot the place for a cheerful evening. $$-$$$, major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

![Image 3](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571576-standard.jpg)

_Lisa DeJong , The Plain Dealer_

**Bruno's Ristorante**

[Bruno's Ristorante,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/brunos_ristorante_clevelands_classic_italian_neighborhood_restaurant.html)2644 West 41st St. (one-way north between I-90 and Clark Avenue), Cleveland, 216-961-7087, [brunosristorante.net](http://www.brunosristorante.net/):Bruno DiSiena left the Cleveland Browns as executive chef when it looked like they were leaving town. Our advantage. This is Cleveland's red-sauce capital, especially with pasta and eggplant. The room is charming in a homestyle way, but tiny. Expect eavesdropping to be part of the deal. Reservations a must near the weekend. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian-American _(Debbi Snook, The Plain Dealer)_

**Cibreo Italian Kitchen**

[Cibreo Italian Kitchen,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/cibreo_italian_kitchen_tuscan_country_in_downtown_cleveland.html)1438 Euclid Ave. (Playhouse Square), Cleveland, 216-862-9212, [cibreocleveland.com](http://thedriftwoodgroup.com/restaurants/cibreo-italian-kitchen/): Rich pastas, buttery cheeses, crisp pan-fried fish and tender braised meats in a Tuscan countryside setting- just across from Playhouse Square. Convenient, though a little chaotic, for before theater dining, a quiet respite if you choose to eat while everyone else is at the show. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. _(Beth Segal, Special to cleveland.com)_

Great selection of steaks, veal, pastas and sauces. $$-$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. _(Bob Migra, Special to cleveland.com)_

[D'Agnese's,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2012/04/dagneses_serving_quintessential_italian-american_cuisine_treated_with_respect.html)1100 W. Royalton Road, Broadview Heights, 440-237-7378, [dagneses.com](http://dagneses.com/): It's easy to understand why so many food-savvy Italians of my acquaintance frequent this relative hideaway. It's one of those rare spots you look forward to revisiting - for the unvarnished pleasure of well-prepared fare (especially the seafood, lamb and veal) served in a genial atmosphere. $$-$$$, all major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Traditional Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

Gather friends and pass the plates. The combined and skillful team of Dante Boccuzzi (Dante, Ginko, DBA) and Carmella DelBusso (Oggi and the former Portofino) - are the "D" and "C" in the name. $$-$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian _. (Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

_Gus Chan, The Plain Dealer_

**Eddie's Pizzeria Cerino**

[Eddie's Pizzeria Cerino,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2010/04/eddies_pizzeria_cerino_does_just_about_everything_right.html)7305 Broadview Road, Seven Hills, 216-236-6007, [pizzeriacerino.com](http://www.pizzeriacerino.com/): Quality Italian fare, perfect pizzas, modest prices and a comfortable atmosphere have patrons flocking to Eddie's in Seven Hills. $$, all major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Italian, pizza. _(Bob Migra, Special to cleveland.com)_

![Image 9](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571640-standard.jpg)

_Allison Carey, The Plain Dealer_

**Flour**

[Flour,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2012/04/flour_the_food_might_not_be_rustic_italian_but_its_good.html)34205 Chagrin Blvd., Moreland Hills; 216-464-3700, flourrestaurant.com: Flour bills itself as an Italian kitchen, "polished, sophisticated and urbane" eatery and "starkly modern" (zinc-topped tables, cement floor, gray walls). Executive chef Matt Mytro and chef-owner Paul Minnillo anchor the menu with fresh pastas (like Lobster Strozzapretti, with pancetta and bone marrow), solid starters and wood-fired pizzas. Great monthly featured dishes as well. $$-$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Modern Italian. _(Peter Chakerian, Special to cleveland.com)_

_Thomas Ondrey, The Plain Dealer_

**Giovanni's Ristorante**

[Giovanni's Ristorante,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/giovannis_in_beachwood_remains_a_bastion_of_old_world_elegance_excellence.html) 25550 Chagrin Blvd., Beachwood; 216-831-8625,[giovanniscleveland.com:](http://www.giovanniscleveland.com/) Old World charm heightened by exceptional cuisine, tableside preparations and exacting service combine to make dining at Giovanni's a singular experience. Truly, a classic. $$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

Don't Edit

_John Kuntz, cleveland.com_

**Johnny's Bar**

[Johnny's Bar,](http://www.thegreenhousetavern.com/)3164 Fulton Road, Cleveland, 216-281-0055,[johnnyscleveland.com:](http://www.johnnyscleveland.com/) Head to the original restaurant on Fulton Road for upscale Italian, seafood and pasta. Johnny's has not slipped a bit. The menu is still dotted with many of the favorites from 20 years ago, dishes like grilled long-bone veal chop, cold-smoked filet mignon, and a variety of pastas and seafood specialties. $$$$, all major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Italian. _(Bob Migra, Special to cleveland.com)_

_Gus Chan, The Plain Dealer_

**Johnny's Downtown**

**[Johnny's Downtown,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2011/04/johnnys_downtown_a_grand_destination_for_a_power_lunch_or_people_watching.html)**1406 West Sixth St., Cleveland (Warehouse District); 216-623-0055,[johnnyscleveland.com.](http://www.johnnyscleveland.com/) Sister stop to the original Johnny's Bar on Fulton, Downtown launched in 1993 in a refurbished, mid-19 th century building that once housed a general store. Cozy, upscale environs, piano music in the bar, and appeal to the upscale and business crowds, Johnny's Italian menu is anchored by steaks, chops, veal, fish and pastas. Bonuses: two wine cellar-like private rooms and a grape selection that has earned them Wine Spectator's Award of Excellence. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian with Steaks, Chops, Seafood._(Peter Chakerian, Special to cleveland.com)_

![Image 13](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571658-standard.jpg)

_Lisa DeJong, The Plain Dealer_

**La Campagna**

[La Campagna,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/03/at_la_campagna_in_westlake_its_like_nonna_is_in_the_kitchen_--_except_maybe_even_better.html)27337 Detroit Road (just west of Dover Center Road), Westlake; 440-871-1771,[lacampagnaonline.net](https://www.facebook.com/pages/La-Campagna/154280371251147): Rarely have I found Italian food as lusty and nuanced. Rather than leaning heavily on the garlic-and-oregano crutch, chef-owner Carmella Fragassi coaxes all sorts of flavor from a broad battery of ingredients. Here, the menu changes more-or-less daily. Though you're likely to find a handful of offerings carrying over from day to day, Fragassi hews to the old-world tradition of embracing both the season and ... well, whatever looks good in the market. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian._(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. (_David Farkas, Special to cleveland.com)_

![Image 15](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571695-standard.jpg)

_Lisa DeJong, The Plain Dealer_

**Lockkeepers**

[Lockkeepers,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/04/lockkeepers_affordable_options_and_sophisticated_fare_meet_in_valley_view.html)8001 Rockside Road, Valley View; 216-524-9404, [lockkeepers.com:](http://www.lockkeepers.com/) Affordable options and sophisticated fare meet on an Italian-inspired menu by Venetian native chef Alberto Leandri at this restaurant in Valley View. Traditional dishes, modern interpretations and house-made pastas merge here. Portions are generous, and likely will leave enough for lunch. $$$. All major credit cards: Cuisine: Italian. _(David Farkas, Special to cleveland.com; updated by Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

Don't Edit

Don't Edit

![Image 16](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571715-standard.jpg)

_Gus Chan, The Plain Dealer_

**Luca Italian Cuisine**

[Luca Italian Cuisine,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/11/luca_sits_atop_the_superior_viaduct_offering_stunning_views_and_a_menu_of_posh_dishes_luxurious_tast.html)2100 Superior Viaduct, Cleveland, 216-862-2761, [lucacleveland.com](http://www.lucacleveland.com/): Who knew Cleveland was so beautiful? From the windows of this luxe ristorante perched on top of the Superior-Viaduct bridge, the night-time city shimmers in urban splendor. The food is just as glamorous, big bowls of sweet succulent shellfish, massive slow roasted boar shanks, black and white striped ravioli stuffed with lobster, divinely decadent tiramisu. Almost everything here is deluxe, but chef/owner Luca Sema knows how to make it fun without pretense or stuffiness. He seems to be operating the very clubbiest of chic clubs. And every one with the wherewithal is welcome to bask in the cosmopolitan luster that makes it one of the most glamorous places in town. $$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. _(Beth Segal, Special to cleveland.com)_

![Image 17](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571718-standard.jpg)

_Plain Dealer File Photo_

**Michaelangelo's**

[Michaelangelo's,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2010/04/michaelangelos_on_murray_hill_exemplary_contemporary_italian_cuisine_in_an_exquisitely_understated_d.html) 2198 Murray Hill Road, Cleveland, 216-721-0300, mangelos.com. Italian fare beyond the familiar? Few restaurants in town rival Michaelangelo's. Chef Michael Annandono treats humble or glorious fare with equal respect. Terrific pastas (especially the stuffed varieties), boldly flavorful sautes and toothsome braised meats are highlights. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

Don't Edit

![Image 18](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571725-standard.jpg)

_Plain Dealer File Photo_

**Stino da Napoli**

[Stino da Napoli,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/04/stino_da_napoli_timeless_yet_fresh_1.html)19070 Old Detroit Road, Rocky River, 440-331-3944, [stinodanapoli.com](http://stinodanapoli.com/): Classic and creative pastas (generally excellent sauces; the smoky Vesuvio is memorable) and interesting veal, chicken and tilapia dishes (especially a version that combines a beautifully sauteed filet with three perfect shrimp) populate Stino's menu. A procession of specials are daily highlights. The chef's version of Veal Marsala should be the template for all others. $$-$$$, no credit cards, cash or check only. Cuisine: Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

# Paris Wolfe, cleveland.com

Paris Wolfe covers Cleveland’s food scene for cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer. She writes about the people and businesses behind the food, as well as the traditions, cultures and neighborhoods that shape how Northeast Ohio eats. Her reporting also examines the changes affecting local restaurants, grocery stores, farms and food businesses. Follow Paris for stories about the people, places and forces shaping Cleveland’s food culture.

# Alex Darus, cleveland.com

Alex is a food and culture writer on cleveland.com's life and culture team, primarily covering restaurants, bars, spirits, beer, wine, entertainment, and cooking. She's interviewed notable chefs both local and beyond and writes many of cleveland.com's food and drink guides. Alex started as an intern on the life and culture team before joining the staff full-time in 2023. She is a graduate of Ohio University's E.W. Scripps School of Journalism and its student-run newspaper The Post. When she isn't working, Alex can often be found at a happy hour in her native Lakewood, joined by her Cavalier King Charles named Martini.

# Last Meals Being Served at Americano in Bratenahl

![Image 3: Avatar photo](https://www.clevescene.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/cropped-doug-at-never-say-dive-scaled-1-96x96.jpg)[Douglas Trattner](https://www.clevescene.com/author/dougtrattner/)September 16, 2015 August 12, 2025

For a restaurant as difficult to find as Americano – located beyond a gatehouse and inside an exclusive lakefront condo building that frowned upon signage and advertising – this wonderful little bistro managed to make a lot of diners very happy. The Euro-American bistro run by partners Cole Davis and chef Vytauras Sasnauskas had a good run, too, one which will cease following dinner service on September 26th after a little more than seven years.

Owner Davis explained that his inability to secure a long-term commitment with the condo board led him to the painful decision to close his first – but likely not last – restaurant.

“This is heartbreaking to us, as we have so enjoyed serving delicious meals and drinks to you over the past 7-plus years, and deeply wanted to continue,” Cole wrote to Americano’s Facebook followers. “Despite massive effort on both parts, the board has decided to go in a new direction with the restaurant.”

There is still time to show your support by dining at the restaurant (One Bratenahl Pl., 216-541-3900) before closing night. A great time to swing by might be for one of the popular Americano Pizza Café nights (Tuesday 5-7 p.m. weather permitting) or one of the Fantastic Big Wine Sales (Thursdays 5-7 p.m.).

Back in June, we broke the news of chef-partner Vytauras Sasnauskas’ plans to open Citizen Pie, a Neapolitan-style pizzeria and café across the street from the Beachland Ballroom in Collinwood. Sasnauskas’ partners in the venture are Claudia Young and Velvet Tango Room owner Paulius Nasvytis. The latest estimates place opening day in October.

Cleveland is a pretty damn great place to live. You know that in your heart, which is why you've stuck around and made yourself a nice life here, but every once in awhile it's nice to be reminded of that glorious fact. That's the mission of Best of Cleveland, the issue that we turn over to you, the reader. After all, who knows better what makes Cleveland so damn great.

This year, we asked you to help us identify Cleveland's royalty -- the ambitious people, the indispensable places, the bold ventures, the breathtaking developments, the luxurious services, the powerful leaders and the sumptuous feasts. We are all connected in these ventures in some way, and we are all -- each and every one of us -- royalty.

After weeks of voting, you crowned over 190 winners. Actual crowns would be far too expensive to give out, so instead we give you this free magazine, which you can fold up and wear like a crown if you're in the mood. It's worth its weight in gold, either way.

Enjoy, and thank you. We are forever humble and grateful,
