_(Thomas Ondrey)_

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Americano Bistro, tucked away in a space on the ground level of One Bratenahl Place in one of Northeast Ohio's most exclusive addresses, will serve its final meals on Saturday, Sept. 26. "Our inability to secure a lease" has led to the closure, operator Cole Davis, president of VC Dining and Drinks Inc., said in a prepared statement.

Representatives for the condominium board would offer no comment for the decision not to offer another lease.

Vytauras Sasnauskas, Davis' former partner in the restaurant and Americano's chef, took to Facebook to express his feelings on the loss.

"Americano was my home, my baby and my 2nd family. I gave everything I've got over 7 years there," Sasnauskas wrote. He stepped away from the restaurant in January for personal reasons, he added.

But Sasnauskas will be back on the restaurant's patio later today, from 5 to 7 p.m., preparing the restaurant's signature hand-made pizzas. They're offered only on Tuesdays, on Americano's patio and in the bar and lounge areas - meaning that the last Americano's Pizza Cafe will be held Sept. 22.

In the statement, Davis indicated that he is seeking another location to "create another unique dining experience." Vytauras' Facebook posting invites old friends to come say goodbye and support the restaurant's staff.

Meanwhile, Davis and company intend to conduct a sale of the restaurant's collection of wine. Sales will be held from 5 to 7 p.m. Thursdays, September 17 and 24.

_**CLOSING Sept. 26:** Americano Bistro, 1 Bratenahl Place, Bratenahl; [americanocleveland.com,](http://www.americanocleveland.com/index.html)216-541-3900. Bar and lounge hours are 4 p.m. to 12 a.m. Monday through Saturday. Dining room hours are 5 to 10 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday. Closed Sunday. *   Published: Jun. 14, 2016, 6:51 p.m.

By 
*   [Joe Crea, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/jcrea/ "Joe Crea, cleveland.com")

![Image 1](https://image.cleveland.com/home/cleve-media/width2048/img/ent_impact_home/photo/20571348-standard.jpg)

Not too long ago, dinner at an Italian restaurant meant a platter of spaghetti big enough to feed an army, large green salads and a basket of crusty bread. You can still find plenty of reliable places that offer hearty Italian-American fare -- but today you're just as likely to find authentic and artfully composed regional cuisine from Tuscany, Milan, Bologna, even Compobasso and Calabria. These days, chefs with Italian heritage (or simply a penchant for the diverse nuances of dishes from the peninsula) offer a spectrum of flavors.

Here are 20 great restaurants from the 2016 A-List guide to to Northeast Ohio's Top 100 restaurants with Italian cuisine as a centerpiece on the menu. The 2016 list includes Aldo's, Bruno's, Cibreo, Corleone's, D'Agneses, DC Pasta Company, Eddie's Pizzeria Cerino, Flour, Giovanni's, Johnny's Bar, Johnny's Downtown, La Campagna, Lago, Lockkeepers, Luca, Michaelangelo's, Stino Da Napoli, Trentina and Vero Pizzeria.

**Aldo's**

[Aldo's Restaurant](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2010/04/aldos_in_brooklyn_a_comfortable_family-style_recipe_with_a_big_emphasis_on_fine_preparations.html), 8459 Memphis Ave., Brooklyn, 216-749-7060: Enthusiastic appreciation for well-executed Italian classics and an ever-changing menu of fresh dishes (especially seafood) make this small, noisy spot the place for a cheerful evening. $$-$$$, major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

**Bruno's Ristorante**

[Bruno's Ristorante,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/brunos_ristorante_clevelands_classic_italian_neighborhood_restaurant.html)2644 West 41st St. (one-way north between I-90 and Clark Avenue), Cleveland, 216-961-7087, [brunosristorante.net](http://www.brunosristorante.net/):Bruno DiSiena left the Cleveland Browns as executive chef when it looked like they were leaving town. Our advantage. This is Cleveland's red-sauce capital, especially with pasta and eggplant. The room is charming in a homestyle way, but tiny. Expect eavesdropping to be part of the deal. Reservations a must near the weekend. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian-American _(Debbi Snook, The Plain Dealer)_

**Cibreo Italian Kitchen**

[Cibreo Italian Kitchen,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/cibreo_italian_kitchen_tuscan_country_in_downtown_cleveland.html)1438 Euclid Ave. (Playhouse Square), Cleveland, 216-862-9212, [cibreocleveland.com](http://thedriftwoodgroup.com/restaurants/cibreo-italian-kitchen/): Rich pastas, buttery cheeses, crisp pan-fried fish and tender braised meats in a Tuscan countryside setting- just across from Playhouse Square. Convenient, though a little chaotic, for before theater dining, a quiet respite if you choose to eat while everyone else is at the show. $$$. All major credit cards. **D'Agnese's**

[D'Agnese's,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2012/04/dagneses_serving_quintessential_italian-american_cuisine_treated_with_respect.html)1100 W. Royalton Road, Broadview Heights, 440-237-7378, [dagneses.com](http://dagneses.com/): It's easy to understand why so many food-savvy Italians of my acquaintance frequent this relative hideaway. It's one of those rare spots you look forward to revisiting - for the unvarnished pleasure of well-prepared fare (especially the seafood, lamb and veal) served in a genial atmosphere. $$-$$$, all major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Traditional Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

**Flour**

[Flour,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2012/04/flour_the_food_might_not_be_rustic_italian_but_its_good.html)34205 Chagrin Blvd., Moreland Hills; 216-464-3700, flourrestaurant.com: Flour bills itself as an Italian kitchen, "polished, sophisticated and urbane" eatery and "starkly modern" (zinc-topped tables, cement floor, gray walls). Executive chef Matt Mytro and chef-owner Paul Minnillo anchor the menu with fresh pastas (like Lobster Strozzapretti, with pancetta and bone marrow), solid starters and wood-fired pizzas. Great monthly featured dishes as well. $$-$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Modern Italian. _(Peter Chakerian, Special to cleveland.com)_

**Johnny's Bar**

[Johnny's Bar,](http://www.thegreenhousetavern.com/)3164 Fulton Road, Cleveland, 216-281-0055,[johnnyscleveland.com:](http://www.johnnyscleveland.com/) Head to the original restaurant on Fulton Road for upscale Italian, seafood and pasta. Johnny's has not slipped a bit. The menu is still dotted with many of the favorites from 20 years ago, dishes like grilled long-bone veal chop, cold-smoked filet mignon, and a variety of pastas and seafood specialties. $$$$, all major credit cards accepted. Cuisine: Italian. _(Bob Migra, Special to cleveland.com)_

**Johnny's Downtown**

**[Johnny's Downtown,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2011/04/johnnys_downtown_a_grand_destination_for_a_power_lunch_or_people_watching.html)**1406 West Sixth St., Cleveland (Warehouse District); 216-623-0055,[johnnyscleveland.com.](http://www.johnnyscleveland.com/) Sister stop to the original Johnny's Bar on Fulton, Downtown launched in 1993 in a refurbished, mid-19 th century building that once housed a general store. Cozy, upscale environs, piano music in the bar, and appeal to the upscale and business crowds, Johnny's Italian menu is anchored by steaks, chops, veal, fish and pastas. Bonuses: two wine cellar-like private rooms and a grape selection that has earned them Wine Spectator's Award of Excellence. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian with Steaks, Chops, Seafood._(Peter Chakerian, Special to cleveland.com)_

**La Campagna**

[La Campagna,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/03/at_la_campagna_in_westlake_its_like_nonna_is_in_the_kitchen_--_except_maybe_even_better.html)27337 Detroit Road (just west of Dover Center Road), Westlake; 440-871-1771,[lacampagnaonline.net](https://www.facebook.com/pages/La-Campagna/154280371251147): Rarely have I found Italian food as lusty and nuanced. Rather than leaning heavily on the garlic-and-oregano crutch, chef-owner Carmella Fragassi coaxes all sorts of flavor from a broad battery of ingredients. Here, the menu changes more-or-less daily. Though you're likely to find a handful of offerings carrying over from day to day, Fragassi hews to the old-world tradition of embracing both the season and ... well, whatever looks good in the market. $$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian._(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

**Lockkeepers**

[Lockkeepers,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/04/lockkeepers_affordable_options_and_sophisticated_fare_meet_in_valley_view.html)8001 Rockside Road, Valley View; 216-524-9404, [lockkeepers.com:](http://www.lockkeepers.com/) Affordable options and sophisticated fare meet on an Italian-inspired menu by Venetian native chef Alberto Leandri at this restaurant in Valley View. **Luca Italian Cuisine**

[Luca Italian Cuisine,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/11/luca_sits_atop_the_superior_viaduct_offering_stunning_views_and_a_menu_of_posh_dishes_luxurious_tast.html)2100 Superior Viaduct, Cleveland, 216-862-2761, [lucacleveland.com](http://www.lucacleveland.com/): Who knew Cleveland was so beautiful? From the windows of this luxe ristorante perched on top of the Superior-Viaduct bridge, the night-time city shimmers in urban splendor. The food is just as glamorous, big bowls of sweet succulent shellfish, massive slow roasted boar shanks, black and white striped ravioli stuffed with lobster, divinely decadent tiramisu. Almost everything here is deluxe, but chef/owner Luca Sema knows how to make it fun without pretense or stuffiness. He seems to be operating the very clubbiest of chic clubs. And every one with the wherewithal is welcome to bask in the cosmopolitan luster that makes it one of the most glamorous places in town. $$$$. All major credit cards. Cuisine: Italian. _(Beth Segal, Special to cleveland.com)_

**Michaelangelo's**

[Michaelangelo's,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2010/04/michaelangelos_on_murray_hill_exemplary_contemporary_italian_cuisine_in_an_exquisitely_understated_d.html) 2198 Murray Hill Road, Cleveland, 216-721-0300, mangelos.com. Italian fare beyond the familiar? Few restaurants in town rival Michaelangelo's. Chef Michael Annandono treats humble or glorious fare with equal respect. Terrific pastas (especially the stuffed varieties), boldly flavorful sautes and toothsome braised meats are highlights. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

**Stino da Napoli**

[Stino da Napoli,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2013/04/stino_da_napoli_timeless_yet_fresh_1.html)19070 Old Detroit Road, Rocky River, 440-331-3944, [stinodanapoli.com](http://stinodanapoli.com/): Classic and creative pastas (generally excellent sauces; the smoky Vesuvio is memorable) and interesting veal, chicken and tilapia dishes (especially a version that combines a beautifully sauteed filet with three perfect shrimp) populate Stino's menu. A procession of specials are daily highlights. The chef's version of Veal Marsala should be the template for all others. $$-$$$, no credit cards, cash or check only. Cuisine: Italian. _(Joe Crea, cleveland.com)_

[Trentina,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/12/sawyers_trentina_in_cleveland_a_shimmering_showcase_for_flavor_adventures.html) 1903 Ford Drive, Cleveland. 216-421-2900; [restauranttrentina.com](http://www.restauranttrentina.com/): Here is a kitchen that looks deeply -- although not exclusively -- into terroir, that French term for the unique results a local chef can craft from the local landscape. Jonathon Sawyer, his wife Amelia, and his staff are on it, with influence from Northern Italy and Germany on the plate that pose flavors so different, so challenging, many of them create a sense of wonder and contemplation. $$-$$$$; all major credit cards. **Vero Pizzeria**

[Vero Pizzeria,](http://www.cleveland.com/top-restaurants/index.ssf/2014/04/vero_pizza_napoletana_delivers_authenticity_in_cleveland_heights.html)12421 Cedar Rd. (Cedar Fairmount), Cleveland Heights, 216-229-8383, [verocleveland.com](http://verocleveland.com/): Stylish, svelte and flash-baked in a 900 degree firewood oven, Vero's pies raise the craft of Neapolitan pizza-making into a fine, and delicious, art. When the restaurant is full, the wait can be long, but there's a variety of beautifully constructed meat and cheese boards, well-designed salads and veggie dishes to hold your interest. $$-$$$. Most major credit cards. Cuisine: Pizza, Contemporary Bistro. _(Beth Segal, Special to cleveland.com)_

# Americano Original Great Lakes Bistro: Reviving classic bistro food in a retro setting in Bratenahl

*   Updated: Apr. 22, 2010, 5:00 p.m.
*   |Published: Apr. 22, 2010, 4:00 p.m.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Special to The Plain Dealer](link_5)

![Image 1: americano.jpg](http://media.cleveland.com/dining-guide/photo/americanojpg-23af500c1ecbd715_medium.jpg)Thomas Ondrey, The Plain Dealer Crisp Calamari from Americano Bistro, One Bratenahl Place. 

Bistro food gets a fresh take at this Bratenahl favorite.

**[Americano](link_6)**

A subscription is required to read this story.  
[Subscribe now to continue.](link_7)

[Bratenahl Place, Bratenahl](link_8)

There always has been a restaurant of some sort in 1 Bratenahl Place, the posh 1960s-vintage condominium building where Americano resides. Years ago, most of the restaurants were private; Americano is a public restaurant. The staff wears jeans and you are encouraged to do so. The food is fresh and original in its rethinking of classic bistro food and other fare.

The Clay Pot Baked Shrimp ($10) is not the usual porridgey shrimp and grits. Six big, plump crustaceans nestle in a rich tomato-wine sauce, surrounded by dollops of creamy polenta and kernels of fresh sweet corn. A generous slice of house-made grilled bread is there to mop up every delicious, beautiful morsel. Just as good is the Crisp Calamari With Two Sauces ($9). Perfectly deep-fried, tender-fat rings and tentacles are served with a refreshing side of citrus-dressed mesclun.

You'll find a wealth of wonders among the entrees. The Salmon With Vodka Sauce ($17) features succulent salmon perched on a bed of house-made pumpernickel cavatelli and a melange of just-sauteed tomato, spinach and potato.

There's just room for a kind word about the posh and sweetly Seared Scallops ($23), though not the accompanying wild rice/wild mushroom risotto, which had a gummy texture. And the root-beer-bourbon-sauced Char-Grilled Strip Steak ($20), with chef Vytauras Sasnauskas' crisp frites, had a tender richness. -- _Beth Segal_

[READ THE FULL REVIEW](link_9)

![Image 2: A_List_decal_2010.jpg](http://media.cleveland.com/dining-guide/photo/a-list-decal-2010jpg-3e8b448f5e901296_small.jpg)

**Contact:** 216-541-3900.

**Online**: [Americanocleveland.com.](link_6)

**Hours**: Dinner, 5-10 p.m. Tuesday-Saturday; bar and lounge, 4 p.m.-midnight Monday-Saturday.

**Prices**: Appetizers, $7-$10; entrees, $16-$23; desserts, $5.

**Reservations**: Yes.

**Credit cards**: All major.

**Cleanliness**: Sparkling.

**Kid-friendliness**: Nothing specific, but eager to please.

**Quality of service**: Mostly excellent, though sometimes uneven.

**Noise level**: Nice and quiet.

# Great Lakes Brewing Co., Edwins Restaurant, Saucy Brew Works: WTAM 5-minute food-drinks chat

*   Updated: Mar. 07, 2023, 11:50 a.m.
*   |Published: Jan. 13, 2021, 5:15 a.m.

![Image 1: It’s all about new things this week on our regular WTAM food and drinks chat. Bill Wills and I talk about new beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes through Edwins Restaurant.](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/Z2CSPIBISZG57NCPU7ASWEGWJQ.jpg?auth=511e49cbdfea81fc851e5b984419785210de0d482c02357a962900e7feb31b71&width=1280&smart=true&quality=90)

It’s all about new things this week on our regular WTAM food and drinks chat. Bill Wills and I talk about new beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes through Edwins Restaurant.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Marc Bona, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/ "Marc Bona, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio – On our 5-minute weekly chat on food and drinks on [WTAM](https://advancelocal-my.sharepoint.com/personal/mbona1_advancelocal_net/Documents/wtam.iheart.com), Bill Wills and I cover three new things in the culinary world in Greater Cleveland: New beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes offered online via Edwins Restaurant.

**Great Lakes Brewing Co.’s beer-release calendar is out**

Great Lakes Brewing Co. is out with its beer-release calendar for 2021, and the state’s first craft brewery has a couple of new brews in the works, including Crushworthy, a low-calorie wheat beer, a new India Pale Ale, a new variety pack and more. Here are all the details about what is coming out and when: [About Great Lakes Brewing Co.’s beer-release calendar](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/01/great-lakes-brewing-cos-2021-beer-release-calendar-is-out.html)

**Edwins Restaurant launches virtual cooking classes**

Edwins has started Vivant @ Home, a virtual cooking class to demystify meal preparation and to show how making a healthy meal doesn’t have to take a lot of time. It also will aim to offer family- or date-night dinner inspiration. Here’s more on the classes: [About Edwins’ virtual classes](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/01/edwins-launches-virtual-cooking-classes.html)

**Saucy Brew Works expanding to Independence**

Saucy Brew Works had a lot going on in 2020, and the folks behind the brewery are continuing that busy pace. They are set to break ground on a brewery-brewpub-event center adjacent to Topgolf in Independence. # Nick Camino of WKYC offers favorite dining choices - Five for Friday

*   Updated: Mar. 07, 2023, 12:44 p.m.
*   |Published: Mar. 11, 2021, 5:30 a.m.

![Image 1: For this week’s Five for Friday, Nick Camino of WKYC offers his favorite dining choices throughout Northeast Ohio. (Marissa Camino Photography)](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/NJQMX3UL6ZHXPJEONA45SDHCLI.jpg?auth=0e72e2d48910ed88fdbecb3a90662468525eec83de6290d616afa3384b755d22&width=1280&smart=true&quality=90)

For this week’s Five for Friday, Nick Camino of WKYC offers his favorite dining choices throughout Northeast Ohio. (Marissa Camino Photography )

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Marc Bona, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/ "Marc Bona, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio – Nick Camino has been a steady fixture for years anchoring sports in Cleveland. He gained a bit of fame at the beginning of the coronavirus pandemic when WKYC staffers broadcast from their homes. Camino talked sports from his kitchen.

And what a kitchen. It was spotless and minimalistic. A large shiny pot here, one or two tasteful pieces of décor there. But not one speck of, well, anything resembling dirt or grime.

Camino – who went to Solon High School and Cleveland State University - hosted sports talk shows for 13 years on WTAM 1100-AM and has been full time at WKYC as sports anchor/reporter since 2019. He and his family – wife Marissa and sons Giovanni and Rocco - live in Twinsburg.

Each week we survey a notable Clevelander about where they like to eat in Northeast Ohio. Here are Camino’s choices:

**1. What’s your favorite restaurant and why?**

This is a tough question, because we enjoy going out to eat at a variety of different places. I have to go with [Angelo’s Nido Italia](https://www.nidoitalia.com/) in Little Italy (12020 Mayfield Road, Cleveland). It’s the best Italian spot in Cleveland. Menu is fantastic, love the atmosphere, too. Angelo does an A+ job all-around from the appetizer to the dessert.

**2. Favorite dish you have ordered from anywhere?**

The Tuscan Ribeye from [Bull & Bird Steakhouse](https://bullandbirdsteakhouse.com/) (87 West St.) in downtown Chagrin Falls is the best steak I’ve had. It was part of Hyde Park Restaurant Group. But if you’re heading to Angelo’s Nido Italia from above, I highly recommend the Veal Tuscano. His potato gnocchi in tomato cream sauce is top-notch, too. (Note: Bull & Bird is now closed.)

**3. Favorite dish to make at home?**

OK, so I can’t cook. It’s embarrassing. But my wife Marissa is incredible in the kitchen. Right up there with Nana Camino and my mom. Obviously we do a lot of Italian in our house. Pizzas, pastas, meatballs, meatless meatballs (mushroom/bread crumbs), all that good stuff. But we do have variety. Recently Marissa started doing Chicken Tikka Masala over rice with naan bread, which is an Indian dish. We also enjoy good Chinese food. My wife makes fried rice a lot with homemade General Tso chicken and also a Bourbon Chicken.

**4. What is your favorite brunch or breakfast spot?**

Good question! Two places that actually remind me of each other. Old-school diners. [Fresh Start Diner](http://thefreshstartdiner.com/) (9810 Ravenna Road, Twinsburg) is the first. Dan (Wyman) and his dad do a great job. I used to run into Les Levine there all the time. So you know if Les was there, it was a great spot. Another good place is [Jim’s Open Kitchen](https://www.facebook.com/jimsopenkitchen/) (33779 Aurora Road, Solon).

**5. Favorite drink or dessert in Northeast Ohio?**

For good cocktails, [M Italian](https://www.mitalian.com/) (22 W. Orange St., Chagrin Falls). Fresh-squeezed Limoncello Mules are awesome. For dessert, you can’t go wrong at [Red, the Steakhouse](https://www.google.com/search?client=firefox-b-1-d&q=Red%2C+the+Steakhouse+) (200 Park Ave., Orange Village, Pinecrest development) with their fried dough. It’s like a fresh, Italian doughnut.

# Americano Original Great Lakes Bistro: Reviving classic bistro food in a retro setting in Bratenahl

*   Updated: Apr. 22, 2010, 5:00 p.m.
*   |Published: Apr. 22, 2010, 4:00 p.m.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Special to The Plain Dealer](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/clevepdspeci/ "Special to The Plain Dealer")

![Image 1: americano.jpg](http://media.cleveland.com/dining-guide/photo/americanojpg-23af500c1ecbd715_medium.jpg)Thomas Ondrey, The Plain Dealer Crisp Calamari from Americano Bistro, One Bratenahl Place. 

Bistro food gets a fresh take at this Bratenahl favorite.

**[Americano](http://www.americanocleveland.com/)**

A subscription is required to read this story.  
[Subscribe now to continue.](https://www.cleveland.com/digitalsubscription/intercept?failsafe=true)

[Bratenahl Place, Bratenahl](http://maps.google.com/maps?f=q&source=s_q&hl=en&geocode=&q=1+Bratenahl+Place,+Bratenahl&sll=41.501331,-81.595195&sspn=0.006412,0.013583&ie=UTF8&hq=&hnear=1+Bratenahl+Pl,+Bratenahl,+Cuyahoga,+Ohio+44108&z=16)

There always has been a restaurant of some sort in 1 Bratenahl Place, the posh 1960s-vintage condominium building where Americano resides. Years ago, most of the restaurants were private; Americano is a public restaurant. The staff wears jeans and you are encouraged to do so. The food is fresh and original in its rethinking of classic bistro food and other fare.

The Clay Pot Baked Shrimp ($10) is not the usual porridgey shrimp and grits. Six big, plump crustaceans nestle in a rich tomato-wine sauce, surrounded by dollops of creamy polenta and kernels of fresh sweet corn. A generous slice of house-made grilled bread is there to mop up every delicious, beautiful morsel. Just as good is the Crisp Calamari With Two Sauces ($9). Perfectly deep-fried, tender-fat rings and tentacles are served with a refreshing side of citrus-dressed mesclun.

You'll find a wealth of wonders among the entrees. The Salmon With Vodka Sauce ($17) features succulent salmon perched on a bed of house-made pumpernickel cavatelli and a melange of just-sauteed tomato, spinach and potato.

There's just room for a kind word about the posh and sweetly Seared Scallops ($23), though not the accompanying wild rice/wild mushroom risotto, which had a gummy texture. And the root-beer-bourbon-sauced Char-Grilled Strip Steak ($20), with chef Vytauras Sasnauskas' crisp frites, had a tender richness. -- _Beth Segal_

# Nick Camino of WKYC offers favorite dining choices - Five for Friday

*   Updated: Mar. 07, 2023, 12:44 p.m.
*   |Published: Mar. 11, 2021, 5:30 a.m.

![Image 1: For this week’s Five for Friday, Nick Camino of WKYC offers his favorite dining choices throughout Northeast Ohio. (Marissa Camino Photography)](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/NJQMX3UL6ZHXPJEONA45SDHCLI.jpg?auth=0e72e2d48910ed88fdbecb3a90662468525eec83de6290d616afa3384b755d22&width=1280&smart=true&quality=90)

For this week’s Five for Friday, Nick Camino of WKYC offers his favorite dining choices throughout Northeast Ohio. (Marissa Camino Photography )

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Marc Bona, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/ "Marc Bona, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio – Nick Camino has been a steady fixture for years anchoring sports in Cleveland. He gained a bit of fame at the beginning of the coronavirus pandemic when WKYC staffers broadcast from their homes. Camino talked sports from his kitchen.

And what a kitchen. It was spotless and minimalistic. A large shiny pot here, one or two tasteful pieces of décor there. But not one speck of, well, anything resembling dirt or grime.

Camino – who went to Solon High School and Cleveland State University - hosted sports talk shows for 13 years on WTAM 1100-AM and has been full time at WKYC as sports anchor/reporter since 2019. He and his family – wife Marissa and sons Giovanni and Rocco - live in Twinsburg.

Each week we survey a notable Clevelander about where they like to eat in Northeast Ohio. Here are Camino’s choices:

**1. What’s your favorite restaurant and why?**

This is a tough question, because we enjoy going out to eat at a variety of different places. I have to go with [Angelo’s Nido Italia](https://www.nidoitalia.com/) in Little Italy (12020 Mayfield Road, Cleveland). It’s the best Italian spot in Cleveland. Menu is fantastic, love the atmosphere, too. Angelo does an A+ job all-around from the appetizer to the dessert.

**2. Favorite dish you have ordered from anywhere?**

The Tuscan Ribeye from [Bull & Bird Steakhouse](https://bullandbirdsteakhouse.com/) (87 West St.) in downtown Chagrin Falls is the best steak I’ve had. It was part of Hyde Park Restaurant Group. But if you’re heading to Angelo’s Nido Italia from above, I highly recommend the Veal Tuscano. His potato gnocchi in tomato cream sauce is top-notch, too. (Note: Bull & Bird is now closed.)

**3. Favorite dish to make at home?**

OK, so I can’t cook. It’s embarrassing. But my wife Marissa is incredible in the kitchen. Right up there with Nana Camino and my mom. Obviously we do a lot of Italian in our house. Pizzas, pastas, meatballs, meatless meatballs (mushroom/bread crumbs), all that good stuff. But we do have variety. Recently Marissa started doing Chicken Tikka Masala over rice with naan bread, which is an Indian dish. We also enjoy good Chinese food. My wife makes fried rice a lot with homemade General Tso chicken and also a Bourbon Chicken.

**4. What is your favorite brunch or breakfast spot?**

Good question! Two places that actually remind me of each other. Old-school diners. [Fresh Start Diner](http://thefreshstartdiner.com/) (9810 Ravenna Road, Twinsburg) is the first. Dan (Wyman) and his dad do a great job. I used to run into Les Levine there all the time. So you know if Les was there, it was a great spot. Another good place is [Jim’s Open Kitchen](https://www.facebook.com/jimsopenkitchen/) (33779 Aurora Road, Solon).

**5. Favorite drink or dessert in Northeast Ohio?**

For good cocktails, [M Italian](https://www.mitalian.com/) (22 W. Orange St., Chagrin Falls). Fresh-squeezed Limoncello Mules are awesome. For dessert, you can’t go wrong at [Red, the Steakhouse](https://www.google.com/search?client=firefox-b-1-d&q=Red%2C+the+Steakhouse+) (200 Park Ave., Orange Village, Pinecrest development) with their fried dough. It’s like a fresh, Italian doughnut.

_What do notable Clevelanders eat when they want some good chow? Welcome to_ _**Five for Friday**_ _- a weekly look at Northeast Ohioans and their favorite eats._

# Great Lakes Brewing Co., Edwins Restaurant, Saucy Brew Works: WTAM 5-minute food-drinks chat

*   Updated: Mar. 07, 2023, 11:50 a.m.
*   |Published: Jan. 13, 2021, 5:15 a.m.

![Image 1: It’s all about new things this week on our regular WTAM food and drinks chat. Bill Wills and I talk about new beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes through Edwins Restaurant.](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/Z2CSPIBISZG57NCPU7ASWEGWJQ.jpg?auth=511e49cbdfea81fc851e5b984419785210de0d482c02357a962900e7feb31b71&width=1280&smart=true&quality=90)

It’s all about new things this week on our regular WTAM food and drinks chat. Bill Wills and I talk about new beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes through Edwins Restaurant.

*    See more of our coverage in your search results  Set as Google Preferred Source 

By 
*   [Marc Bona, cleveland.com](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/ "Marc Bona, cleveland.com")

CLEVELAND, Ohio – On our 5-minute weekly chat on food and drinks on [WTAM](https://advancelocal-my.sharepoint.com/personal/mbona1_advancelocal_net/Documents/wtam.iheart.com), Bill Wills and I cover three new things in the culinary world in Greater Cleveland: New beers at Great Lakes Brewing Co., a new location for Saucy Brew Works, and new cooking classes offered online via Edwins Restaurant.

**Great Lakes Brewing Co.’s beer-release calendar is out**

Great Lakes Brewing Co. is out with its beer-release calendar for 2021, and the state’s first craft brewery has a couple of new brews in the works, including Crushworthy, a low-calorie wheat beer, a new India Pale Ale, a new variety pack and more. Here are all the details about what is coming out and when: [About Great Lakes Brewing Co.’s beer-release calendar](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/01/great-lakes-brewing-cos-2021-beer-release-calendar-is-out.html)

**Edwins Restaurant launches virtual cooking classes**

Edwins has started Vivant @ Home, a virtual cooking class to demystify meal preparation and to show how making a healthy meal doesn’t have to take a lot of time. It also will aim to offer family- or date-night dinner inspiration. Here’s more on the classes: [About Edwins’ virtual classes](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/01/edwins-launches-virtual-cooking-classes.html)

**Saucy Brew Works expanding to Independence**

Saucy Brew Works had a lot going on in 2020, and the folks behind the brewery are continuing that busy pace. They are set to break ground on a brewery-brewpub-event center adjacent to Topgolf in Independence. Here’s more about the ambitious plan: [About Saucy’s deal in Independence](https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/01/saucy-brew-works-moving-ahead-with-independence-brewery-pub-event-space.html)

## FAQ

### How do I measure distance between two addresses?

Search for your first address using the search bar to navigate to it, then click on the map to drop a point. Search for your second address and click again. The direct distance appears instantly in both kilometers and miles. Choose Drive, Walk, or Bike to compare a road- or path-following route and estimated travel time.

### Can I compare driving, walking, biking, and straight-line distance?

Yes. Direct mode measures straight-line distance (as the crow flies) using the Haversine formula. Drive, Walk, and Bike modes follow the relevant OpenStreetMap road and path network and show both route distance and estimated travel time.

### How accurate is the measurement?

The Haversine formula is accurate to within **0.5%** for most distances. It uses the Earth's mean radius of 6,371 km and treats the Earth as a perfect sphere. For everyday use: real estate, delivery zones, travel planning: the margin is negligible.

### What is straight-line distance used for?

Straight-line distance is useful whenever you need proximity regardless of roads: comparing locations, defining approximate delivery or service zones, estimating flight distances, and planning outdoor activities. Always confirm official school, property, or legal boundaries with the responsible authority.

### Can I measure a multi-stop route?

Yes. Click to place as many points as you need. The tool sums up all the straight-line segments and shows a total path distance along with per-segment distances. Drag any point to fine-tune its position.

### Can I measure area on a map?

Yes. Place at least 3 points, then click **Close shape** in the panel. You'll see both perimeter and enclosed area in m², km², and acres. This is useful for rough planning and visualization, not as a legal boundary or professional survey.

### Can I measure distances between cities or countries?

Yes: the tool works for any two points on Earth. For reference: New York to London is approximately **5,570 km** (3,460 miles) straight-line; Los Angeles to Tokyo is roughly **8,815 km** (5,478 miles). Simply search for each city and click to place your points.

### What is the Haversine formula?

The Haversine formula is a trigonometric equation that calculates the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere from their latitude and longitude. It accounts for the Earth's curvature and returns the shortest surface path.

### Can I share a measurement?

Yes. Click the Share button to copy a link. The link encodes all your points and the current map view: anyone who opens it sees the exact same measurement. No account required on either end.

### Can I switch between km and miles?

Yes. The distance panel shows both units simultaneously. Use the **km** and **mi** buttons in the toolbar to choose which unit is shown as the primary value.

### How do I undo or remove a point?

Click the Undo button in the toolbar to remove the last placed point, or press **Backspace** on your keyboard. Click **Clear all** to start over from scratch.

## Distance Between Two Addresses: Free Online Calculator

This free tool compares direct, driving, walking, and cycling distance between any two addresses on an interactive map. Enter both addresses, then switch modes to see the route, distance, and estimated travel time in kilometers or miles. No account or download required: it works directly in your browser.

## How to Measure the Distance Between Two Addresses

1.   **Search for your first address**: type it into the search bar at the top of the page and press Enter. The map will navigate to that location.
2.   **Click to place a point**: click on the map to drop a numbered marker at your first address.
3.   **Search for your second address**: type the destination into the search bar and navigate there.
4.   **Click to place the second point**: the direct distance is calculated instantly and displayed in both kilometers and miles.
5.   **Compare travel modes**: choose Drive, Walk, or Bike to follow the relevant road and path network and see an estimated travel time.
6.   **Share your measurement**: click Share to copy a link that anyone can open to see the exact same measurement.

## What Is Straight-Line Distance?

Direct distance measures the distance between points. It does not follow roads or paths. Select Drive, Walk, or Bike to see a route and an estimated travel time.

## Common Uses for Address Distance Calculation

*   **Real estate**: compare distances from a property to nearby schools, shops, or work. Select Walk to measure a walking route.
*   **Logistics and delivery**: define service zones or check whether a delivery address is within a set radius of a depot.
*   **Travel planning**: estimate straight-line flight distances or compare the proximity of hotels and attractions.
*   **Outdoor activities**: measure hiking or cycling routes where roads aren't the constraint.
*   **Property surveys**: measure boundary perimeters and land parcel areas in acres or m².

## Tool Features at a Glance

*   **Dual address input**: type both addresses into the From / To form and click Calculate Distance. The map automatically places both points and shows the result.
*   **Direct, Drive, Walk, and Bike modes**: compare the shortest direct distance with road-following driving, pedestrian, and cycling routes and estimated travel times.
*   **Click-to-place mode**: click anywhere on the map to drop a numbered waypoint. Drag any marker to fine-tune its position.
*   **Multi-stop paths**: add as many intermediate waypoints as you need. Each segment distance is listed individually, and the panel shows the running total.
*   **Area measurement**: close a polygon with three or more points to calculate enclosed area in m², km², and acres alongside perimeter.
*   **Shareable links**: select Share to copy a link to your measurement. The recipient can open it without an account.
*   **km / miles toggle**: both units are shown simultaneously; use the toolbar buttons to set which appears as the primary value.
*   **Globe view and multiple map styles**: switch between standard street map, light, and topographic views, or enable the 3-D globe projection.

## Tips for Getting Accurate Results

*   **Use full addresses rather than just city names** when precision matters (e.g., for school catchment checks or property boundary work). Check each marker on the map. Search results can place it at an entrance, a nearby street, or the center of an area.
*   **Zoom in before clicking** to place points. The closer the zoom level, the more accurately your click lands on the intended location.
*   **Drag waypoints after placing them**: you don't need to undo and redo. Every marker is draggable; the distances update in real time as you move it.
*   **Use Close shape for land parcels**: once you trace a property boundary with three or more points and close the polygon, area in acres is shown instantly. Useful for estimating lot size when official survey documents aren't available.
*   **Compare like with like**: use Direct for proximity or flight estimates, Drive for road trips, Walk for pedestrian paths, and Bike for cycle-friendly routes.

## More Reference Distances Between Well-Known Locations

*   New York to Los Angeles: **3,940 km** (2,450 miles)
*   London to Paris: **340 km** (211 miles)
*   New York to London: **5,570 km** (3,460 miles)
*   Sydney to Melbourne: **714 km** (444 miles)
*   Los Angeles to Tokyo: **8,815 km** (5,478 miles)
*   Mumbai to Delhi: **1,148 km** (713 miles)
*   Toronto to Montreal: **504 km** (313 miles)
*   Berlin to Vienna: **524 km** (326 miles)
*   Dubai to Singapore: **5,840 km** (3,629 miles)
*   São Paulo to Buenos Aires: **1,750 km** (1,087 miles)
*   Chicago to Houston: **1,515 km** (941 miles)
*   Amsterdam to Brussels: **174 km** (108 miles)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Is this tool free?Yes. The distance calculator is completely free to use with no account required. Unlimited measurements, shareable links, and area calculation are all included at no cost.Does it work on mobile?Yes. The tool is fully responsive and works on iOS and Android browsers. Tap to place points, pinch to zoom, and share measurements directly from your phone.Can I measure area as well as distance?Yes. After placing three or more points, click Close shape to close the polygon. The tool shows perimeter and enclosed area in m², km², and acres.How many points can I add?There is no hard limit. You can add dozens of waypoints to measure multi-stop routes. Each segment's individual distance is shown alongside the total path length.Can I measure the distance between two countries or continents?Yes. Search for each city or landmark and place a point. Direct distance can measure across oceans; it does not show a travel route.How is this different from Google Maps distance?This tool keeps direct, driving, walking, and cycling distance together so you can compare them quickly. Direct distance remains useful for proximity checks, school catchment areas, delivery zone radii, and flight estimation; the travel modes follow OpenStreetMap roads and paths. For turn-by-turn navigation, use a dedicated navigation app.What does "as the crow flies" mean?"As the crow flies" is an idiom for the shortest possible path between two points, ignoring roads, terrain, and obstacles: the path a bird would take flying in a straight line. Mathematically, it corresponds to the great-circle distance on the Earth's surface.Can I undo a point I placed by mistake?Yes. Click the Undo button in the toolbar, or press Backspace on your keyboard, to remove the last placed point. Click Clear all to reset the entire measurement.

# About Draw on a Map

A lightweight map annotation tool for people who need to explain a route, mark a meeting spot, or share a quick visual plan without creating an account.

![Image 2](https://drawonamap.com/pwa-screenshot-wide.png)
## Why this product exists

Most map products are built for navigation, account-based collaboration, or long-term storage. That works well for many cases, but it adds friction when the actual job is simple: draw something on a map and send it.

Draw on a Map was built to remove that friction. The goal is speed, clarity, and low ceremony. Open the map, mark what matters, and share the result.

## Who built it

Draw on a Map is built and maintained by Sergio Garcia and Emilia Hansson, two software engineers. The site is intentionally simple: a focused interface, fast loading, and minimal data collection.

### Sergio Garcia

Software engineer.

[github.com/singiamtel](link_5) · [LinkedIn](link_6)

### Emilia Hansson

Software engineer. Co-creator and maintainer of Draw on a Map.

[github.com/emiliaajax](link_7)

### Publisher details

**Product:** Draw on a Map

**Publisher:** Draw on a Map

**Maintainer:** Sunshine Projects

**Support:**[support@drawonamap.com](mailto:support@drawonamap.com)

## How the tool works

Share a link so others can open your drawing without signing in.

## Product principles

*   Fast enough to use in the moment, not after setup.
*   Simple enough to explain without a tutorial.
*   Private by default, with no account required.
*   Useful on both desktop and mobile.

## Where to start

If you are new to the product, the main app is the right entry point. If you want examples and tutorials, the blog covers practical use cases like route sketching, marking meeting spots, and measuring distances.

[Start drawing](https://drawonamap.com/)

## Draw Routes, Mark Spots, and Share: Instantly

Draw on a Map is a free online tool for annotating any location on Earth. Select a drawing tool, sketch directly on the map, and share the result with a single link. No account, no download, no setup required.

## What You Can Do

*   **Draw freehand routes**: trace hiking trails, cycling paths, or custom travel routes with the pen tool.
*   **Mark meeting spots**: drop a circle or marker on a location and share the link via WhatsApp, Telegram, or email.
*   **Plan travel itineraries**: use different colors to mark each stop and draw connecting routes for any destination worldwide.
*   **Draw radius circles**: visualize a delivery zone, search area, neighborhood boundary, or commute radius around any point.
*   **Embed maps on websites**: generate an iframe embed code to place your annotated map on any page or blog.
*   **Explain directions**: draw the route with arrows and share the link instead of writing text directions.

## How to Draw on a Map

1.   **Open drawonamap.com**: no signup or installation required, works instantly in any browser.
2.   **Search for a location**: type an address or place name in the search bar and press Enter to navigate there.
3.   **Select a drawing tool**: choose from pen (freehand), line, arrow, circle, or eraser in the toolbar.
4.   **Draw on the map**: click and drag to draw. Adjust color and line thickness before drawing.
5.   **Share your map**: click the Share button to copy a link. Anyone who opens it sees your exact drawing.

## Free Map Drawing Tools

*   [Interactive World Map](link_8): explore countries, zoom, draw routes, mark places, and share the map.
*   [Interactive US Map](link_9): explore the United States, mark locations, draw routes, and create radius areas.
*   [Distance Calculator](https://drawonamap.com/distance-between-two-addresses/): measure straight-line distance between any two addresses.
*   [Map Radius Tool](link_10): draw a radius circle around any point and visualize who falls inside it.
*   [Plot a Route](link_11): add stops, calculate drive/walk/bike distances, and share the route.
*   [Map Marker Tool](link_12): mark a meeting spot, address, venue, or landmark on a map.
*   [Mapping Tool](link_13): draw, mark, measure, and share custom maps online.
*   [Printable Custom Map](link_14): create a map, preview a print-ready PDF or PNG, and choose a watermarked or clean download.
*   [Route Planner](link_15): plan multi-stop routes and share them as a link.
*   [Draw Circle on Map](link_16): mark delivery zones, school catchment areas, or search areas.
*   [Service Area Widget](link_17): add a "Do you service my address?" checker to a business website.

## Draw Routes, Mark Spots, and Share: Instantly

Draw on a Map is a free online tool for annotating any location on Earth. Select a drawing tool, sketch directly on the map, and share the result with a single link. No account, no download, no setup required.

## What You Can Do

*   **Draw freehand routes**: trace hiking trails, cycling paths, or custom travel routes with the pen tool.
*   **Mark meeting spots**: drop a circle or marker on a location and share the link via WhatsApp, Telegram, or email.
*   **Plan travel itineraries**: use different colors to mark each stop and draw connecting routes for any destination worldwide.
*   **Draw radius circles**: visualize a delivery zone, search area, neighborhood boundary, or commute radius around any point.
*   **Embed maps on websites**: generate an iframe embed code to place your annotated map on any page or blog.
*   **Explain directions**: draw the route with arrows and share the link instead of writing text directions.

## How to Draw on a Map

1.   **Open drawonamap.com**: no signup or installation required, works instantly in any browser.
2.   **Search for a location**: type an address or place name in the search bar and press Enter to navigate there.
3.   **Select a drawing tool**: choose from pen (freehand), line, arrow, circle, or eraser in the toolbar.
4.   **Draw on the map**: click and drag to draw. Adjust color and line thickness before drawing.
5.   **Share your map**: click the Share button to copy a link. Anyone who opens it sees your exact drawing.

## Free Map Drawing Tools

*   [Interactive World Map](link_8): explore countries, zoom, draw routes, mark places, and share the map.
*   [Interactive US Map](link_9): explore the United States, mark locations, draw routes, and create radius areas.
*   [Distance Calculator](https://drawonamap.com/distance-between-two-addresses/): measure straight-line distance between any two addresses.
*   [Map Radius Tool](link_10): draw a radius circle around any point and visualize who falls inside it.
*   [Plot a Route](link_11): add stops, calculate drive/walk/bike distances, and share the route.
*   [Map Marker Tool](link_12): mark a meeting spot, address, venue, or landmark on a map.
*   [Mapping Tool](link_13): draw, mark, measure, and share custom maps online.
*   [Printable Custom Map](link_14): create a map, preview a print-ready PDF or PNG, and choose a watermarked or clean download.
*   [Route Planner](link_15): plan multi-stop routes and share them as a link.
*   [Draw Circle on Map](link_16): mark delivery zones, school catchment areas, or search areas.
*   [Service Area Widget](link_17): add a "Do you service my address?" checker to a business website.

Title: Draw a Circle on a Map: Freeform or Exact Radius

URL Source: https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/

Published Time: 2026-02-21

Markdown Content:
[Skip to content](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#main-content)

[![Image 1](https://drawonamap.com/favicon.webp)Draw on a Map](https://drawonamap.com/)[Service Area](https://drawonamap.com/service-area-widget/)[Embed a map](https://drawonamap.com/embed-map/)[Datasets](https://drawonamap.com/datasets/)[Guides](https://drawonamap.com/blog/)[Pro](https://drawonamap.com/pro/?feature=generic_pro&source=public_navigation)[Start drawing](https://drawonamap.com/)

# Draw a circle around the place you choose

Mark a search area or set an exact radius in kilometers or miles. Use Draw on a Map to create the circle and share a free map link.

[Draw your circle ↗](https://drawonamap.com/draw-circle-on-map/)[Read the guide ↓](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#guide-details)

Free drawing and standard share links. No account needed to start.

![Image 2: A purple circle marks an approximate area around Annecy and the north end of the lake.](https://drawonamap.com/_astro/circle-map-preview.CE_3G5Hv_1gkwrM.webp)

A purple circle marks an approximate area around Annecy and the north end of the lake.

[Make your map](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#make-your-map)[Read the guide](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#guide-details)[Draw your circle ↗](https://drawonamap.com/draw-circle-on-map/)
## Make the map you need.

01
### Find your location

Search for the town or place you want to mark. Move the map until the area is in view.

02
### Choose the circle size

Draw a freeform circle for an approximate area. Use Exact radius when you need a set distance from a center point.

03
### Send the map link

Copy a standard share link and send it with your instructions. Drawing and standard link sharing are free.

## On this page

*   [Draw your search area](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#draw-your-search-area)
*   [Need exactly 1 km from a place?](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#need-exactly-1-km-from-a-place)
*   [Share the finished map](https://drawonamap.com/blog/how-to-draw-a-circle-on-a-map/#share-the-finished-map)

Use a circle to show where to search for accommodation, meet a group, or check places near an address. This example marks an accommodation search area in Annecy. Follow the same steps for your own location.

![Image 3: A purple circle around Annecy and the north end of Lake Annecy](https://drawonamap.com/_astro/circle-map-preview.CE_3G5Hv_bTu1n.webp)

_This circle marks an approximate search area. It does not show a measured radius or a walking distance._

## Draw your search area

Open the [circle drawing tool](https://drawonamap.com/draw-circle-on-map/), then follow these steps:

1.   Search for **Annecy**, or choose your own location.
2.   With **Circle** selected, choose **Freeform**.
3.   Choose a color that stands out against the map.
4.   Drag from one edge of your intended circle to the opposite edge.
5.   Release to finish the circle.

![Image 4: Circle tool panel with Freeform selected, color choices, stroke width, and opacity](https://drawonamap.com/_astro/circle-tool-options.BPOni22R_Z8yX36.webp)

The drag sets the diameter, across the full circle. Start at the edge, not the center. If the circle covers the wrong area, select **Undo** and draw it again.

In the Annecy example, part of the circle falls on water. Check the area before you share it. A circle does not follow streets or the shoreline.

## Need exactly 1 km from a place?

Use **Exact radius** when the distance matters. A radius runs from the center to the edge of the circle.

1.   In the **Circle** panel, select **Exact radius**.
2.   Enter **1** and select **km**. For miles, select **mi**.
3.   Select **Apply**.
4.   Click the map at the place you want to use as the center.

![Image 5: Exact radius dialog with a radius of 1 kilometer](https://drawonamap.com/_astro/circle-exact-radius.BkkNpCQ-_ZU45Iv.webp)

This gives you a 1 km straight-line radius. A route along roads or around the lake can be longer. Use the [route planner](https://drawonamap.com/route-planner/) when you need a route distance.

## Share the finished map

Select **Share** and send the copied link to your friend. Keep a copy of the link so you can reopen the drawing. Core drawing and standard link sharing are free and require no account.

For the accommodation example, include a short message such as: “Look for places inside this circle. Check the walking route before you book.”

## FAQ

### Is this route planner free?

Yes. Multi-stop routing, driving distances, walking and cycling directions, travel time estimates, and shareable links are all completely free. No account or payment is required.

### How many stops can I add?

There is no hard limit. Add as many waypoints as your route requires. Each leg's distance and duration is listed individually, and the panel shows the running total.

### Does it give turn-by-turn directions?

Yes. Step-by-step directions for each leg appear in the sidebar when you are in Drive, Walk, or Bike mode. The directions are powered by OpenStreetMap's routing engine.

### How do I share my route?

Select Share route to copy a link to your route. The recipient can open it without an account.

## Plot a Route Online

Use this free route planner to plot a route on an interactive map. Add a starting point, destination, and optional stops, then choose Drive, Walk, or Bike mode to calculate road-following distances and estimated travel times.

## How to Plot a Route on a Map

1.   **Enter your starting point**: search for an address, city, or landmark.
2.   **Add your destination**: select the endpoint from the search results.
3.   **Add stops**: insert as many waypoints as you need for a multi-stop route.
4.   **Choose a mode**: switch between driving, walking, and cycling.
5.   **Share your route**: copy a link that opens the same plotted route.

## Route Plotting Uses

*   **Road trips**: plan stops and compare total distance before leaving.
*   **Walking directions**: plot custom pedestrian routes and share them.
*   **Delivery routes**: add multiple stops and share the route with a driver.

## Draw a five-mile radius around an address

A radius is the distance from the center of a circle to its edge. Enter **5 miles** to show all points within that direct distance of your chosen center. Exact radius circles and link sharing are free and require no account.

1.   Search for the address. For an example, use **10 Downing Street, London**.
2.   Choose **Enter exact radius** in the circle controls.
3.   Enter **5**, select **mi**, and apply the value.
4.   Click the address location on the map to place the center.
5.   Select **Share** and open the copied link to check the result.

The circle has a radius of 5 miles and a diameter of 10 miles. The distance runs directly from the center to the edge. It does not follow roads.

## Radius distance and travel distance

| Your question | Tool to use |
| --- | --- |
| What is within five miles in any direction? | Exact radius circle |
| How far is the drive to a specific address? | Route planner in Drive mode |
| How far is the walk to a specific place? | Route planner in Walk mode |
| Is this address inside my business boundary? | Service Area Widget with your approved boundary |

A point inside the circle can require more than five miles of travel. Rivers, road layouts, and access restrictions can change the route. A circle does not show a drive-time area or an official school boundary.

## Compare two distances

Place a **1 km** circle at your chosen center. Then place a **3 km** circle at the same center in another color. The smaller circle shows the nearer area; the larger circle shows the wider search area. Use **Share** to send both circles in one map.

Select an existing circle and use **Enter exact radius** to change its radius. Check the center and units before sharing.

## Draw an approximate circle

Choose **Draw a circle by eye** and drag from one edge to the opposite edge. This sets the diameter. Use an exact radius when a measured distance matters.

## Free Map Markers Tool

Use this map markers tool when you need to point someone to an exact place. The **Marker tool is already selected**: search for an address or location, then click the map once to drop each pin. Share a link that opens the same marked map.

## How to Mark a Location on a Map

1.   **Search for the place**: type an address, city, venue, or landmark in the search bar.
2.   **Zoom to the exact spot**: adjust the map until the location is clear.
3.   **Add a marker**: click the map once to drop a pin. Keep clicking to mark more places, or switch tools to add a label, circle, or arrow.
4.   **Share the map**: click Share to copy a link with the same marker and map view.

## Common Map Marker Uses

*   **Meeting spots**: mark where people should gather.
*   **Event venues**: highlight entrances, parking, stages, exits, and pickup points.
*   **Travel stops**: mark hotels, restaurants, scenic stops, and places to visit.
*   **Property notes**: mark lots, access roads, boundaries, and nearby amenities.

*   [Draw on a Map](https://drawonamap.com/): draw routes, arrows, circles, and annotations on any map.
*   [Mapping Tool](https://drawonamap.com/mapping-tool/): combine markers with routes, measurements, circles, and other map annotations.
*   [World Map](https://drawonamap.com/world-map/): mark places on an interactive world map.
*   [US Map](https://drawonamap.com/us-map/): mark places on a United States map.

This demo uses a sample area. Your widget uses your own boundary, messages, and brand.

## From your service area to your website

Build the checker before you commit. Test real addresses and check the result your customers will see.

### 1. Set your service area

Find your business. Start with a radius or draw a custom boundary, then adjust the edge to match where you work.

### 2. Make it yours

Add your business name and color. Write the inside and outside messages, and add a link to call or request a quote.

### 3. Test, then publish

Check addresses on both sides of your boundary. When you are ready, start your trial and copy the embed code.

## Add it to the website you already have

Install it yourself with the instructions below, or [ask us to help install it](https://drawonamap.com/contact/). Your website must allow iframe embeds.

WordPress
1.   Add a Custom HTML block to your page.
2.   Paste your widget embed code.
3.   Preview the page, then publish it.

Your account must have permission to embed iframes. WordPress.com plan restrictions can apply.

[WordPress instructions](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/custom-html/)

Wix
1.   In the editor, add an Embed HTML element.
2.   Paste your widget code into its code settings.
3.   Set the element height, check the mobile view, and publish.

[Wix instructions](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-embedding-a-site-or-a-widget)

Squarespace
1.   Add a Code block to your page.
2.   Paste the widget embed code as HTML.
3.   Save and check the published page.

Iframe code requires a plan that supports this premium feature.

[Squarespace instructions](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206543167-Code-blocks)

Custom HTML
1.   Copy the embed code after you publish your widget.
2.   Paste it where the checker should appear on your page.
3.   Check the page on desktop and mobile.

If someone manages your site, send them the embed code.

## Publish with a 30-day trial.

Draw your boundary and check real addresses at no cost. Start your trial when the checker is ready for your website.

Build and test it free. Publish with a 30-day trial, then pay $19/month. Cancel any time.

### We can help install it on your website

Send us your website link and the platform you use. We will help you add the checker to your site and test it with you. You can ask for help before you start a trial.

[Get installation help](https://drawonamap.com/contact/) · [About the product](https://drawonamap.com/about/)

### Service Area Widget

$19 USD / month after the trial

30 days to try it on your website.

*   Your service boundary and customer address checker
*   Your business name, color, and result messages
*   A customer action, such as calling or requesting a quote
*   A hosted widget and website embed code

[Build my address checker](https://drawonamap.com/service-area-widget/create/?source=landing)
A payment method is required to publish. Your first charge is after the 30-day trial. Your service area is saved so you can edit it later. [Terms](https://drawonamap.com/terms/) · [Privacy](https://drawonamap.com/privacy/)

## Before you start

Do I need an account to try it?
No. Build your area and test addresses without an account or payment card. You create your account when you publish.

What happens if I cancel?
Cancel through the billing portal in your account. Once subscription access ends, you cannot publish a new checker or save changes to a service area. Canceling does not delete an existing public map or remove its embed. Delete the map if you want to remove it.

Can I change the boundary and messages?
Yes. You can adjust the boundary and set different messages for customers inside and outside your area. Test both results before you publish.

Is this a driving-distance check?
No. The checker tests whether an address is inside your boundary. A radius measures straight-line distance. It does not calculate driving time or confirm that a road reaches an address.

Can I use it on any website?
Your website must support iframe embeds. Some website plans and editor permissions restrict custom code. Check the platform instructions above or [contact us](https://drawonamap.com/contact/) before publishing.

What if I only need to display a map?
You can [embed a custom map](https://drawonamap.com/embed-map/) without an address checker. You can also [draw a coverage circle](https://drawonamap.com/draw-circle-on-map/).

CLEVELAND, Ohio - In light of the shutdown order restricting dine-in service at eateries, we are updating our list of restaurants that offer takeout and delivery on a daily basis.

If you are a restaurant owner with news about delivery, takeout and carry-out options as we all deal with coronavirus concerns, email restaurants@cleveland.com. Include the name of your restaurant, address, brief details of what you are offering (full or limited menu, delivery services, hours). Include all details in the body text of the email please.

**NORTHEAST OHIO TAKEOUT AND DELIVERY OPTIONS**

*   3 Aprons offers carryout and curbside pickup for limited menu of Detroit-style pizza, quiches and pastries 5-8 p.m. Thursdays-Sundays. Orders need to be placed two to three hours in advance due to lack of ingredients available. (12204 Larchmere Blvd., Cleveland, 216-810-6111)

*   83 & Chestnut Pub and Eatery [offers pickup orders only](link_8), with 12-packs and cases of beer also available. Normal menu will be available; no weekly specials. Call 440-219-4955 for more information. (9001 Avon Belden Rd., North Ridgeville)

# Marc Bona, cleveland.com

As a features writer on cleveland.com's life and culture team, I primarily cover food, restaurants, beer, wine, sports entertainment and sports history. I have written four books, all on sports including "Not Your Average Joe," a bio on Browns great Joe Thomas that I co-authored with Dan Murphy (Gray and Company, 2023). I live in Akron, have won several Cleveland Press Club awards and have a rescue dog named after Cleveland pitching great Addie Joss. Proud grad of THE U of Iowa - aka Caitlin Clark University. Email: mbona@cleveland.com for story tips or speak-and-sign events.

13h ago[Marc Bona](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/posts.html)   ![Image 3: On a recent tour of Progressive Field, architects detail the multi-year project that upgraded clubhouses, added Terrace Hall and North Coast Social Club, and created what Athletic Business calls the best clubhouse in the Majors.](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/YDT3WVWODZFQNLZ3Z44FSC4OYI.jpg?auth=3ac28cd13fa7a925e9a9a6bdd222c7db8dadafb9f5b5fa91feab1e1da70d601a&smart=true&quality=90&width=500&height=342)

5 days ago[Marc Bona](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/posts.html)   ![Image 5: Jake Turner, who previously brewed at Maize Valley Winery & Brewery, is the brewer at Unfused Brew Hall, which is in the heart of downtown Canton. Unfused will feature an array of beers, full bar and German-themed food.](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/FEWTOIN5KJA63FBCCXCLOVJT5E.jpg?auth=94d335898151b9a06dde0edbb2dcc62a83da0695e3fa08725f406a5efcd35f76&smart=true&quality=90&width=500&height=375)

Peg’s Foundation is a transformational art gallery that provides support for families dealing with mental illness. It recently procured a 1917 Tiffany stained-glass window salvaged from a fire.

6 days ago[Marc Bona](https://www.cleveland.com/staff/mbona/posts.html)   ![Image 6: Peg’s Foundation is a transformational art gallery that provides support for families dealing with mental illness. It recently procured a 1917 Tiffany stained-glass window salvaged from a fire.](https://www.cleveland.com/resizer/v2/IOMRAE3BDRB4NDFHD6VZQXMYHE.jpg?auth=cebf3de6e381797399b5cf8ed1f8c116e7f8e5864ca975d46472ac9ecbc94c0b&smart=true&quality=90&width=500&height=375)

DiMaggio was playing first base for the first time in his career. # Joey Morona, cleveland.com

Joey Morona walked into the offices of the OG cleveland.com in the fall of 1998 with a rudimentary knowledge of HTML and a dream. In the time since, he has interviewed the likes of Alicia Keys, James Gunn, William Shatner, Joe & Anthony Russo, General Hospital’s Carly and both Property Brothers. Joey, a Cleveland native, first-gen Filipino-American, and UCF graduate, primarily covers film, theater, and TV, occasionally writing reviews as a Tomatometer-approved critic and member of the Critics Choice Association. (That nitpicky review of “Project Hail Mary”? That was him). In previous roles at cleveland.com, he was in the room when: LeBron James was drafted in New York City, Tim Couch cried at his locker, Dick Cheney met John Edwards for the first time (allegedly), and Dua Lipa slayed backstage at the 2024 Rock Hall inductions. Joey's journalism career originally began at a local TV station, where he claims to have come up with the phrase: “The news starts now!” Ask him about his interests in Disney parks and women’s basketball, or his beagle Marley, or his spinoff idea for "The Pitt," or his committment to the Oxford comma. Not to be confused with his twin brother, you can reach Joey at jmorona@cleveland.com.

# Marc Bona, cleveland.com

As a features writer on cleveland.com's life and culture team, I primarily cover food, restaurants, beer, wine, sports entertainment and sports history. I have written four books, all on sports including "Not Your Average Joe," a bio on Browns great Joe Thomas that I co-authored with Dan Murphy (Gray and Company, 2023). I live in Akron, have won several Cleveland Press Club awards and have a rescue dog named after Cleveland pitching great Addie Joss. Proud grad of THE U of Iowa - aka Caitlin Clark University. # Joey Morona, cleveland.com

Joey Morona walked into the offices of the OG cleveland.com in the fall of 1998 with a rudimentary knowledge of HTML and a dream. In the time since, he has interviewed the likes of Alicia Keys, James Gunn, William Shatner, Joe & Anthony Russo, General Hospital’s Carly and both Property Brothers. Joey, a Cleveland native, first-gen Filipino-American, and UCF graduate, primarily covers film, theater, and TV, occasionally writing reviews as a Tomatometer-approved critic and member of the Critics Choice Association. (That nitpicky review of “Project Hail Mary”? That was him). In previous roles at cleveland.com, he was in the room when: LeBron James was drafted in New York City, Tim Couch cried at his locker, Dick Cheney met John Edwards for the first time (allegedly), and Dua Lipa slayed backstage at the 2024 Rock Hall inductions. Joey's journalism career originally began at a local TV station, where he claims to have come up with the phrase: “The news starts now!” Ask him about his interests in Disney parks and women’s basketball, or his beagle Marley, or his spinoff idea for "The Pitt," or his committment to the Oxford comma. Not to be confused with his twin brother, you can reach Joey at jmorona@cleveland.com.

# 10 romantic spots to celebrate Valentine's Day in Cleveland

![Image 8](https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/valentines-day-in-cleveland-10-romantic-spots)

 Prev Next 

undefined

undefined

By: News 5 Staff 

Posted 10:17 PM, Feb 07, 2017

and last updated 10:29 PM, Feb 07, 2017

Valentine's Day is just around the corner and reservations to the city's most romantic spots are filling up.

With the plethora of restaurants and bars saturating the city, choosing a romantic spot to enjoy an evening of good food and drinks may be tricky, but with this list of ten spots that show the diversity of cuisine around Cleveland, finding the perfect spot to celebrate the day with a loved one just got easier.

1. **Le Petit Triangle**: If you can't go to Paris, but want to have a vibe of a Parisian cafe and the taste of French cuisine, look no further than this cafe located in the heart of Ohio City. Owners Tom and Joy Harold share their passion for fine dining and French flare. Let the crepes and the Boeuf Bourguignon take you from Cleveland to Paris.

![Image 10](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/PETIT_1486501597073_54728264_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: Phone: 216-281-18881

1881 Fulton Avenue Cleveland, Ohio 44113

2. **Dante:** In the historic neighborhood of Tremont, Michelin Star Chef and Parma native, Dante Boccuzzi,transformed an old bank and vault building into a food destination where customers can have an Italian and American cuisine in a cozy, trendy atmosphere.

![Image 11](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/Dante_1486502346455_54728270_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: 216-274-1200

2247 Professor Avenue Cleveland, Ohio 44113

3**. Alley Cat:**Looking to have some of the city's best seafood while overlooking the Cuyahoga River? Located on the East Bank Waterfront in the Flats, Alley Cat serves up traditional waterfront cuisine with a flare. This two-story restaurant has private rooms and an extensive wine list.

![Image 12](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/alley_1486502664706_54726339_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: 216-574-9999

1056 Old River Road Cleveland, Ohio 44113

# 10 romantic spots to celebrate Valentine's Day in Cleveland

![Image 8](https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/valentines-day-in-cleveland-10-romantic-spots)

 Prev Next 

undefined

undefined

By: News 5 Staff 

Posted 10:17 PM, Feb 07, 2017

and last updated 10:29 PM, Feb 07, 2017

Valentine's Day is just around the corner and reservations to the city's most romantic spots are filling up.

With the plethora of restaurants and bars saturating the city, choosing a romantic spot to enjoy an evening of good food and drinks may be tricky, but with this list of ten spots that show the diversity of cuisine around Cleveland, finding the perfect spot to celebrate the day with a loved one just got easier.

1. **Le Petit Triangle**: If you can't go to Paris, but want to have a vibe of a Parisian cafe and the taste of French cuisine, look no further than this cafe located in the heart of Ohio City. Owners Tom and Joy Harold share their passion for fine dining and French flare. Let the crepes and the Boeuf Bourguignon take you from Cleveland to Paris.

![Image 10](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/PETIT_1486501597073_54728264_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: Phone: 216-281-18881

1881 Fulton Avenue Cleveland, Ohio 44113

2. **Dante:** In the historic neighborhood of Tremont, Michelin Star Chef and Parma native, Dante Boccuzzi,transformed an old bank and vault building into a food destination where customers can have an Italian and American cuisine in a cozy, trendy atmosphere.

![Image 11](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/Dante_1486502346455_54728270_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: 216-274-1200

2247 Professor Avenue Cleveland, Ohio 44113

3**. Alley Cat:**Looking to have some of the city's best seafood while overlooking the Cuyahoga River? Located on the East Bank Waterfront in the Flats, Alley Cat serves up traditional waterfront cuisine with a flare. This two-story restaurant has private rooms and an extensive wine list.

![Image 12](http://media2.newsnet5.com/photo/2017/02/07/alley_1486502664706_54726339_ver1.0_640_480.jpg)

For reservations: 216-574-9999

1056 Old River Road Cleveland, Ohio 44113

# 'What Happened Now?' Newsletter

**By JOE DONATELLI**

You want to stay informed about what's happening in Northeast Ohio, but life happens, and it's hard to stay on top of it all. Or maybe you've just grown bored with the same-old same-old. Does that sound like you?

"What Happened Now?" is a newsletter written by someone who shares local news like one friend talking to another. It's not just headlines — it's humor, mixed with empathy, mixed with disbelief that our leaders still don't get it, mixed with admiration for anyone making Northeast Ohio into A Better Land. The stories are from News 5, plus our media partners and other local publications, and they range from the big story of the day, to the ridiculous, to the tales of heartache and triumph that bring us together as a community.

Real feedback from actual readers:

*   **"I can't tell you how much I love the newsletter (or apparently I can, because I just did). It's often the best thing I read on any given day. Really appreciate the time and effort you put into it."**
*   **"With the newsletter being sent daily, I thought it might start to get lost in the usual barrage of spam emails and such, but I really look forward to it and enjoy reading it."**
*   **"This is a fantastic service you're providing. Interesting, timely and mostly local."**
*   **"Thanks for this newsletter. It makes me smile!"**
*   **"Read you all the time. With a million things competing for my eyeballs, you are a can't-miss. Great stuff!"**
*   **"It’s such a unique and genuine/personalized way to deliver updates in a world that often feels oversaturated with bad news these days. Nice work!"**

You can subscribe here: [**https://www.news5cleveland.com/account/manage-email-preferences**](link_1)

Add your email at the top of the page and select the newsletter "What Happened Now?" down at the bottom of the page. Then hit SUBMIT.

Thanks,

Joe Donatelli

Digital Director

News 5 Cleveland

# The 50 best Cleveland patios for enjoying a meal and an adult beverage (or two)

Posted 10:00 AM, Aug 13, 2021

and last updated 1:58 PM, Sep 03, 2021

[![Image 9](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8bd8811/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1200x1200+398+0/resize/300x300!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F72%2F6f%2F754a95dd4dda9ffa3b9818be1a01%2Fdrew-scofield.jpg)](https://www.news5cleveland.com/drew-scofield [link_118])

By:[Drew Scofield](link_118), Joe Donatelli 

![Image 10: Thumbnail](https://cf.cdn.uplynk.com/ausw/slices/551/b2c1c5c2af374f52af57ddcae54c6663/55103663a1974c4ca20199233c23fbef/poster_d1ae3dc11fa04bb38822cd4e54e063bc.jpg)![Image 11](blob:http://localhost/526678ffaf9724e36d431c3ad606e6be [link_119])

 Prev Next 

Bar 32 at the Hilton Hotel in Downtown Cleveland provides million dollar views of Cleveland.

![Image 12: Bar 32 at the Hilton makes Best Patio in Cleveland list](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/bce1744/2147483647/strip/false/crop/1280x714+0+3/resize/95x53!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcf.cdn.uplynk.com%2Fausw%2Fslices%2F551%2Fb2c1c5c2af374f52af57ddcae54c6663%2F55103663a1974c4ca20199233c23fbef%2Fposter_d1ae3dc11fa04bb38822cd4e54e063bc.jpg)

![Image 13: Best Patios Work In Progress 2.png](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/caf748e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F3e%2Fab%2Fea899c294abe9477d6b6bba739e8%2Fbest-patios-work-in-progress-2.png)

CLEVELAND — Cleveland patios -- everyone has a favorite. From rooftop access and panoramic views, to cityscapes, lake and river views, plus great food and drink, the best Cleveland-area patios all have something special to offer.

In no particular order, yet numbered anyway because the Internet demands it...

**1. Felice Urban Cafe**  
12502 Larchmere Blvd., Cleveland  
There's a bocce court, a pizza oven and the cutest shed-turned-backyard-bar behind this converted home, now a restaurant.

# The 50 best Cleveland patios for enjoying a meal and an adult beverage (or two)

Posted 10:00 AM, Aug 13, 2021

and last updated 1:58 PM, Sep 03, 2021

[![Image 9](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8bd8811/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1200x1200+398+0/resize/300x300!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F72%2F6f%2F754a95dd4dda9ffa3b9818be1a01%2Fdrew-scofield.jpg)](https://www.news5cleveland.com/drew-scofield [link_118])

By:[Drew Scofield](link_118), Joe Donatelli 

![Image 10: Thumbnail](https://cf.cdn.uplynk.com/ausw/slices/551/b2c1c5c2af374f52af57ddcae54c6663/55103663a1974c4ca20199233c23fbef/poster_d1ae3dc11fa04bb38822cd4e54e063bc.jpg)![Image 11](blob:http://localhost/526678ffaf9724e36d431c3ad606e6be [link_119])

 Prev Next 

Bar 32 at the Hilton Hotel in Downtown Cleveland provides million dollar views of Cleveland.

![Image 12: Bar 32 at the Hilton makes Best Patio in Cleveland list](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/bce1744/2147483647/strip/false/crop/1280x714+0+3/resize/95x53!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcf.cdn.uplynk.com%2Fausw%2Fslices%2F551%2Fb2c1c5c2af374f52af57ddcae54c6663%2F55103663a1974c4ca20199233c23fbef%2Fposter_d1ae3dc11fa04bb38822cd4e54e063bc.jpg)

![Image 13: Best Patios Work In Progress 2.png](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/caf748e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F3e%2Fab%2Fea899c294abe9477d6b6bba739e8%2Fbest-patios-work-in-progress-2.png)

CLEVELAND — Cleveland patios -- everyone has a favorite. From rooftop access and panoramic views, to cityscapes, lake and river views, plus great food and drink, the best Cleveland-area patios all have something special to offer.

In no particular order, yet numbered anyway because the Internet demands it...

**1. Felice Urban Cafe**  
12502 Larchmere Blvd., Cleveland  
There's a bocce court, a pizza oven and the cutest shed-turned-backyard-bar behind this converted home, now a restaurant.
